# Forge documentation

Forge is a fast, memory-safe IDE in the spirit of PHPStorm for Windows, Linux and macOS, built
with Rust + Tauri 2 and a SolidJS UI. Layout, wording and the default keymap follow PHPStorm 1:1;
the look is Forge's own ("Ember" dark, "Anvil" light).

![Forge workbench](docs/screenshots/workbench-dark.png)

Languages and large feature sets ship as **packs**:

| Pack | Focus |
| --- | --- |
| **PHPForge** | PHP, Composer, PHPUnit, Xdebug, Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine (DQL) |
| **WebForge** | HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, React, Vue, Angular |
| **LuaForge** | Lua 5.1–5.4, LuaJIT, LÖVE, Neovim |

The core adds Git and code review (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea), Run/Debug configurations, a
terminal, database tools, Scratches with an HTTP client, Docker/Compose/Kubernetes, remote
development over SSH, language servers for about 30 more languages, AI (your own providers,
Claude Code and Gemini CLI as a native chat) and a browser companion.

## Where to start

## Recently added

- **Splash screen and updates**: the wordmark fills with molten metal while Forge loads, the
  last project reopens, and signed updates are offered on startup or with Help | Check for
  Updates… ([First start](docs/guide/getting-started/first-start.md#the-splash-screen)).
- **Main menu**: PHPStorm's menus behind ☰, merged into the toolbar or as a menu bar
  ([Workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu)).
- **Find in Files** (`Ctrl+Shift+F`) and the **Choose Declaration** popup
  ([Search Everywhere](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files), [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)).
- **One-click language server installs**, including Intelephense with its own Node.js
  ([Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md#installing-a-server)).
- **HTTP client**: environment picker, response handlers, body files, dynamic variables
  ([Scratches and HTTP client](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md#http-client-http-files)).
- **Services**: Kubernetes port forwarding, container picker, deployment logs, Docker over SSH
  and Docker contexts ([Services](docs/guide/user/services.md)).
- **Remote parity**: frameworks, language servers, databases, Xdebug and AI agents in remote
  projects, `ProxyJump`/`ProxyCommand` ([Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md)).
- **Dialog windows and OS-styled window controls**
  ([Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#window-controls)).

## Not available yet

Refactorings (Rename, Extract, Move), Find Usages, Replace in Files, quick-fixes (`Alt+Enter`),
bookmarks, TODO, Local History, split editors, Get from VCS, stash, multiple project windows, a
plugin Marketplace and automatic updates. The pages mark smaller gaps with notes.

## About this guide

The guide is plain Markdown with a small frontmatter contract so any documentation generator can
render it; see [About this guide](docs/guide/README.md). Every user-visible change to Forge updates the
matching page.

# Getting started

Forge is a PHPStorm-style IDE for Windows, Linux and macOS, built with Rust and Tauri 2. If you
have used PHPStorm, most of what you know carries over: the same layout, the same action names
and the same default keymap. This section takes you from download to a working project.

| Page | What you learn |
| --- | --- |
| [Installation](docs/guide/getting-started/installation.md) | Install the AppImage, deb/rpm, Windows or macOS bundle, and what the system needs |
| [First start and the Welcome screen](docs/guide/getting-started/first-start.md) | What you see on the first launch, the Welcome screen, recent projects |
| [Opening and creating projects](docs/guide/getting-started/projects.md) | Open a folder, the New Project wizard and its generators, the default project directory |
| [Project type detection](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md) | How Forge recognizes Laravel, Symfony, React, LÖVE & co. and which plugins it activates |
| [Coming from PHPStorm](docs/guide/getting-started/from-phpstorm.md) | What is the same, what is different, and what is not there yet |

After that, the [user guide](docs/guide/user/index.md) has one page per feature, and the
[keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) lists every shortcut.

# Installation

Forge is a single native application (the binary is called `forge`). It is distributed as the
bundles Tauri produces for each operating system:

| System | Bundle | File name (version 0.1.0) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any x86_64 Linux | AppImage | `Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage` |
| Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS | deb | `Forge_0.1.0_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL | rpm | `Forge-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Windows 10/11 | MSI or NSIS installer | `Forge_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi`, `Forge_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe` |
| macOS 11+ | disk image | `Forge_0.1.0_aarch64.dmg` (Apple silicon) or `_x64.dmg` (Intel) |

> **Note:** Forge is at version 0.1.0 and the project does not publish signed downloads yet.
> If there is no ready-made bundle for your system, build one yourself with
> [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md) (about six minutes on a recent machine).
> Cross-compiling is not supported: build Windows bundles on Windows and macOS bundles on a Mac.

## Linux

Forge uses the system WebView (WebKitGTK 4.1), so that library must be installed on every
Linux system, whatever the bundle type.

### AppImage on Arch Linux and EndeavourOS

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed webkit2gtk-4.1 fuse2
chmod +x Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
```

`fuse2` lets the AppImage mount itself. If you would rather not install FUSE, run it with
`APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1` (see below).

To start Forge from your application launcher, move the AppImage to a stable place such as
`~/Applications/` and create a desktop entry, or use a helper like AppImageLauncher or Gear Lever.

### AppImage on Ubuntu and Debian

```sh
# Ubuntu 24.04 and newer
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libfuse2t64
# Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libfuse2

chmod +x Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
```

### Running the AppImage without FUSE

An AppImage normally mounts itself with FUSE. In containers, on systems without `fuse2`, or
when you see `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`, let it extract itself to a temporary
folder instead:

```sh
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
```

The start takes a little longer because the image is unpacked on every launch. You can also
unpack it once with `./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract` and run
`squashfs-root/AppRun`.

### deb package

```sh
sudo apt install ./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.deb
```

`apt` pulls in WebKitGTK automatically. The package installs the `forge` command, so you can
start it from a terminal (see [command-line arguments](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md)).

### rpm package

```sh
sudo dnf install ./Forge-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm      # Fedora, RHEL
sudo zypper install ./Forge-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm   # openSUSE
```

### What else Forge uses on Linux

Forge works without any of these, but features light up when they are installed:

| Tool | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `git` | Git integration (commit, diff, blame, branches, log) |
| `php` | running PHP scripts, PHPUnit, artisan, the Symfony console, PHP scratches |
| `composer` | Composer scripts, new Laravel/Symfony projects |
| Node.js + `npm` | npm scripts and new web projects (language servers do not need it: Forge downloads Node.js itself when missing) |
| language servers | completion, hover and diagnostics, see [Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) |
| `docker`, `kubectl` | the Services tool window |
| a Secret Service keyring (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) | storing API keys, tokens and passwords, see [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#keychain-on-linux) |

## Windows

Run the `.msi` or the `-setup.exe` installer and start Forge from the Start menu. Forge uses
Microsoft Edge WebView2, which is part of Windows 10 (April 2018 and later) and Windows 11; the
installer adds it on older systems.

The terminal starts PowerShell 7 (`pwsh.exe`) when it is installed, else Windows PowerShell,
else the shell named by `%ComSpec%`, unless you choose another one in Settings | Tools |
Terminal.

## macOS

Open the `.dmg` and drag Forge to Applications. Because the app is not signed and notarized
yet, Gatekeeper refuses the first start. Either right-click Forge in Finder and choose
**Open**, or remove the quarantine flag:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Forge.app
```

On macOS the default keymap is PHPStorm's macOS keymap (`Cmd` instead of `Ctrl`), and Settings
opens with `Cmd+,`.

## Updating and uninstalling

There is no built-in updater yet. Replace the AppImage or install the newer package over the
old one. Uninstalling the app leaves your settings and caches in place; see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md) for what to delete for a clean slate.

## Next step

[First start and the Welcome screen](docs/guide/getting-started/first-start.md)

description: What Forge shows on its first launch, the Welcome screen and its recent projects list.

# First start and the Welcome screen

## Starting Forge

Start Forge from your application menu, or from a terminal:

```sh
forge                       # Welcome screen
forge ~/Projects/shop       # open a folder as the project
forge src/App.tsx:12        # open a file at line 12 (in the project it belongs to)
```

All launcher forms are listed in [CLI arguments and forge:// links](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md).
If Forge is already running, a second `forge …` call is handed to the running window instead
of starting another instance.

Without a project argument Forge reopens the last local project you worked on, if it still
exists ("Reopen projects on startup", `system.reopenLastProject` under Settings | Appearance &
Behavior | System Settings). With that setting off, or when there is no recent project, it shows
the **Welcome screen**. Remote projects are not reopened automatically.

## The splash screen

![Splash screen while Forge loads](docs/screenshots/splash-progress.png)

While Forge starts, a small window shows the Forge wordmark. Its letters fill with molten
metal as the loading steps finish, so the fill is the real progress. The line at the bottom
names the current step:

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Loading the core | settings and the keymap |
| Loading plugins | the built-in plugins' settings and servers (Browser Companion) |
| Opening project | the project from the command line, a `forge://` link or the last session, and its framework detection |
| Starting background services | language server registration, file watcher, data sources, Docker / Kubernetes |
| Checking for updates | at most once a day, see [Updates](#updates) |
| Opening workbench | the main window loads; the splash closes when it is shown |

Turn the splash off with "Show splash screen on startup" (`appearance.showSplash`) under
Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance. Forge then starts without it and shows the
main window when loading is done.

## Updates

![Update offer on the splash screen](docs/screenshots/splash-update.png)

Release builds check for a new version on the last splash step, at most once a day. When one
exists, the splash shows **Update available** with the download size and three buttons:

| Button | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Download and restart** | downloads the update, checks its signature against Forge's signing key, installs it and restarts Forge |
| **Later** | opens the workbench; Forge asks again the next day |
| **Skip this version** | this version is never offered automatically again |

![Downloading an update](docs/screenshots/splash-downloading.png)

While downloading, the panel shows the megabytes, the speed and "Signature: verifying… →
valid". An update whose signature does not match is not installed. When the download fails
(offline, bad signature) the splash says so and opens the workbench after a moment.

**Help | Check for Updates…** checks at any time, also for skipped versions. The settings are
under Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings | Updates:

![Updates settings](docs/screenshots/settings-updates.png)

- "Check for updates on startup" (`updates.checkOnStartup`)
- "Update channel" (`updates.channel`): stable releases, or beta releases as well
- "Update feed URL" (`updates.endpoint`): another `latest.json`, e.g. a company mirror
- a skipped version can be offered again with **Offer Again**

> **Note:** builds made without the updater key (for example your own builds) never check for
> updates; the settings page says "Updates are not configured in this build". Development
> builds never check either.

## The Welcome screen

![Welcome screen with recent projects](docs/screenshots/welcome.png)

The left side has four entries, as in PHPStorm:

| Entry | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Projects** | Recent projects, with a search field and the buttons **New Project**, **Open** and **Get from VCS** |
| **Remote Development** | SSH connections and remote projects, see [Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) |
| **Customize** | opens the Settings dialog |
| **Plugins** | opens the Settings dialog (Settings | Plugins) |

The gear icon at the bottom opens Settings as well.

### Recent projects

Every project you open is added to the list. Each row shows a colored badge with the project's
initials, the name, the path and, on the right, the detected project type ("Laravel 12",
"Symfony 7", "React 19", "LÖVE 11", "PHP 8.3", …). Remote projects carry an **SSH** badge and
reconnect when you click them.

![Project type badges on the Welcome screen](docs/screenshots/welcome-project-badges.png)

Type in **Search projects** to filter by name or path. Click a row to open the project.

The list is stored in `recent-projects.json` in Forge's config folder (see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)).

### Empty state

On the very first start there are no recent projects, and the screen shows three large
buttons instead: **New Project**, **Open** and **Get from VCS**.

> **Note:** **Get from VCS** (cloning a repository) is not available yet; the button is
> disabled.

## Window title bar

Forge draws its own title bar. Its buttons look like your desktop's by default (Windows,
macOS traffic lights, GNOME or KDE Plasma). You can change the style, or switch back to the
operating system's own title bar, with Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance |
**Window controls**. See [Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#window-controls).

## What next

- [Open or create a project](docs/guide/getting-started/projects.md)
- [Learn the workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md)

title: Opening and creating projects
description: Open a folder as a project, create new projects with the New Project wizard and choose the default project directory.
order: 30
tags: [projects, new project, wizard, generators]
---

# Opening and creating projects

A Forge project is a folder. There is no project file to import: open the folder, and Forge
[detects what it contains](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md) and turns on the matching plugins.
Project-specific data lives in a `.forge/` folder inside the project (settings, run
configurations, breakpoints, data sources); see [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md).

## Open an existing project

- On the Welcome screen click **Open** and choose the folder.
- From a terminal: `forge path/to/project`.
- In the workbench, the project widget at the left of the main toolbar (the badge with the
  project name) runs **Open…** as well.

Opening a project replaces the current one in the same window and closes its editor tabs.

> **Note:** the setting "Open project in" (`system.openProjectIn`: new window, same window or
> ask) is not applied yet; projects always open in the current window.

Remote projects (folders on a Linux server reached over SSH) open from Welcome |
**Remote Development**, see [Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md).

To close the project and return to the Welcome screen, run **Close Project** through
[Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-action) (`Ctrl+Shift+A`).

## Create a new project

Click **New Project** on the Welcome screen, or run the **New Project…** action
(`NewProject`) with Find Action.

![New Project dialog](docs/screenshots/new-project-laravel.png)

1. Pick a generator on the left.
2. Enter the **Name** and the **Location**. "Project will be created in:" shows the final
   folder. The location defaults to the **Default project directory**.
3. Set the generator's options.
4. Check the **Commands to run** box: it shows exactly which commands Forge runs, or which
   files it writes for offline templates.
5. Click **Create**. The dialog shows the steps and their output, then opens the new project.

![Creating a project](docs/screenshots/new-project-progress.png)

### Generators

| Group | Generator | What it does | Needs | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP | Empty PHP Project | Composer project with PSR-4 autoloading, `src/`, `tests/` and PHPUnit | — (offline template) | PHP version, sample code, Git repository |
| PHP | Laravel | `composer create-project laravel/laravel` or a starter kit (`laravel/react-starter-kit`, `laravel/vue-starter-kit`, `laravel/livewire-starter-kit`) | `composer` | Starter kit (None, React, Vue, Livewire), Git repository |
| PHP | Symfony | `symfony new` when the Symfony CLI is installed, else `composer create-project symfony/skeleton` | `composer` | Project type (Web application, Skeleton), Git repository |
| PHP | Composer Package | reusable library with PHPUnit, README and MIT licence | — (offline template) | Vendor, PHP version, sample code, Git repository |
| PHP | WordPress Plugin | plugin header, main class, shortcode, `readme.txt`, uninstall hook | — (offline template) | PHP version, Git repository |
| Web | Empty HTML/CSS/JS | `index.html`, a stylesheet and a script | — (offline template) | sample code, Git repository |
| Web | Vite + TypeScript | `npm create vite@latest` (vanilla TypeScript) | `npm` | install dependencies, Git repository |
| Web | React | Vite React template | `npm` | TypeScript, install dependencies, Git repository |
| Web | Vue.js | Vite Vue 3 template | `npm` | TypeScript, install dependencies, Git repository |
| Web | Angular | `npx @angular/cli@latest new` | `npx` | install dependencies, Git repository |
| Web | Svelte | `npx sv create` (SvelteKit, minimal template) | `npx` | TypeScript, install dependencies, Git repository |
| Lua | Lua Script | a script, a module and a LuaLS configuration | — (offline template) | Lua version, sample code, Git repository |
| Lua | LÖVE Game | LÖVE 11 game with `main.lua`, `conf.lua` and API completion | — (offline template) | sample code, Git repository |
| Lua | Neovim Plugin | plugin with `setup()`, a user command and a help file | — (offline template) | GitHub user, Git repository |
| Other | Empty Project | an empty folder | — | Git repository |

Generators that call an official CLI (composer, symfony, npm, npx) check that the tool is on
your `PATH` first. If it is missing, the dialog says so and offers an offline alternative, for
example "Create Empty HTML/CSS/JS instead":

![Missing tool](docs/screenshots/new-project-missing-tool.png)

**Create Git repository** runs `git init` in the new folder.

## Default project directory

New projects go to `~/Projects` unless you pick another location. Change it in
Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings | **Default project directory**
(`system.defaultProjectDirectory`).

![Default project directory setting](docs/screenshots/settings-default-project-directory.png)

## Demo projects (browser mode)

When Forge runs in a plain browser for development (`pnpm dev`, see
[Development setup](docs/guide/developer/dev-setup.md)), it opens built-in demo projects instead of
folders on disk: a Laravel shop by default, and Symfony, React, Vue, Angular, Lua (LÖVE) and
remote demos with `?project=symfony|react|vue|angular|lua|remote`. They exist for screenshots
and development and are not part of the desktop app.


---

Source: docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md

---
title: Project type detection
description: How Forge recognizes languages, frameworks and tools in a project and which plugins it activates for them.
order: 40
tags: [projects, detection, plugins, packs]
---

# Project type detection

When a project opens, Forge reads marker files in the project root **and one folder level
below it** (so a monorepo with `backend/` and `frontend/` is understood) and decides which
languages, frameworks and tools the project uses. Plugins that belong to a framework only
activate when that framework is found, so a Laravel project does not show Symfony tool windows
and a plain Lua project does not start PHP language servers.

## What is detected

### Languages

| Language | Detected from |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `composer.json`, or any `.php` file |
| TypeScript | `tsconfig.json`, `.ts` or `.tsx` files |
| JavaScript | `.js`, `.mjs` or `.jsx` files |
| HTML | `.html` or `.htm` files |
| CSS | `.css` or `.scss` files |
| Lua | a `.lua` file in the root, two or more `.lua` files in a folder, `.luarc.json`, `.luarc.jsonc`, `.luacheckrc`, `stylua.toml`, `.stylua.toml`, `selene.toml` or a `*.rockspec` |
| Rust | `Cargo.toml` |
| Go | `go.mod` |
| Python | `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` or `setup.py` |

### Frameworks

| Framework | Detected from |
| --- | --- |
| Laravel | `laravel/framework` in `composer.json`, or an `artisan` file |
| Symfony | `symfony/framework-bundle`, or `bin/console` together with `config/bundles.php` |
| Doctrine | `doctrine/orm` |
| Drupal | `drupal/core` or `drupal/core-recommended` |
| Magento | `magento/framework`, `magento/product-community-edition`, or `app/etc/env.php` with `bin/magento` |
| WordPress | `johnpbloch/wordpress`, `roots/wordpress`, `wp-config.php`, `wp-config-sample.php` or `wp-includes/` |
| Livewire | `livewire/livewire` |
| PHPUnit, Pest | `phpunit/phpunit`, `pestphp/pest` |
| Next.js, Nuxt, React, Vue.js, Svelte, Solid, Vite | `next`, `nuxt`, `react`, `vue`, `svelte`, `solid-js`, `vite` in `package.json`; Vite also from a `vite.config.*` file |
| Angular | `@angular/core` in `package.json`, or `angular.json` |
| LÖVE | `conf.lua`, or a `main.lua` that uses `love.` |
| Neovim | `init.lua` next to a `lua/` folder (or one that uses `vim.`), or `lua/` together with `plugin/` |

Versions come from `composer.lock` / the npm lock files when present, otherwise from the
version constraints in the manifests. The PHP version comes from `require.php`.

### Tools

`composer`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` (from lock files and `package.json`), `luarocks`
(`*.rockspec`), `docker` (`Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml`/`compose.yml`,
`docker-compose.yml`/`.yaml`) and `git` (a `.git` folder).

Folders that are never scanned as sub-projects: `vendor`, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`,
`build`, `storage`, `var`, `public` and hidden folders. At most 64 sub-folders are checked.

## Primary type

The most specific framework becomes the project's **primary** type, in this order: Laravel,
Symfony, Drupal, WordPress, Magento, Next.js, Nuxt, Angular, Svelte, Vue.js, React, Solid, LÖVE,
Neovim, Vite. Without a framework the primary language is used (PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript,
Lua, Rust, Go, Python, HTML, CSS).

The primary type appears

- as the badge next to the project on the Welcome screen,
- in the status bar (for example "Laravel 12"); click it to open Settings | Plugins. Laravel
  and Symfony replace this widget with their own (see [Laravel](docs/guide/user/laravel.md) and
  [Symfony](docs/guide/user/symfony.md)),
- in a one-time balloon "Laravel project detected — Laravel support enabled" with a
  **Configure** link to the framework's settings page.

![Detected project balloon](docs/screenshots/project-detected-balloon.png)

## Packs and plugins that activate

| Pack | Activates for |
| --- | --- |
| PHPForge | PHP projects; Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine, Composer, PHPUnit/Pest and Xdebug plugins for their framework or tool |
| WebForge | JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML or CSS; React for `react`/`next`, Vue.js for `vue`/`nuxt`, Angular for `angular` |
| LuaForge | Lua projects |

Core plugins (Git, Terminal, Run/Debug, Database, Services, AI, language servers, …) are
always active. Each plugin can still be switched off in Settings | Plugins, see
[Plugins and packs](docs/guide/user/plugins-and-packs.md). The exact rules are the `projectTypes`
of each plugin, listed in [Reference: plugins](docs/guide/reference/plugins.md).

## Re-detect

Detection runs when the project opens. If you add a framework later (for example
`composer require symfony/framework-bundle`), run **Detect Project Type** with Find Action
(`Ctrl+Shift+A`), or reopen the project, so the new plugins activate.

Source: docs/guide/getting-started/from-phpstorm.md

---
title: Coming from PHPStorm
description: A quick switch guide for PHPStorm users - what works the same, what is different and what Forge does not have yet.
order: 50
tags: [phpstorm, migration, keymap]
---

# Coming from PHPStorm

Forge copies PHPStorm's New UI on purpose: the layout, the names of tool windows and actions,
the Settings tree and the default keymap are the same. The colors are Forge's own ("Ember"
dark and "Anvil" light). This page lists what you can rely on, what works differently, and
what is not there yet.

## Same as in PHPStorm

- **Keymap.** Forge ships PHPStorm's default keymaps for Windows/Linux and macOS and uses
  PHPStorm's action ids (`GotoClass`, `ReformatCode`, `CheckinProject`, …). `Double Shift`,
  `Ctrl+Shift+A`, `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+N`, `Ctrl+E`, `Ctrl+B`, `Alt+Insert`, `Ctrl+K`,
  `Shift+F10`, `Alt+1` … `Alt+0` and `Alt+F12` do what you expect. See the
  [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md).
- **Workbench.** Main menu (☰, merged or as a menu bar), main toolbar with project and branch
  widgets, run widget and search; tool
  window stripes on the left, right and bottom; editor tabs with breadcrumbs; status bar.
- **Tool windows** with the same names and shortcuts: Project (`Alt+1`), Run (`Alt+4`), Debug
  (`Alt+5`), Problems (`Alt+6`), Structure (`Alt+7`), Services (`Alt+8`), Git (`Alt+9`), Commit
  (`Alt+0`), Terminal (`Alt+F12`), Database, Pull Requests, AI Chat.
- **Settings tree.** Appearance & Behavior, Keymap, Editor, Plugins, Version Control,
  Languages & Frameworks, Tools, Build, Execution, Deployment. `Ctrl+Alt+S` opens it.
- **Run/Debug configurations** with the same types for PHP (PHP Script, PHP Built-in Web
  Server, PHPUnit, PHP Remote Debug, Composer, Artisan) and "Store as project file".
- **Xdebug** on port 9003 with breakpoints, stepping (`F7`, `F8`, `Shift+F8`, `F9`),
  Evaluate Expression (`Alt+F8`), servers with path mappings and the "Incoming Connection From
  Xdebug" dialog.
- **Scratches and Consoles** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert`), including `.http` request files.
- **Database tools** for MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite with query consoles and a data
  grid.
- **Laravel and Symfony support** in the spirit of Laravel Idea and the Symfony plugin: route,
  view, config, service and template completion and navigation, gutter icons, artisan and
  console runners.

## Different from PHPStorm

| Topic | PHPStorm | Forge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP intelligence | built-in PHP engine | an external language server: Intelephense (free, or premium with your own licence key) or Phpactor, plus Forge's own PHP index for structure, search, hover and code generation. See [Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md). |
| Other languages | plugins | language servers from a catalog of about 30, installed from Settings, see [Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) |
| Projects | `.idea/` folder | `.forge/` folder with TOML/JSON files; there is no project model to import |
| Project tree | single click selects | single click **opens** files by default; switch off "Open files with single click" (Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance) for PHPStorm's behaviour |
| AI | AI Assistant subscription | bring your own provider (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) or your installed Claude Code / Gemini CLI |
| Plugins | Marketplace | built-in plugins grouped in packs (PHPForge, WebForge, LuaForge); no Marketplace yet |
| Remote development | Gateway | built in: SSH connection, Forge uploads a small agent to the host |
| Theme | Darcula/Light/New UI themes | Forge Ember (dark), Forge Anvil (light), Solarized Dark and Light |

## Not there yet

The following PHPStorm features are not implemented on this version. Their shortcuts stay
bound and show "*Action* is not available yet" so you are not surprised by something else
happening.

- Get from VCS
- Replace in Files (`Ctrl+Shift+R`), Find Usages (`Alt+F7`), Find tool window
- Refactorings: Rename (`Shift+F6`), Extract/Introduce, Move, Change Signature, Safe Delete
- Show Context Actions / quick-fixes (`Alt+Enter`), Quick Documentation popup (`Ctrl+Q`; hover
  documentation works with the mouse), File Structure popup (`Ctrl+F12`)
- Bookmarks, TODO and Notifications tool windows, Local History
- Live templates, Surround With, Optimize Imports, Type/Call/Method Hierarchy
- Go to Implementation (`Ctrl+Alt+B`), Go to Super Method, Go to Test
- Split editors, Distraction Free / Presentation / Zen modes
- Get from VCS, stash/unstash, Commit and Push
- Marketplace, settings export/import, automatic updates

The [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) marks every action as implemented or not.

## Moving a project over

1. Open the project folder in Forge. The `.idea/` folder is ignored; nothing is converted.
2. Install the language servers you need from Settings | Languages & Frameworks |
   Language Servers. For PHP, accept the offer "Intelephense is not installed" (or click **Install
   Intelephense**) and, if you own a licence, enter the key on the same page.
3. Set the PHP interpreter and language level in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP.
4. Recreate run configurations in Run | Edit Configurations (the run widget in the toolbar).
   PHPStorm's `.run/` XML files are not imported.
5. Recreate data sources in the Database tool window. Laravel's `DB_*` and Symfony's
   `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` are offered automatically.
6. If you changed shortcuts in PHPStorm, re-assign them in Settings | Keymap. Keymap files
   cannot be imported yet.

---
title: Workbench and tool windows

# Workbench and tool windows

The workbench is the main window of an open project. It follows PHPStorm's New UI.

![The workbench](docs/screenshots/workbench-dark.png)

| Area | Where | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main toolbar | top | ☰ main menu, project widget, Git branch widget, run widget, AI Chat, Search Everywhere, theme toggle, Settings; it is also the window's title bar |
| Tool window stripes | left, right and bottom edges | buttons that show and hide tool windows |
| Editor | center | tabs, breadcrumbs and the code editor |
| Status bar | bottom | path of the current file, background tasks, project information, caret position, file type, Git branch |

## Main toolbar

From left to right:

- **☰ Main Menu** (`Alt+\`), see [Main menu](#main-menu) below.

- **Project widget**: the badge and name of the open project; click it to open another
  project.
- **Branch widget**: the current Git branch; click it for the [Branches popup](docs/guide/user/git.md#branches).
- Toolbar items of plugins, for example Xdebug's **Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections**
  button (see [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md)).
- **Run widget**: the selected run configuration with **Run** and **Debug** buttons, see
  [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md).
- **AI Chat**, **Search Everywhere** (`Double Shift`), the **theme toggle** (dark/light) and
  **Settings** (`Ctrl+Alt+S`).

Empty parts of the toolbar move the window; a double click maximizes it. The window buttons
sit at the toolbar's ends, styled for your desktop (see
[Window controls](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#window-controls)).

## Main menu

The main menu has PHPStorm's menus: **File, Edit, View, Navigate, Code, Refactor, Run, Tools,
Git** (**VCS** in projects without Git), **Window** and **Help**. Every entry shows its shortcut;
actions Forge has not implemented yet stay visible but disabled. Plugins add their own entries,
for example Tools | Laravel (Run Artisan Command…, Show Routes), Tools | Symfony and
Run | Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections. File | Open Recent and View | Tool Windows are
filled with your recent projects and the available tool windows.
File | New | **File** and **Directory** create the entry in the folder selected in the Project
view, else in the folder of the active editor, else in the project root (nested paths such as
`Jobs/SendMail.php` create the folders too).

![Main menu](docs/screenshots/main-menu-file.png)

Where the menu appears is chosen with Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | UI
Options | **Main menu** (`appearance.mainMenu`), as in PHPStorm's New UI:

| Value | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `hamburger` (default) — Hamburger menu | behind the ☰ button at the left of the main toolbar |
| `merged` — Merged with main toolbar | the menu names (File, Edit, …) directly in the main toolbar |
| `toolbar` — Show in separate toolbar | a classic menu bar above the main toolbar |

View | Appearance | **Show Main Menu in Separate Toolbar** switches to the last mode from the
menu itself; **Compact Mode** and **Tool Window Bars** are toggles in the same submenu.

![Merged with the main toolbar](docs/screenshots/main-menu-merged.png)

Keyboard: `Alt+\` opens the menu; the underlined letter (mnemonic) picks an entry, alone or with
`Alt`; arrow keys move, `Right`/`Left` open and close submenus and switch between the menus of
the menu bar; `Escape` closes. **Help | About** shows the version; **Help | Keymap Reference**
opens Settings | Keymap; **Help | Check for Updates…** checks for a new version (see
[Updates](docs/guide/getting-started/first-start.md#updates)).

![Main menu in a separate toolbar](docs/screenshots/main-menu-bar.png)

## Tool windows

Tool windows are the panels along the edges. Click a stripe button, or press the tool window's
shortcut, to show it; pressing the shortcut again hides it, as in PHPStorm.

| Tool window | Stripe | Shortcut | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project | left | `Alt+1` (macOS `Cmd+1`) | below |
| Commit | left | `Alt+0` (macOS `Cmd+0`) | [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md) |
| Pull Requests | left | — | [Code hosts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md) |
| Structure | left | `Alt+7` (macOS `Cmd+7`) | [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#structure), [LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md) |
| npm | left | — | [WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md) |
| Run | bottom | `Alt+4` (macOS `Cmd+4`) | [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md) |
| Debug | bottom | `Alt+5` (macOS `Cmd+5`) | [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md) |
| Services | bottom | `Alt+8` (macOS `Cmd+8`) | [Services](docs/guide/user/services.md) |
| Routes (Laravel) | bottom | — | [Laravel](docs/guide/user/laravel.md) |
| Symfony | bottom | — | [Symfony](docs/guide/user/symfony.md) |
| Terminal | bottom | `Alt+F12` | [Terminal](docs/guide/user/terminal.md) |
| Problems | bottom | `Alt+6` (macOS `Cmd+6`) | [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#problems) |
| Git | bottom | `Alt+9` (macOS `Cmd+9`) | [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#log) |
| AI Chat | right | — | [AI](docs/guide/user/ai.md) |
| Database | right | — | [Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md) |
| Doctrine | right | — | [Doctrine](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md) |
| Notifications | right | — | placeholder, see note |

Framework tool windows (Routes, Symfony, Doctrine, npm) only appear in projects that use the
framework.

> **Note:** the Notifications tool window is a placeholder ("coming soon"). Bookmarks
> (`Alt+2`), Find (`Alt+3`) and TODO are not available yet.

### Managing tool windows

| Action | Shortcut (Windows/Linux) | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hide the active tool window | `Shift+Escape` | `Shift+Escape` |
| Hide all tool windows (again: restore) | `Ctrl+Shift+F12` | `Cmd+Shift+F12` |
| Jump to the last tool window | `F12` | `F12` |
| Stretch the focused tool window | `Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right/Up/Down` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left/Right/Up/Down` |
| Close the active tab of a tool window (Run, Terminal) | `Ctrl+Shift+F4` | `Cmd+Shift+F4` |

**Hide Side Tool Windows** has no default shortcut; run it from Find Action. Drag the border
between a tool window and the editor to resize it.

The stripes can be hidden with Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Show tool
window bars**. **Compact mode** on the same page makes toolbars and tool window headers
smaller.

> **Note:** tool window sizes and which tool windows are open are not remembered between
> sessions yet. "Restore Default Layout" and "Maximize Tool Window" are not available yet.

## Project view

The Project tool window (`Alt+1`) shows the project folder as a tree.

- **Single click opens** a file and expands a folder by default. To work like PHPStorm (single
  click selects, double click opens), turn off Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance |
  Project View | **Open files with single click** (`projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick`).
- **Keyboard**: `Up`/`Down` move the selection, `Right` expands, `Left` collapses or goes to
  the parent, `Home`/`End` jump to the first/last row, `Enter` or `F4` opens.
- Files and folders ignored by Git (`.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, the global excludes
  file) are grayed out.
- **Scratches and Consoles** appear at the bottom of the tree, see
  [Scratches, consoles and HTTP client](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md).

![Project view](docs/screenshots/project-tree-double-click.png)

### Context menu

Right-click a file, a folder or the empty area below the tree:

| Entry | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| New > File / Directory | Creates a file or folder in the selected folder (or the file's folder). The name may contain `/` to create nested folders, e.g. `app/Models/Order.php`. A new file opens in the editor. |
| Copy Path/Reference > Absolute Path (`Ctrl+Shift+C`), Path From Project Root, File Name | Copies to the clipboard |
| Find in Files… | searches the folder (or the project), see [Find in Files](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files) |
| Rename… | Renames the file or folder. Unsaved changes in open tabs are saved first and the tabs follow the new name. |
| Delete… | Deletes after a confirmation; folders with all their content. This cannot be undone. |
| Reload from Disk | Re-reads the folder |

![Project view context menu](docs/screenshots/file-menu-new-file.png)

## Editor tabs

- Each open file has a tab. The active one is highlighted; a modified file is marked until it
  is saved.
- Close a tab with its × button, a middle click, or `Ctrl+F4` (macOS `Cmd+W`).
- `Alt+Right` / `Alt+Left` (macOS `Ctrl+Right` / `Ctrl+Left`) select the next/previous tab.
- **Close All Tabs**, **Close Other Tabs**, **Close Unmodified Tabs** and **Reopen Closed Tab**
  are available through Find Action.
- `Ctrl+S` (macOS `Cmd+S`) saves all files (**Save All**).
- Some tabs are not files: merge requests, issues, database consoles and table editors open as
  tabs as well.

Breadcrumbs above the editor show the file's folder path.

> **Note:** pinned tabs and split editors are not available yet.

## Recent Files and Switcher

**Recent Files** (`Ctrl+E`, macOS `Cmd+E`) lists tool windows on the left and recently opened
files on the right. Type to filter (speed search). Press `Ctrl+E` again to show only
recently **edited** files; **Recently Changed Files** opens that view directly.

![Recent Files](docs/screenshots/recent-files.png)

The **Switcher** (`Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab`) is the same popup for quick switching: keep
`Ctrl` pressed, press `Tab` to move, release to open.

**Back** and **Forward** (`Ctrl+Alt+Left` / `Ctrl+Alt+Right`, macOS `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]`) move
through your navigation history.

## Status bar

![Status bar while indexing](docs/screenshots/status-bar-indexing.png)

Left: the project name and the path of the current file. Right, depending on the project:

| Widget | Shows | Click |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remote connection | host and latency of a remote project | connection popup, see [Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) |
| Xdebug | listening state and port | [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md) |
| PHP indexing | "Indexing… 45%" while the PHP index is built | — |
| Language servers | "Indexing… TypeScript 45%" or the running servers | opens Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers |
| Docker | connection to the Docker daemon | [Services](docs/guide/user/services.md) |
| Project type | "Laravel 12", "Symfony 7.2 · dev", "React 19" | Settings | Plugins, or the framework's popup |
| PHP version | the PHP language level, e.g. "PHP 8.3" | PHP settings |
| CI status | pipeline status of the current branch | [Code hosts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md) |
| Caret | `line:column` | — |
| `LF`, `UTF-8`, `4 spaces` | line separator, encoding and indentation | — |
| File type | e.g. "PHP", "Blade", "TypeScript" | — |
| Branch | the current Git branch | — |

> **Note:** the line separator, encoding and indentation widgets are labels only; they
> cannot be changed from the status bar yet.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/editor.md

---
title: Editor
description: Editing, completion, hover documentation, Parameter Info, Go to Declaration, problems, formatting, folding, find and replace, gutter icons and the editor context menu.
order: 20
tags: [editor, completion, hover, navigation, diagnostics, context menu]
---

# Editor

Forge's editor is built on CodeMirror 6. Language intelligence (completion, hover, diagnostics,
Go to Declaration, formatting) comes from [language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) and from
Forge's own indexes for PHP, Lua and the frameworks. Shortcuts below are the Windows/Linux
defaults with macOS in parentheses; the full list is in the
[keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md).

## Code completion

- Completion pops up while you type, from the language server(s) of the file and, in
  framework projects, from Forge's framework sources (Laravel routes and views, Symfony
  services, Twig, DQL, …). Each item has a kind icon (class, method, property, variable,
  keyword, …).
- **Basic Completion** `Ctrl+Space` (also `Shift+Space`) opens it explicitly. Then words
  that already occur in the document are offered as well; this works in every file, even
  without a language server.
- `Enter` or `Tab` accepts. Functions are inserted with parentheses and the caret between
  them; snippet placeholders from the server can be filled in with `Tab`.
- Brackets and quotes are closed automatically.

![Completion](docs/screenshots/lsp-completion.png)

## Quick documentation on hover

Hold the mouse over a symbol to see its documentation: signature, description, parameters
and return value, deprecation notes and links, rendered PHPStorm-style. Problems at that
position are shown in the same popup.

For PHP, Forge merges the language server's answer with its own index (PHPDoc, attributes,
inherited documentation) and falls back to the index when no server runs. Lua uses LuaForge's
index until lua-language-server answers.

![Hover documentation](docs/screenshots/lsp-hover.png)

> **Note:** the keyboard actions Quick Documentation (`Ctrl+Q`) and External Documentation
> (`Shift+F1`) are not available yet; use the mouse hover.

## Parameter Info

**Parameter Info** (`Ctrl+P`, macOS `Cmd+P`) shows the parameters of the call at the caret,
the current one in bold, with its documentation. It also opens automatically after you type
`(` and follows you as you type `,`.

![Parameter Info](docs/screenshots/lsp-parameter-info.png)

## Go to Declaration

**Go to Declaration or Usages** (`Ctrl+B`, macOS `Cmd+B`) or `Ctrl+Click` (macOS
`Cmd+Click`) jumps to the declaration of the symbol at the caret. While `Ctrl` is held, the
symbol under the mouse is underlined like a link.

Forge first asks its framework providers, which know things a language server cannot
resolve: Laravel route names, views, config keys and Eloquent attributes; Symfony service ids,
routes and Twig templates; Doctrine entities and DQL fields; React/Vue/Angular components and
props; Lua modules. Then it asks the language server.

When there are several targets — from a framework provider (a view that exists in two places, a
component used in many templates) or from the language server — the **Choose Declaration**
popup lists them at the caret with file, line and the code of each target, as in PHPStorm. Pick
one with the arrow keys and `Enter`, or `Escape` to cancel. The same popup is used by line
markers with several targets, in every language pack (PHP and its frameworks, WebForge,
LuaForge).

![Choose Declaration in React](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-choose-declaration-react.png)

![Choose Declaration in Lua](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-choose-declaration-lua.png)

If nothing is found, a hint "Cannot find declaration to go to" appears at the caret.

**Back** / **Forward** (`Ctrl+Alt+Left` / `Ctrl+Alt+Right`, macOS `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]`) return
to where you were.

> **Note:** Go to Implementation (`Ctrl+Alt+B`), Type Declaration, Super Method, Test and
> Find Usages (`Alt+F7`) are not available yet. In React and Vue projects, Go to Declaration on
> a component's own name lists its usages instead.

## Problems

Diagnostics from language servers (and Forge's own syntax checks for YAML, JSON, INI, dotenv,
Bash, Python, Postfix and similar files) appear as:

- squiggles: red for errors, yellow for warnings, a weaker underline for weak warnings; unused
  code is grayed, deprecated usages are struck through;
- markers in the gutter;
- the **inspection widget** in the top-right corner of the editor: a ✓ when the file is clean,
  otherwise the number of errors and warnings. Click it to open the Problems tool window.

**Next Highlighted Error** `F2` and **Previous Highlighted Error** `Shift+F2` move the caret
between problems.

The **Problems** tool window (`Alt+6`, macOS `Cmd+6`) has two tabs: **Current File** and
**Project Errors**, each a file → problem tree. Click a problem to open it.

![Problems tool window](docs/screenshots/lsp-problems.png)

> **Note:** quick-fixes and Show Context Actions (`Alt+Enter`) are not available yet.

## Reformat Code

**Reformat Code** (`Ctrl+Alt+L`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+L`) formats the file with the language
server's document formatting. Lua files use StyLua when it is installed (see
[LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md)).

## Editing actions

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duplicate Line or Selection | `Ctrl+D` | `Cmd+D` |
| Delete Line | `Ctrl+Y` | `Cmd+Backspace` |
| Comment with Line Comment | `Ctrl+/` | `Cmd+/` |
| Comment with Block Comment | `Ctrl+Shift+/` | `Cmd+Alt+/` |
| Move Line Up / Down | `Alt+Shift+Up` / `Down` | same |
| Move Statement Up / Down (moves the line) | `Ctrl+Shift+Up` / `Down` | `Cmd+Shift+Up` / `Down` |
| Extend / Shrink Selection | `Ctrl+W` / `Ctrl+Shift+W` | `Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down` |
| Add Selection for Next Occurrence | `Alt+J` | `Ctrl+G` |
| Unselect Occurrence | `Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` |
| Select All Occurrences | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Cmd+G` |
| Join Lines | `Ctrl+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+J` |
| Toggle Case | `Ctrl+Shift+U` | `Cmd+Shift+U` |
| Split Line | `Ctrl+Enter` | `Cmd+Enter` |
| Start New Line | `Shift+Enter` | `Shift+Enter` |
| Start New Line Before Current | `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` | `Cmd+Alt+Enter` |
| Auto-Indent Lines | `Ctrl+Alt+I` | `Ctrl+Alt+I` |
| Move Caret to Matching Brace | `Ctrl+Shift+M` | `Ctrl+M` |
| Scroll Up / Down | `Ctrl+Up` / `Ctrl+Down` | — |
| Go to Line/Column | `Ctrl+G` | `Cmd+L` |
| Undo / Redo | `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` |
| Copy Absolute Path | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Shift+C` |
| Copy Reference (`path:line`) | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+C` |

Without a selection, **Copy** and **Cut** take the whole line, as in PHPStorm. `Alt`+drag
makes a rectangular (column) selection.

## Folding

Click the fold markers in the gutter, or use:

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expand / Collapse | `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` | `Cmd+=` / `Cmd+-` |
| Expand / Collapse Recursively | `Ctrl+Alt+=` / `Ctrl+Alt+-` | `Cmd+Alt+=` / `Cmd+Alt+-` |
| Expand All / Collapse All | `Ctrl+Shift+=` / `Ctrl+Shift+-` | `Cmd+Shift+=` / `Cmd+Shift+-` |

## Find and replace in a file

**Find** (`Ctrl+F`, macOS `Cmd+F`) and **Replace** (`Ctrl+R`, macOS `Cmd+R`) open the search
panel of the editor (CodeMirror's search panel) with match case, regular expression and
whole word options. **Find Next**
`F3` and **Find Previous** `Shift+F3` (macOS `Cmd+G` / `Cmd+Shift+G`) move between matches.
Other occurrences of the selected text are highlighted automatically.

To search the whole project, use [Find in Files](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files)
(`Ctrl+Shift+F`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+F`).

> **Note:** Replace in Files (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) and the Find tool window are not available yet.

## Gutter

Left of the text, from outside in: line numbers, feature icons, Git change markers, fold
markers.

- **Git change markers** show added, modified and deleted lines compared with `HEAD`. Click
  one to see the change, roll it back or open the diff. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#in-the-editor).
- **Line markers** of plugins: routes on controller actions, "go to template", entity ⇄
  repository, Angular component ⇄ template, compose services, and more. Click to navigate.
- **Run icons** ▶ next to PHPUnit tests, `package.json` scripts, Lua main chunks, scratch
  files, `.http` requests, compose services and Dockerfiles.
- **Breakpoints**: click a line number in a PHP file to toggle a breakpoint (drawn over the
  number, as in the New UI), or press `Ctrl+F8` (macOS `Cmd+F8`). Right-click it to edit its
  condition. See [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md).
- **Annotate with Git Blame**: right-click the gutter. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#blame).

## Context menu

Right-click in the editor (or press the `Menu` key on Windows/Linux keyboards) to open the
editor context menu:

![Editor context menu](docs/screenshots/context-menu-editor.png)

| Entry | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Show Context Actions | not available yet |
| Paste from History… | not available yet |
| Cut, Copy, Paste | works |
| Copy / Paste Special > Copy Absolute Path, Copy Reference, Paste as Plain Text | works |
| Select All | works |
| Column Selection Mode | not available yet (use `Alt`+drag) |
| Find Usages | not available yet |
| Refactor > Rename…, Refactor This… | not available yet |
| Go To > Declaration or Usages, Line/Column | works |
| Go To > Implementation(s) | not available yet |
| Generate… | works in PHP files, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate) |
| Reformat Code | works |
| Optimize Imports | not available yet |
| Comment with Line Comment | works |
| Git > Annotate with Git Blame | works |

Right-clicking outside the current selection moves the caret there first, like PHPStorm.

## Files changed on disk

When a file changes on disk (a checkout, a pull, a rollback, an AI agent's edit, a change in
another editor), the open tab is reloaded with the new content. The reload is not an undo
step: `Ctrl+Z` does not go back across it.

Line endings are preserved: a file with Windows line endings (CRLF) stays CRLF when you save
it.

## Soft wraps and appearance

Settings | Editor | General controls soft wrapping (`editor.softWraps` with the patterns in
`editor.softWrapFiles`, by default `*.md; *.txt; *.rst; *.adoc`), whitespace, line numbers,
the caret row highlight, caret blinking and smooth scrolling. Settings | Editor | Font sets the
font, size, line height and ligatures. See the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

> **Note:** "Remove trailing spaces on save", "Ensure line break at end of file", the
> Code Style options and Inlay Hints are listed in Settings but not applied yet.

---
title: Search Everywhere and Find Action
description: Find files, classes, symbols and actions with Search Everywhere, Go to Class/File/Symbol and Find Action, and how fuzzy matching works.
order: 30
tags: [search, navigation, find action, go to file]

# Search Everywhere and Find Action

## Search Everywhere

Press `Shift` twice (**Double Shift**), or click the magnifier in the main toolbar.

![Search Everywhere](docs/screenshots/search-everywhere.png)

The popup has tabs; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` switch between them:

| Tab | Opens directly with | Finds | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All | `Double Shift` | the best few results of every tab | — |
| Classes | **Go to Class** `Ctrl+N` (macOS `Cmd+O`) | classes, interfaces, traits, enums, Lua classes | PHP index, LuaForge index, language servers (`workspace/symbol`) |
| Files | **Go to File** `Ctrl+Shift+N` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+O`) | project files; without a query, recent files | Forge's file search (respects `.gitignore`) |
| Symbols | **Go to Symbol** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` (macOS `Cmd+Alt+O`) | functions, methods, constants, properties | PHP index, LuaForge index, language servers |
| Actions | **Find Action** `Ctrl+Shift+A` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) | every IDE action and command | the keymap and registered commands |
| Text | — | lines of text in project files | Find in Files (`forge-find`) |

- `Up`/`Down`, `PageUp`/`PageDown` move the selection, `Enter` opens it, `Escape` closes.
- In the All tab, a "more" row under a group switches to that group's tab.
- Pressing a tab's shortcut again while the popup is open toggles the checkbox in the header:
  **Include non-project items** (most tabs) or **Include disabled actions** (Actions).

Results from language servers appear once a server for that language runs, so the Symbols
tab also finds TypeScript, Python, Go or Rust symbols in a polyglot project.

![Symbols from language servers](docs/screenshots/search-everywhere-lsp-symbols.png)

### Fuzzy matching

Matching works like PHPStorm's:

- Characters of the query must appear in order, case-insensitively.
- Matches at word starts, after separators (`/ _ - . : $` and spaces) and on **camel humps**
  score higher, so `OrCo` finds `OrderController` first and `usrctl` finds `UserController`.
- For files you can type part of the path: `models/user` finds `app/Models/User.php`.
- A file called exactly what you typed, with or without its extension, comes first (`user` puts `User.php` above `UserSeeder.php`), and files under `vendor`, `node_modules` and similar folders rank below the project's own files with the same match. When nothing matches, Go to File and the Files tab try once more with one swapped pair of neighbouring letters or one extra letter in the query (`ordre` finds `Order.php`); this is off in substring mode. In Search Everywhere's Files tab, files you opened recently and files next to the one you are editing get a small boost.
- For classes, symbols and actions a word must start where a hump or separator starts
  ("strict" matching), which keeps the lists short.

![Go to File with camel humps](docs/screenshots/goto-file-camel-humps.png)

To match only text that contains what you typed, turn off **Settings > Tools > Search > Fuzzy
matching** (`search.everywhere.fuzzy`). Files, Classes and Symbols in Search Everywhere and Go to
File then find `OrderCon` in `OrderController` but no longer `orco`. PHP and Lua classes from their
own language index and the Actions tab keep fuzzy matching.

The button at the right end of the search field switches between fuzzy and substring matching for the current session without touching the setting.

![Substring matching switched on in Go to File](docs/screenshots/search-index-exact-toggle.png)

Ranking happens in Rust (`forge-fuzzy`), so the same rules apply in every list with a
speed search: Recent Files, the New Scratch File popup, choosers.

## Find Action

**Find Action** (`Ctrl+Shift+A`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) is the Actions tab on its own. Type an
action's name, for example "reformat", "commit", "new scratch" or "close project".

![Find Action](docs/screenshots/find-action.png)

- Each row shows the action, its menu group (e.g. "Code | Folding") and its shortcut.
- You can also type the action id (`ReformatCode`), which ranks below title matches.
- Actions Forge has not implemented yet are dimmed and listed last; running one shows
  "*Action* is not available yet". Turn on **Include disabled actions** to see them while
  searching.

Find Action is the fastest way to reach commands that have no shortcut and no menu yet, for
example **Close Project**, **Detect Project Type**, **Reindex PHP Files**, **Show Git Log**,
**Fetch** or **New SSH Connection…**.

## Recent Files

See [Workbench: Recent Files and Switcher](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher).

## Find in Files

**Find in Files** (`Ctrl+Shift+F`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+F`, also Edit | Find | Find in Files… and
the Project view's context menu) searches the text of every project file.

![Find in Files](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-find-in-files.png)

The status bar shows the size of the search index ("272,700 files", or "Indexing" while it builds or refreshes). Hover it for how many files are searched by content, how many binary or oversized files are listed by name only, and when the index was last updated.

![Search index in the status bar](docs/screenshots/search-index-status.png)

- Type the text; results update as you type, one row per matching line with the file name and
  line number. The header counts matches and files.
- Options next to the field: **Cc** match case, **W** whole words, **.\*** regular expression.
- **Scope** tabs under the field: **In Project**, **Directory** (a project-relative folder), **Open Files** (the editor tabs) and **Changed Files** (files git reports as modified, added or untracked). The open and changed lists are taken when the search runs; the Find window keeps the list it was opened with.

![Find in Files scopes](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-scopes.png)

- In the Find window, the list next to the directory field adds **lines of context** (1 to 5) above and below each match. Context lines are dimmed, shown once even when two matches share them, and a click opens the file there.

![Find window with context lines](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-context.png)

- In the Find window, the first list next to the directory field orders the files: **By path** (which also groups them by folder), **By matches** (most matching lines first) or **By modified** (newest first; only for the project's own files, a remote project keeps the path order).

![Find window ordered by matches](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-sorted.png)

- **File mask**: tick it and enter patterns such as `*.php` or `*.php, !*Test.php`
  (`!` excludes).
- Scope: **In Project** or **Directory** (a folder of the project; empty means the project
  root).
- `Up`/`Down` select a row; the preview below shows the file around the match. `Enter` opens
  the file at the match, `Escape` closes.

Ignored files (`.gitignore`), binary files and very large files are skipped. In remote projects
the search runs on the host.

The **Text** tab of Search Everywhere uses the same search (from two characters on).

> **Note:** Replace in Files (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) and the Find tool window ("Open in Find Tool
> Window") are not available yet.

Source: docs/guide/user/file-types.md

---
title: File types and syntax highlighting
description: How Forge recognizes file types, which languages it highlights, the extra support for config formats, and template data languages for Twig, Smarty, Latte and others.
order: 40
tags: [file types, syntax highlighting, templates, twig, smarty, data languages]
---

# File types and syntax highlighting

## How a file's type is chosen

Like PHPStorm's Settings | Editor | File Types, Forge decides a file's type from, in this order:

1. **file names and path patterns**, e.g. `Dockerfile`, `.env.local`, `composer.lock`,
   `config/services.yaml` (in Symfony projects);
2. the **longest matching extension**, so `user.blade.php` is Blade, not PHP, and
   `page.html.twig` is Twig;
3. the **interpreter of a `#!` line** for files without an extension (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`,
   `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, `#!/usr/bin/env lua`).

Files that match nothing are "Plain text". The type is shown in the status bar and decides the
highlighting, the indentation (2 or 4 spaces), the language server and the file icon.

Plugins add types or replace bundled ones while they are active: in a Symfony project
`config/services*.yaml` becomes "Symfony Services", elsewhere it is plain YAML.

The complete list of types, extensions and file names is in the
[file types reference](docs/guide/reference/file-types.md).

## Highlighted languages

About 70 languages are highlighted, among them PHP, Blade, Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja2,
Handlebars, Go templates, Velocity, Pug, HTML, CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less, Stylus, JavaScript,
TypeScript (and JSX/TSX), Vue, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, Markdown, SQL, Lua, Python, Go, Rust,
Java, Kotlin, C, C++, C#, Ruby, Shell, PowerShell, Dockerfile, Nginx, Apache config, INI,
dotenv, Makefile, CMake, LaTeX, HTTP requests and many more.

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![TypeScript](docs/screenshots/syntax-typescript.png) | ![YAML](docs/screenshots/syntax-yaml.png) | ![Twig](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig.png) |
| ![Dockerfile](docs/screenshots/syntax-dockerfile.png) | ![.env](docs/screenshots/syntax-env.png) | ![Markdown](docs/screenshots/syntax-markdown.png) |

## Config and script formats with extra support

Some formats get more than colors, without needing a language server:

| Format | Files | Extras |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell Script | `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.bats`, `.bashrc`, `.profile`, `PKGBUILD`, `#!` scripts | completion of keywords, builtins, functions and variables; folding |
| Python | `.py`, `.pyi`, `SConstruct`, `#!` scripts | scope-aware completion, syntax checks |
| YAML | `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.neon`, `.clang-format`, … | folding, syntax checks |
| JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, `.lock`, `.babelrc`, `composer.lock`, … | folding, syntax checks |
| Dotenv | `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.*.local`, `.env.example`, … | `${VAR}` interpolation, completion of variables in the file, Symfony Flex section folding, checks for unquoted spaces, unterminated quotes and duplicate keys |
| Ignore files | `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore`, `.npmignore`, `.*ignore` | pattern syntax, duplicate pattern hints |
| Dockerfile | `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.*`, `Containerfile`, `.dockerfile` | instruction, flag, stage and build-arg completion, hover docs, checks (unknown instruction, missing `FROM`) |
| Docker Compose | `compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `compose.*.yaml`, … | Compose Specification completion and hover docs, works in incomplete files |
| INI | `.ini`, `php.ini`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitconfig`, systemd units, `my.cnf`, … | section folding, checks for broken sections and duplicate keys |
| Config | `.conf`, `.config` | key/value pairs, interpolation, nginx-style blocks |
| Postfix | `main.cf`, `master.cf` | parameter and restriction completion with documentation, lookup table types, checks |
| E-Mail | `.eml` | header/MIME highlighting, header completion, decoding of encoded words on hover, folding, checks |
| Symfony Services | `config/services*.yaml` (Symfony projects) | service, parameter and tag completion, `@service` and `%parameter%` highlighting |

These syntax checks feed the Problems view, but step aside when a language server for the
file is running (for example yaml-language-server), so you do not get every problem twice.

## Template data languages

Template languages (Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja2, Handlebars, Go templates) mix template tags
with content in another language, the **data language**. Forge highlights the content in its
real language and draws the template tags on top, so a LaTeX or SQL template is just as
readable as an HTML one.

![Twig in LaTeX](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig-latex.png)

The data language of a file is chosen from the first of these that applies:

1. the patterns in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | **Template Data Languages**
   (`templates.dataLanguages`), one entry per pattern: `legacy/latex/*.tpl=latex`,
   `*.mail.twig=text`;
2. a **compound file name**: `invoice.tex.twig` is LaTeX, `report.sql.twig` is SQL,
   `style.css.tpl` is CSS, `config.yaml.twig` is YAML;
3. HTML.

Data languages: `html`, `xml`, `latex`, `css`, `scss`, `less`, `javascript`, `typescript`,
`json`, `sql`, `yaml`, `ini`, `shell`, `go`, `text`. The setting can be stored per project and
applies to files opened afterwards.

![Twig in SQL](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig-sql.png)

### Smarty delimiters

Smarty's delimiters are configurable on the same page (`templates.smarty.leftDelimiter`,
`templates.smarty.rightDelimiter`, default `{` and `}`). Use e.g. `<{` and `}>` for LaTeX
templates, where `{` is part of the content.

![Smarty](docs/screenshots/syntax-smarty.png)

## Language intelligence

Highlighting is built in. Completion, hover and diagnostics for most languages come from a
[language server](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md); Forge suggests installing one when a file uses a
feature only a server provides (for example a JSON `$schema` or a YAML
`# yaml-language-server: $schema=` modeline).


---

Source: docs/guide/user/language-servers.md

---
title: Language servers
description: How Forge finds, installs, configures and starts language servers, Intelephense free and premium licence keys, and per-server settings.
order: 50
tags: [lsp, language servers, intelephense, phpactor, install]
---

# Language servers

Completion, hover documentation, diagnostics, Go to Declaration and formatting for most
languages come from **language servers**: separate programs that speak the Language Server
Protocol. Forge does not bundle them. It knows about 30 of them, finds the ones you have
installed, offers to install missing ones, and starts them when a project needs them.

Servers start **lazily**: when you open the first file of a language. Several servers can serve
the same file and their results are merged, for example TypeScript + ESLint + Tailwind CSS on
a `.tsx` file.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers

![Language Servers settings](docs/screenshots/language-servers-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start language servers for languages found in the project | `langservers.autoStart` | on |
| Files scanned to detect languages (ignored files, `node_modules` and `vendor` are skipped) | `langservers.scanLimit` | 20000 |
| Suggest installing missing language servers | `langservers.hints.enabled` | on |

Below is the server table, grouped by language. Groups for languages that occur in the open
project are marked **used in this project**; **Project languages only** hides the others. The
header shows how many servers are running and installed, and **Detect Again** (the refresh
icon) searches for executables again.

Each row has:

- an **Enabled** checkbox (`langservers.servers.<id>.enabled`);
- the **Status**: Running (with indexing progress), Installed, Not found, Disabled, or why a
  server is skipped (for example "Chosen in Languages & Frameworks | PHP" for the PHP
  servers, or a server of the same alternative group already running);
- the **Path** where it was found, or an **Install…** button.

Select a row to see its details:

![Server details](docs/screenshots/language-servers-details.png)

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Description, licence, homepage | from the catalog |
| Command | the command line Forge starts |
| Executable | a custom path to the executable (`langservers.servers.<id>.path`); empty = detect automatically |
| Extra settings (JSON) | merged into the server's settings (`langservers.servers.<id>.settings`); put startup options under an `"initializationOptions"` key. **Show Defaults** shows what Forge sends by default. |
| Install | the ways to install it |

### Where Forge looks for servers

In this order: the project's `node_modules/.bin`, Forge's own server folder
(`<data dir>/forge/langservers/node_modules/.bin`, e.g.
`~/.local/share/forge/langservers` on Linux), the `PATH`, npm/nvm/volta/fnm global folders,
`~/.local/bin`, Composer's global `vendor/bin`, cargo, go, dotnet and gem folders, Neovim's
Mason (`~/.local/share/nvim/mason/bin`) and Windows `.cmd` shims. TypeScript SDKs and
`@vue/typescript-plugin` are also looked up in the project's and Forge's `node_modules`.

### Installing a server

**npm servers install with one click.** Their rows have an **Install** button; Forge downloads
everything itself, nothing else needs to be installed first:

1. **Node.js**: a `node` 18 or newer on the machine is used; otherwise Forge downloads the
   official Node.js LTS build from `langservers.download.nodeMirror`
   (default `https://nodejs.org/dist`), checks it against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt` and
   keeps it in `<data dir>/forge/runtimes/`.
2. **The package**: packages without dependencies (Intelephense) come straight from the npm
   registry (`langservers.download.npmRegistry`, default `https://registry.npmjs.org`) and are
   checked against the registry's sha512 integrity hash; others are installed with the npm that
   belongs to that Node.js, into Forge's server folder — never globally.
3. Servers in Forge's folder are started with Forge's Node.js, so no `node` on your `PATH` is
   needed.

Progress shows in the status bar ("Installing Intelephense: Downloading Node.js … 45%") and in
the row. Afterwards the server starts with the next matching file, without reopening the
project.

![Install buttons](docs/screenshots/language-servers-install-buttons.png)

Other servers keep **Install…**, which opens a dialog with the command and its output:

![Install dialog](docs/screenshots/language-servers-install-output.png)

- Other tools (`brew`, `pipx`, `go install`, `cargo install`, `dotnet tool`, `gem`,
  `composer global require`) run exactly as listed in the catalog, without a shell.
- Commands that need root (`apt`, `pacman`) are only shown with **Copy Command**; run them in a
  terminal.
- Download-only servers link to their release page; download them and set **Executable**.

The full list of servers, their commands and install options is in the
[language servers reference](docs/guide/reference/language-servers.md).

### Updates

Once a day Forge asks the npm registry whether the servers it installed have newer versions
(**Check for updates of servers installed by Forge once a day**, `langservers.updates.check`).
A balloon "Language server update available" offers **Update** / **Not now**; updating
restarts the server.

![Update offer](docs/screenshots/language-server-update-offer.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check for updates once a day | `langservers.updates.check` | on |
| npm registry | `langservers.download.npmRegistry` | `https://registry.npmjs.org` |
| Node.js download mirror | `langservers.download.nodeMirror` | `https://nodejs.org/dist` |

For development there is also a command-line installer (`pnpm langservers` in `app/ui`, binary
`forge-langservers`): `install [--accept-intelephense-licence] [package…]`, `updates`, `where`.

### Alternatives

Some servers are alternatives: only the first enabled and installed one starts.
`typescript-language-server` is preferred over `vtsls`; `basedpyright` over `pyright`.
Disable the preferred one to use the other.

### Servers that depend on the project

ESLint starts only with an ESLint config (`eslint.config.*`, `.eslintrc*`) or an `eslint`
dependency; Tailwind CSS only with `tailwind.config.*` or a Tailwind dependency; the Angular
Language Service only with `@angular/core`. Servers that belong to a plugin (TypeScript to
WebForge, Vue to `forge.vue`, Lua to `forge.lua`) start only while that plugin is active.

## Install suggestions in the editor

When a file uses something only a language server provides, and that server is not installed,
a banner above the editor offers it, for example for a JSON file with `"$schema"` or a YAML file
with a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=…` modeline: "The $schema of this file is not used: no
validation, completion or documentation from it."

- **Install…** opens the install dialog.
- **Not now** hides the banner until Forge restarts.
- **Don't show again** stores the server in `langservers.hints.dismissed`.

## Status bar

The language server widget shows "Indexing… TypeScript 45%" while a server reports progress,
otherwise the running servers and their state. Click it to open the Language Servers page.

## PHP: Intelephense and Phpactor

PHP servers are configured by the PHP pack, on Settings | Languages & Frameworks | **PHP**
(`php.lsp.server`):

| Choice | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Auto (default) | Intelephense if installed, else Phpactor |
| Intelephense | always Intelephense (shows where it was found, or "not found on PATH (npm i -g intelephense)") |
| phpactor | always Phpactor |
| None (built-in index only) | no language server; completion and diagnostics from a server are missing, Forge's index still gives structure, search, hover and Generate |

The server starts when a PHP project opens and restarts when these settings change. Its cache
goes to `<cache dir>/forge/intelephense`, never into your project.

### Installing Intelephense

Intelephense is never bundled with Forge (its licence forbids redistribution), but Forge
downloads it for you from the npm registry. When a local PHP project opens without it, a
balloon says "PHP language server Intelephense is not installed" with **Install**, **Not now**
and **Don't ask again**. The PHP settings page and the Language Servers page have an
**Install Intelephense** button as well.

![Install offer](docs/screenshots/intelephense-install-offer.png)

The first install asks you to accept the Intelephense licence (stored as
`php.intelephense.licenceAccepted`). Forge then installs it as described in
[Installing a server](#installing-a-server) (with Node.js if needed) and starts it right away.

![Installing](docs/screenshots/intelephense-install-progress.png)

| Option (Settings \| Languages & Frameworks \| PHP) | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When Intelephense is not installed: Ask when a PHP project opens, Install automatically, Do not install | `php.intelephense.autoInstall` | `ask` |
| I accept the Intelephense licence | `php.intelephense.licenceAccepted` | off |

You can still install it yourself (`npm install -g intelephense`); Forge finds it on the `PATH`.

### Intelephense licence key (premium)

Intelephense is free; a licence key from intelephense.com unlocks its premium features (rename,
code actions, type hierarchy and more). Forge never ships a key.

1. Open Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers (or the PHP page) and find
   **Intelephense: Free**.
2. Click **Enter Licence Key…**, paste your key and confirm with `Enter`.
3. The status changes to **Premium (key …1234)** and Intelephense restarts.

![Licence dialog](docs/screenshots/intelephense-licence-dialog.png)

The key is stored in the operating system's keychain (service `forge-lsp`, account
`intelephense`), never in a settings file, and is passed to the server as `licenceKey`. In free
mode no key is sent. **Change Licence Key…** replaces it; **Remove Licence** in the dialog
deletes it.

> **Note:** a key saved by an older Forge version in the setting `php.lsp.licenceKey` is moved
> to the keychain once.

## Lua

lua-language-server gets the APIs of LÖVE or Neovim depending on Settings | Languages &
Frameworks | Lua | **Lua environment**. See [LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md#lua-language-server).

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) language servers run on the remote host, next to
the files: the PHP server (the Forge agent finds Intelephense or Phpactor on the host) and the
catalog servers, whose project scan, detection (`node_modules/.bin`, `PATH`, npm/nvm/volta, …)
and configuration happen on the host too.

> **Note:** installing servers from the settings page is refused for remote projects; install
> them on the host from the terminal. The Intelephense install offer is shown for local projects
> only.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Not found" although it is installed**: Forge may have been started from a desktop launcher
  with a shorter `PATH` than your shell. Set **Executable** to the full path, or start Forge
  from a terminal.
- **A Node-based server fails to start**: servers you installed yourself need `node` on Forge's
  `PATH`; servers installed by Forge use Forge's Node.js.
- More in [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#language-server-not-found).
