---
title: Keymap
description: Forge's PHPStorm-compatible keymap - the default keymaps for Windows/Linux and macOS, changing shortcuts, chords and double taps, conflicts and focus contexts.
order: 240
tags: [keymap, shortcuts, phpstorm]
---

# Keymap

Forge ships **PHPStorm's default keymaps** 1:1, for Windows/Linux and for macOS, keyed by
PHPStorm's action ids. Shortcuts you know from PHPStorm work the same, and actions that Forge has
not implemented yet stay bound and show "*Action* is not available yet" instead of doing
something unexpected.

The complete list with both platforms is in the [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md); the
[shortcut pages](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md) explain them by topic and the
[reference card](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/reference-card.md) fits on one page.

## The most important shortcuts

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search Everywhere | `Double Shift` | `Double Shift` |
| Find Action | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | `Cmd+Shift+A` |
| Go to Class / File / Symbol | `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+Shift+N` / `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` | `Cmd+O` / `Cmd+Shift+O` / `Cmd+Alt+O` |
| Recent Files | `Ctrl+E` | `Cmd+E` |
| Go to Declaration | `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Click` | `Cmd+B`, `Cmd+Click` |
| Generate | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| Reformat Code | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` |
| Settings | `Ctrl+Alt+S` | `Cmd+,` |
| Commit | `Ctrl+K` | `Cmd+K` |
| Run / Debug | `Shift+F10` / `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+R` / `Ctrl+D` |
| Project / Terminal tool window | `Alt+1` / `Alt+F12` | `Cmd+1` / `Alt+F12` |
| New Scratch File | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+N` |
| Run Artisan Command (Laravel) | `Ctrl+Shift+X` | `Cmd+Shift+X` |

## Settings | Keymap

![Keymap settings](docs/screenshots/keymap-settings.png)

- **Keymap**: *Platform default* (`auto`), *Windows / Linux* or *macOS* (`keymap.active`). You
  can use the macOS keymap on Linux and vice versa.
- The tree groups actions like PHPStorm: Main Menu (File, Edit, View, Navigate, Code,
  Refactor, Run, Git, Window, …), Editor Actions, Debugger Actions, Other and Plugins.
  Changed actions are highlighted.
- **Search actions** filters by name; **Find Actions by Shortcut** (the keyboard icon) filters
  by pressing the keys.

### Changing a shortcut

Select an action and press `Enter`, double-click it or use **Edit Shortcuts**:

- **Add Keyboard Shortcut** opens a dialog: press the keys (**First stroke**), optionally a
  **Second stroke** for a chord such as `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`. The dialog lists conflicts ("The
  shortcut is already assigned to other actions") before you confirm; **Remove Others** takes
  the shortcut away from them.
- **Remove *shortcut*** removes one shortcut.
- **Reset Shortcuts** restores the defaults of the action; the page can also reset all changes.

![Conflict](docs/screenshots/keymap-shortcut-conflict.png)

Changes are stored in the settings (`keymap.overrides.default` / `keymap.overrides.macOS`, one
entry per action: the action id followed by its shortcuts, separated by tabs), so they live in
`settings.toml` and not in browser storage.

> **Note:** mouse shortcuts ("Add Mouse Shortcut") and importing PHPStorm keymap files are not
> available yet.

## How shortcuts are written

| Notation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Shift+A` | keys pressed together |
| `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C` | a chord: the first stroke, then the second |
| `Double Shift` | press `Shift` twice quickly |
| `Cmd`, `Opt`/`Alt` | macOS modifiers |

Shortcuts use the physical key position, so they work with any keyboard layout (on a German
keyboard `Ctrl+Z` is the key labelled Z).

## Focus contexts

The same keys can mean different things depending on what has focus: the **editor**, a text
**input**, a **tool window** (for example `Alt+Insert` adds a row in a database grid but opens
Generate in the editor), or the **terminal**. In the terminal, plain `Ctrl`+letter,
`Alt`+letter and `Escape` go to the shell; function keys, `Alt`+digit, `Ctrl+Shift` and
`Ctrl+Alt` combinations still reach the IDE.

## Plugin actions

Plugins add their own actions under **Plugins** (and some under Main Menu), for example:

| Action | Default shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Laravel: Run Artisan Command… | `Ctrl+Shift+X` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`) |
| Terminal: New Terminal Tab | `Ctrl+Shift+T` (macOS `Cmd+T`), in the terminal |
| Database: Execute | `Ctrl+Enter` (macOS `Cmd+Enter`), in a console |
| Database: Submit / Add Row / Delete Rows / Revert Selected | `Ctrl+Enter` / `Alt+Insert` / `Ctrl+Y` / `Ctrl+Alt+Z` in a data grid |
| Database: Jump to Query Console… | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` in the Database tool window |
| Symfony: Run Console Command…, Symfony Routes | none |
| Doctrine Entities, npm tool window, Reload npm Scripts | none |

All of them can be rebound like PHPStorm actions.

# Shortcuts by topic

Forge uses PHPStorm's default keymap. These pages explain every **implemented** action by topic:
its shortcut on Windows/Linux and macOS, what it does, where it also lives in the main menu, and a
screenshot when it opens something. Actions that are not implemented yet are listed in the
[keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) and shown disabled in the
[main menu](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md).

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Keymap reference card](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/reference-card.md) | the 60 most important shortcuts on one printable page |
| [General](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/general.md) | Find Action, Settings, the main menu, projects, scratches, themes |
| [Editing](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/editing.md) | completion, Generate, clipboard, lines, selection, comments, formatting, folding |
| [Navigation](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/navigation.md) | declarations, back/forward, lines, problems, Recent Files, editor tabs |
| [Search](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/search.md) | Search Everywhere, Go to Class/File/Symbol, find in file, Find in Files |
| [Refactoring](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/refactoring.md) | what exists today and what is not implemented yet |
| [Run and debug](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/run-debug.md) | run configurations, breakpoints, stepping with Xdebug, artisan and console |
| [Version control (Git)](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/vcs.md) | commit, push, update, branches, log, blame |
| [Tool windows](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/tool-windows.md) | opening, hiding, resizing and switching tool windows |

## Tips

- **Find Action** (`Ctrl+Shift+A`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) runs any action by name and shows its
  shortcut — the quickest way to learn them.
- In menus and popups the underlined letter (mnemonic) picks an entry.
- Shortcuts use the physical key position, so they work with any keyboard layout.
- Change any shortcut in Settings | Keymap; see [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md).

# Keymap reference card

The 60 shortcuts you need most, PHPStorm's default keymap. Print it or keep it open next to Forge. Every action is implemented; the [shortcut pages](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md) explain each one, the [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) lists all of them.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS | Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Search Everywhere | `Double Shift` | `Double Shift` | Select All Occurrences | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Cmd+G` |
| Find Action | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | `Cmd+Shift+A` | Join Lines | `Ctrl+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+J` |
| Go to Class | `Ctrl+N` | `Cmd+O` | Toggle Case | `Ctrl+Shift+U` | `Cmd+Shift+U` |
| Go to File | `Ctrl+Shift+N` | `Cmd+Shift+O` | Start New Line | `Shift+Enter` | `Shift+Enter` |
| Go to Symbol | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` | `Cmd+Alt+O` | Collapse | `Ctrl+-` | `Cmd+-` |
| Recent Files | `Ctrl+E` | `Cmd+E` | Expand | `Ctrl+=` | `Cmd+=` |
| Switcher | `Ctrl+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | Collapse All | `Ctrl+Shift+-` | `Cmd+Shift+-` |
| Find in Files | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `Cmd+Shift+F` | Save All | `Ctrl+S` | `Cmd+S` |
| Find in File | `Ctrl+F` | `Cmd+F` | Close Tab | `Ctrl+F4` | `Cmd+W` |
| Replace in File | `Ctrl+R` | `Cmd+R` | Select Next Tab | `Alt+Right` | `Ctrl+Right` |
| Find Next / Move to Next Occurrence | `F3` | `Cmd+G` | Terminal tool window | `Alt+F12` | `Alt+F12` |
| Go to Line/Column | `Ctrl+G` | `Cmd+L` | Settings | `Ctrl+Alt+S` | `Cmd+,` |
| Go to Declaration or Usages | `Ctrl+B` | `Cmd+B` | Hide Active Tool Window | `Shift+Escape` | `Shift+Escape` |
| Back | `Ctrl+Alt+Left` | `Cmd+[` | New Scratch File | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+N` |
| Forward | `Ctrl+Alt+Right` | `Cmd+]` | Run | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` |
| Next Highlighted Error | `F2` | `F2` | Debug | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` |
| Basic Completion | `Ctrl+Space` | `Ctrl+Space` | Run (choose configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` |
| Parameter Info | `Ctrl+P` | `Cmd+P` | Run Context Configuration | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Shift+R` |
| Generate | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` | Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Reformat Code | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` | Rerun | `Ctrl+F5` | `Cmd+R` |
| Comment with Line Comment | `Ctrl+/` | `Cmd+/` | Toggle Line Breakpoint | `Ctrl+F8` | `Cmd+F8` |
| Comment with Block Comment | `Ctrl+Shift+/` | `Cmd+Alt+/` | Step Over | `F8` | `F8` |
| Duplicate Line or Selection | `Ctrl+D` | `Cmd+D` | Step Into | `F7` | `F7` |
| Delete Line | `Ctrl+Y` | `Cmd+Backspace` | Step Out | `Shift+F8` | `Shift+F8` |
| Move Line Up | `Alt+Shift+Up` | `Alt+Shift+Up` | Resume Program | `F9` | `Cmd+Alt+R` |
| Move Line Down | `Alt+Shift+Down` | `Alt+Shift+Down` | Evaluate Expression | `Alt+F8` | `Alt+F8` |
| Move Statement Up | `Ctrl+Shift+Up` | `Cmd+Shift+Up` | Commit | `Ctrl+K` | `Cmd+K` |
| Extend Selection | `Ctrl+W` | `Alt+Up` | Push | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | `Cmd+Shift+K` |
| Shrink Selection | `Ctrl+Shift+W` | `Alt+Down` | Update Project | `Ctrl+T` | `Cmd+T` |
| Add Selection for Next Occurrence | `Alt+J` | `Ctrl+G` | Project tool window | `Alt+1` | `Cmd+1` |

Notation: `Double Shift` means pressing Shift twice quickly. On macOS, `Cmd` is ⌘ and `Alt` is ⌥ (Option).

| [Collapse Recursively](#collapse-recursively) | `Ctrl+Alt+-`, `Ctrl+Alt+NumPad-` | `Cmd+Alt+-`, `Cmd+Alt+NumPad-` |
| [Expand All](#expand-all) | `Ctrl+Shift+=`, `Ctrl+Shift+NumPad+` | `Cmd+Shift+=`, `Cmd+Shift+NumPad+` |
| [Collapse All](#collapse-all) | `Ctrl+Shift+-`, `Ctrl+Shift+NumPad-` | `Cmd+Shift+-`, `Cmd+Shift+NumPad-` |
| [Scroll Up](#scroll-up) | `Ctrl+Up` | — |
| [Scroll Down](#scroll-down) | `Ctrl+Down` | — |

## Basic Completion

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#code-completion)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate)

# Shortcuts: Navigation

Jumping to declarations, lines, problems, recent files and between editor tabs. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Go to Declaration or Usages](#go-to-declaration-or-usages) | `Ctrl+B` | `Cmd+B` |
| [Back](#back) | `Ctrl+Alt+Left` | `Cmd+[`, `Cmd+Alt+Left` |
| [Forward](#forward) | `Ctrl+Alt+Right` | `Cmd+]`, `Cmd+Alt+Right` |
| [Go to Line/Column](#go-to-linecolumn) | `Ctrl+G` | `Cmd+L` |
| [Move Caret to Matching Brace](#move-caret-to-matching-brace) | `Ctrl+Shift+M` | `Ctrl+M` |
| [Next Highlighted Error](#next-highlighted-error) | `F2` | `F2` |
| [Previous Highlighted Error](#previous-highlighted-error) | `Shift+F2` | `Shift+F2` |
| [Recent Files](#recent-files) | `Ctrl+E` | `Cmd+E` |
| [Recently Changed Files](#recently-changed-files) | — | — |
| [Switcher](#switcher) | `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` |
| [Select Next Tab](#select-next-tab) | `Alt+Right` | `Ctrl+Right`, `Cmd+Shift+]` |
| [Select Previous Tab](#select-previous-tab) | `Alt+Left` | `Ctrl+Left`, `Cmd+Shift+[` |
| [Close Tab](#close-tab) | `Ctrl+F4` | `Cmd+W` |
| [Close All Tabs](#close-all-tabs) | — | — |
| [Close Other Tabs](#close-other-tabs) | — | `Cmd+Alt+W` |
| [Close Unmodified Tabs](#close-unmodified-tabs) | — | — |
| [Reopen Closed Tab](#reopen-closed-tab) | — | — |

## Go to Declaration or Usages

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+B` · macOS `Cmd+B` · action id `GotoDeclaration`

Jumps to the declaration of the symbol at the caret; several targets open the Choose Declaration popup.

**Menu:** Navigate | Declaration or Usages

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Back

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Left` · macOS `Cmd+[`, `Cmd+Alt+Left` · action id `Back`

Goes back to the previous caret location in your navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Back

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Forward

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Right` · macOS `Cmd+]`, `Cmd+Alt+Right` · action id `Forward`

Goes forward in the navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Forward

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Go to Line/Column

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+G` · macOS `Cmd+L` · action id `GotoLine`

Moves the caret to a line (and column) of the current file.

**Menu:** Navigate | Line/Column…

![Go to Line/Column](docs/screenshots/docs-goto-line.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions)

## Move Caret to Matching Brace

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+M` · macOS `Ctrl+M` · action id `EditorMatchBrace`

Moves the caret to the matching bracket.

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions)

## Next Highlighted Error

**Shortcut:** `F2` · macOS `F2` · action id `GotoNextError`

Moves the caret to the next problem in the file.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Highlighted Error

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#problems)

## Previous Highlighted Error

**Shortcut:** `Shift+F2` · macOS `Shift+F2` · action id `GotoPreviousError`

Moves the caret to the previous problem in the file.

**Menu:** Navigate | Previous Highlighted Error

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#problems)

## Recent Files

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+E` · macOS `Cmd+E` · action id `RecentFiles`

Lists recently opened files and the tool windows; press again for recently edited files only.

**Menu:** View | Recent Files

![Recent Files](docs/screenshots/docs-recent-files.png)

More: [Workbench and tool windows](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Recently Changed Files

**Shortcut:** — · macOS — · action id `RecentChangedFiles`

Lists recently edited files.

**Menu:** View | Recently Changed Files

More: [Workbench and tool windows](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Switcher

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` · macOS `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` · action id `Switcher`

Switches between open files and tool windows while `Ctrl` is held.

![Switcher](docs/screenshots/docs-switcher.png)

**Menu:** Window | Editor Tabs | Select Previous Tab

**Menu:** Window | Editor Tabs | Close Tab

More: [Workbench and tool windows](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs)

## Close All Tabs

**Shortcut:** — · macOS — · action id `CloseAllEditors`

# Shortcuts: Search

Search Everywhere, Go to Class/File/Symbol, find in the current file and Find in Files. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Search Everywhere](#search-everywhere) | `Double Shift` | `Double Shift` |
| [Go to Class](#go-to-class) | `Ctrl+N` | `Cmd+O` |
| [Go to File](#go-to-file) | `Ctrl+Shift+N` | `Cmd+Shift+O` |
| [Go to Symbol](#go-to-symbol) | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` | `Cmd+Alt+O` |
| [Find Action](#find-action) | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | `Cmd+Shift+A` |
| [Find in File](#find-in-file) | `Ctrl+F` | `Cmd+F` |
| [Replace in File](#replace-in-file) | `Ctrl+R` | `Cmd+R` |
| [Find Next / Move to Next Occurrence](#find-next--move-to-next-occurrence) | `F3` | `Cmd+G` |
| [Find Previous / Move to Previous Occurrence](#find-previous--move-to-previous-occurrence) | `Shift+F3` | `Cmd+Shift+G` |
| [Find in Files…](#find-in-files) | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `Cmd+Shift+F` |

## Search Everywhere

**Shortcut:** `Double Shift` · macOS `Double Shift` · action id `SearchEverywhere`

Searches classes, files, symbols, actions and text in one popup.

**Menu:** Navigate | Search Everywhere

![Search Everywhere](docs/screenshots/docs-search-everywhere.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md)

## Go to Class

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+N` · macOS `Cmd+O` · action id `GotoClass`

Finds a class, interface, trait or enum by name (camel humps work).

**Menu:** Navigate | Class…

![Go to Class](docs/screenshots/docs-goto-class.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md)

## Go to File

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+N` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+O` · action id `GotoFile`

Finds a project file by name or path.

**Menu:** Navigate | File…

![Go to File](docs/screenshots/docs-goto-file.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md)

## Go to Symbol

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+O` · action id `GotoSymbol`

Finds a function, method, property or constant by name.

**Menu:** Navigate | Symbol…

![Go to Symbol](docs/screenshots/docs-goto-symbol.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md)

## Find Action

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+A` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+A` · action id `GotoAction`

Finds any action by name and runs it (Find Action).

**Menu:** Navigate | Action…; Help | Find Action…

![Find Action](docs/screenshots/docs-find-action.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-action)

## Find in File

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+F` · macOS `Cmd+F` · action id `Find`

Opens the find panel of the editor for the current file.

**Menu:** Edit | Find | Find…

![Find in File](docs/screenshots/docs-find-in-file.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file)

## Replace in File

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+R` · macOS `Cmd+R` · action id `Replace`

Opens the find panel with the replace field.

**Menu:** Edit | Find | Replace…

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file)

## Find Next / Move to Next Occurrence

**Shortcut:** `F3` · macOS `Cmd+G` · action id `FindNext`

Moves to the next match of the current search.

**Menu:** Edit | Find | Find Next / Move to Next Occurrence

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file)

## Find Previous / Move to Previous Occurrence

**Shortcut:** `Shift+F3` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+G` · action id `FindPrevious`

Moves to the previous match.

**Menu:** Edit | Find | Find Previous / Move to Previous Occurrence

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file)

## Find in Files

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+F` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+F` · action id `FindInPath`

Searches the text of all project files, with match case, whole words, regular expressions, file masks and a folder scope.

**Menu:** Edit | Find | Find in Files…

![Find in Files…](docs/screenshots/docs-find-in-files.png)

More: [Search Everywhere and Find Action](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files)

# Shortcuts: Refactoring

Refactorings and code generation. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

> **Note:** the refactorings of PHPStorm's Refactor menu (Rename `Shift+F6`, Change Signature
> `Ctrl+F6`, Extract/Introduce Variable, Constant, Field, Parameter and Method, Inline, Move,
> Copy File, Safe Delete, Pull Members Up / Push Members Down) are not implemented yet. Their
> shortcuts stay reserved and show "*Action* is not available yet"; see the
> [Refactor menu](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/refactor.md). Renaming files and folders works from
> the Project view's context menu. The actions below are the code transformations Forge has
> today.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Generate…](#generate) | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| [Reformat Code](#reformat-code) | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` |

## Generate

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Insert` · macOS `Cmd+N` · action id `Generate`

In PHP files: generates a constructor, getters, setters, overrides, `__toString()` or a PHPDoc block.

**Menu:** Code | Generate…

![Generate…](docs/screenshots/docs-generate.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate)

## Reformat Code

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+L` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+L` · action id `ReformatCode`

Formats the file with the language server's formatter (StyLua for Lua).

**Menu:** Code | Reformat Code

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#reformat-code)

# Shortcuts: Run and debug

Running configurations, breakpoints and stepping through PHP code with Xdebug. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Run](#run) | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` |
| [Debug](#debug) | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` |
| [Run… (choose configuration)](#run-choose-configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` |

---
title: Settings and themes
description: The Settings dialog, user and project settings, settings files, themes (Forge Ember, Forge Anvil, Solarized), fonts and the window title bar styles.
order: 230
tags: [settings, themes, appearance, window controls, fonts]
---

# Settings and themes

## The Settings dialog

**Settings** (`Ctrl+Alt+S`, macOS `Cmd+,`, or the gear in the main toolbar) opens the Settings
dialog, with the same tree as PHPStorm:

- **Appearance & Behavior**: Appearance, System Settings
- **Keymap**
- **Editor**: General, Font, Code Style (PHP), Inlay Hints
- **Plugins**
- **Version Control**: Git, GitLab, Forgejo / Gitea, GitHub
- **Languages & Frameworks**: Language Servers, PHP (Composer, Debug, Servers, Laravel,
  Symfony, Doctrine), Node.js, TypeScript, Lua, Template Data Languages
- **Tools**: Terminal, Database, AI Agents, AI Providers, Browser Companion, HTTP Client, SSH Configurations
- **Build, Execution, Deployment**: Docker (Docker Registry), Kubernetes

![Settings dialog](docs/screenshots/settings-light.png)

- **Search settings** at the top filters the tree and highlights matching options on every
  page, also by keywords ("theme", "autosave", "interpreter").
- **OK** applies and closes, **Apply** applies and keeps the dialog open, **Cancel** discards.
- Invalid values (out of range, wrong type) are flagged right away and not saved.
- In the desktop app the dialog is its own window; its size and position are remembered.

![Search in settings](docs/screenshots/settings-search.png)

Every option, its key, type and default is listed in the
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

## User and project settings

Settings come in three layers; a later one wins:

1. built-in defaults (declared by the plugins),
2. **user** settings: `<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`,
3. **project** settings: `<project>/.forge/settings.toml`.

Pages with options that can be stored per project show **For current project** in the header;
those options are saved to the project's file, which you can commit to share them with your
team (for example the PHP language level or the Symfony environment).

### Settings files

The files are TOML with dotted keys as nested tables. You can edit them by hand; Forge picks up
changes on the next start:

```toml
# ~/.config/forge/settings.toml
[appearance]
theme = "light"
windowControls = "gnome"

[editor.font]
family = "Fira Code"
size = 14

[vcs.hosts]
refreshSeconds = 300
```

Some options have no page in the dialog and can only be set this way, such as
`vcs.hosts.statusBarPipeline` and `vcs.hosts.refreshSeconds`.

Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, licence keys) never go into these files; they are stored
in the operating system keychain.

## Themes

Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Theme** (`appearance.theme`):

| Theme | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Forge Ember (Dark) | `dark` (default) |
| Forge Anvil (Light) | `light` |
| Solarized Dark | `solarized-dark` |
| Solarized Light | `solarized-light` |

The sun/moon button in the main toolbar, **Theme: Toggle Dark/Light** and **Quick Switch
Scheme…** (`` Ctrl+` ``) toggle between dark and light.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![Ember](docs/screenshots/workbench-dark.png) | ![Anvil](docs/screenshots/workbench-light.png) |

## Appearance options

![Appearance](docs/screenshots/settings-appearance.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI font (Inter, System default, Segoe UI, Roboto) | `appearance.uiFont.family` | Inter |
| UI font size (10–20) | `appearance.uiFont.size` | 13 |
| Compact mode | `appearance.compactMode` | off |
| Main menu (Hamburger menu, Merged with main toolbar, Show in separate toolbar) — see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu) | `appearance.mainMenu` | Hamburger menu |
| Window controls | `appearance.windowControls` | Match the system |
| Show tool window bars | `appearance.showToolWindowBars` | on |
| Open files with single click (Project view) | `projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick` | on |

Editor fonts are under Settings | Editor | Font: JetBrains Mono (default), Fira Code, Cascadia
Code, Source Code Pro, Menlo, Consolas or the system monospace font, size (13.5), line height
(1.6) and ligatures.

### Window controls

Forge draws its own title bars. **Window controls** chooses how their buttons look:

| Value | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` — Match the system | detected from the OS and desktop (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `KDE_FULL_SESSION`, …), including the button order of GNOME (`button-layout`) and KDE (`kwinrc`) |
| `windows` | Windows 11 buttons on the right |
| `macos` | traffic lights on the left |
| `gnome` | GNOME/Adwaita round buttons |
| `kde` | KDE Plasma (Breeze) buttons |
| `linux` | generic Linux buttons |
| `native` | the operating system draws the title bar (Forge's toolbar is then below it) |

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Windows](docs/screenshots/titlebar-windows.png) | ![macOS](docs/screenshots/titlebar-macos.png) | ![GNOME](docs/screenshots/titlebar-gnome.png) |
| ![KDE](docs/screenshots/titlebar-kde.png) | ![Linux](docs/screenshots/titlebar-linux.png) | ![GNOME light](docs/screenshots/titlebar-gnome-light.png) |

Large dialogs (Settings, Run/Debug Configurations, New Project, New SSH Connection, Data
Sources and Drivers) open as their own windows with the same style:

![Settings window on KDE](docs/screenshots/settings-window-kde.png)

## Not applied yet

These options are shown in Settings but have no effect on this version: Show tool window
numbers, Smooth scrolling (Appearance), everything under System Settings except **Default
project directory** (reopen projects on startup, confirm exit, open project in, autosave,
synchronize external changes), caret blink period, remove trailing spaces on save, ensure line
break at end of file, Code Style, Inlay Hints, the Git page, the Composer page except the
composer path, console cycle buffer size, terminal audible bell and shell integration. The
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md) marks each of them.

---
title: Plugins and packs
description: How Forge is split into packs and plugins, which plugins exist, when they activate, and how to enable or disable them in Settings | Plugins.
order: 250
tags: [plugins, packs, phpforge, webforge, luaforge]
---

# Plugins and packs

Everything in Forge beyond the workbench is a **plugin**. Plugins are grouped in **packs**:

| Pack | Plugins |
| --- | --- |
| **Core** | Forge Platform (required), Git, GitLab/Forgejo/GitHub, Terminal, Run/Debug, Database Tools and SQL, Docker and Kubernetes, Language Servers, AI Assistant, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Browser Companion |
| **PHPForge** | PHP, Composer, PHPUnit, Xdebug, Laravel, Symfony, Symfony Services, Doctrine |
| **WebForge** | HTML, CSS & JavaScript, React, Vue.js, Angular |
| **LuaForge** | Lua |
| **ScriptForge** / **ConfigForge** | Bash, Python / YAML, JSON, .env, Ignore Files, Docker files, Postfix, E-Mail, INI, Config Files |

All plugins are built in; there is no separate download.

## When plugins are active

A plugin is active when it is **enabled** and the open project **uses** it. Plugins may declare
project types (a language, framework, pack or tool id); without project types they are always
active. For example Laravel needs `laravel`, PHPUnit needs `phpunit` or `pest`, React needs
`react` or `next`. See [Project type detection](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md) and
the full list in [Reference: plugins](docs/guide/reference/plugins.md).

Inactive plugins hide their tool windows, status bar widgets and editor features, and their file
types fall back to the bundled ones (in a non-Symfony project `config/services.yaml` is plain
YAML).

## Settings | Plugins

![Plugins](docs/screenshots/settings-plugins.png)

The **Installed** tab lists all plugins grouped by pack, with a search field and a details pane
(description, version, vendor, dependencies). The checkbox enables or disables a plugin;
**Forge Platform** is required and cannot be disabled. Dependent plugins follow: disabling PHP
also disables Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine, Composer, PHPUnit and Xdebug.

Disabled plugins are remembered in the user settings (`plugins.disabled`, a list of plugin ids).

> **Note:** the **Marketplace** tab is not available yet, and third-party plugins cannot be
> installed. New integrations are added to Forge itself; see
> [Writing a plugin or pack](docs/guide/developer/plugins-and-packs.md).

Source: docs/guide/user/php.md

---
title: PHP
description: PHP support in PHPForge - the PHP index, Structure tool window, hover documentation, class and symbol search, Generate (Alt+Insert) for constructors, getters and setters, and the PHP settings.
order: 60
tags: [php, phpforge, generate, structure, index]
---

# PHP

PHP support is the **PHPForge** pack (plugin `forge.php`). It combines two engines:

- **Forge's PHP index**, built with tree-sitter in Rust: classes, interfaces, traits, enums,
  functions, constants, members, PHPDoc and attributes of every PHP file in the project. It
  powers the Structure tool window, Go to Class/Symbol, index-based hover and the Generate
  actions, and works without any language server.
- **A PHP language server**, Intelephense or Phpactor, for completion, diagnostics,
  Go to Declaration, hover and formatting. See
  [Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md#php-intelephense-and-phpactor).

The pack activates in projects with a `composer.json` or `.php` files.

## The PHP index

Indexing starts when a PHP project opens. The status bar shows **Indexing… 45%** with a
progress bar; afterwards the index follows file changes on its own.

- Files in `vendor/` are not indexed up front. When a class from a dependency is needed (as an
  ancestor, in hover), Forge loads it on demand through Composer's PSR-4 autoload map.
- The index is cached in `<cache dir>/forge/php-index/` (keyed by the project path), so the
  next start only re-reads changed files. Nothing is written into the project.
- **Reindex PHP Files** (Find Action) rebuilds it.
- Extra library folders can be added under Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP |
  **Include Path** (`php.includePaths`); they are also passed to the language server.

## Structure

The **Structure** tool window (`Alt+7`, macOS `Cmd+7`) lists the classes of the active file
with their constants, properties and methods, including signatures and visibility. Click an
entry to jump to it.

- **Show Inherited** adds members of parent classes, traits and interfaces, grayed and with
  the declaring class.
- **Sort Alphabetically** sorts within each kind.

![Structure tool window](docs/screenshots/php-structure.png)

![Inherited members](docs/screenshots/php-structure-inherited.png)

## Go to Class and Go to Symbol

**Go to Class** (`Ctrl+N`, macOS `Cmd+O`) and **Go to Symbol** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N`, macOS
`Cmd+Alt+O`) search the PHP index with camel-hump matching: `OrCo` finds
`OrderController`, `OrderController::sto` finds its `store` method. See
[Search Everywhere](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md).

## Hover documentation

Hovering a class, function, method, property or constant shows its signature, attributes
(for example `#[Route('/orders', name: 'orders')]`) and its PHPDoc (description, `@param`,
`@return`, `@throws`, `@deprecated`, links) as a PHPStorm-style popup. The language server's
answer is merged with the index; when no server runs, or it has nothing for a symbol, the
index answers alone.

![PHP hover](docs/screenshots/php-hover.png)

![Hover from the index](docs/screenshots/php-hover-index-fallback.png)

## Generate

**Generate…** (`Alt+Insert`, macOS `Cmd+N`) in a PHP file opens a popup at the caret with
what can be generated there:

| Entry | Generates |
| --- | --- |
| Constructor | a constructor with a parameter per chosen field that assigns it (`$this->x = $x`) |
| Getters | `getX()` / `isX()` for booleans |
| Setters | `setX()`; tick **Fluent setters** to return `$this` (`: static`) |
| Getters and Setters | both |
| Override Methods… (`Ctrl+O`) | stubs for inherited methods that are not overridden yet |
| Implement Methods… (`Ctrl+I`) | stubs for abstract and interface methods |
| toString() | a `__toString()` method |
| PHPDoc Comment | a PHPDoc block for the function, method or property at the caret, with `@param`, `@return` and `@throws` |

![Generate popup](docs/screenshots/php-generate-popup.png)

Entries that do not apply are disabled (for example Constructor when the class already has
one). Type the underlined letter to pick an entry. For fields and methods a chooser dialog
opens ("Choose Fields to Generate Getters and Setters", "Select Methods to Override") with
**Select All** / **Select None**:

![Choose fields](docs/screenshots/php-generate-chooser.png)

The generated code follows the class's indentation, inserts properties after the last
property and methods at the end of the class, and adds the `use` imports that inherited
signatures need.

![Generated getters and setters](docs/screenshots/php-generate-result.png)

`Ctrl+O` and `Ctrl+I` work directly in PHP editors as shortcuts for Override/Implement
Methods.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP

![PHP settings](docs/screenshots/settings-php.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP language level (7.4 – 8.4) | `php.languageLevel` | 8.3 |
| CLI Interpreter (path to `php`) | `php.interpreter` | `php` |
| Language server (Auto, Intelephense, phpactor, None) | `php.lsp.server` | Auto |
| Max indexed file size for the server (KB) | `php.lsp.maxFileSize` | 5000 |
| When Intelephense is not installed (`ask`, `always`, `never`), see [Installing Intelephense](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md#installing-intelephense) | `php.intelephense.autoInstall` | `ask` |
| I accept the Intelephense licence | `php.intelephense.licenceAccepted` | off |
| Include Path | `php.includePaths` | empty |

The language level and the interpreter can be stored per project ("For current project" in
the page header). The status bar shows the language level ("PHP 8.3"); click it to open this
page. The page also shows the [Intelephense licence](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md#intelephense-licence-key-premium).

Sub-pages: **Composer**, **Debug**, **Servers** (see [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md)),
**Laravel**, **Symfony**, **Doctrine**.

### Composer

Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Composer:

| Option | Setting | Default | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Path to composer | `php.composer.executable` | `composer` | used by Composer run configurations |
| Path to composer.json | `php.composer.json` | `composer.json` | not applied yet |
| Synchronize IDE settings with composer.json | `php.composer.syncWithComposerJson` | on | not applied yet |
| Add packages as libraries | `php.composer.addPackagesAsLibraries` | on | not applied yet |
| Check for package updates on project open | `php.composer.checkUpdates` | off | not applied yet |

Run Composer scripts with a **Composer Script** run configuration, see
[Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md).

### Code style

Settings | Editor | Code Style | PHP lists tabs and indents, brace placement and blank lines.

> **Note:** these options are not applied yet. Reformat Code uses the language server's
> formatter with its own defaults.

## Running and testing PHP

- **PHP Script** run configurations run a file with the CLI interpreter.
- **PHPUnit** configurations run a class, method, directory or `phpunit.xml`; test classes
  and methods get ▶ icons in the gutter and results appear as a test tree.
- **PHP scratch files** run with the project's autoloader.

See [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md), [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md) and
[Scratches](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md).

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the PHP index and the language server run on the
remote host through the Forge agent; Structure, search, hover and Generate work as locally.

---
title: Laravel
description: Laravel support in PHPForge - Blade, completion and navigation for routes, views, config, env, translations and Eloquent, gutter icons, the Routes tool window and Run Artisan Command.

# Laravel

The Laravel plugin (`forge.laravel`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`laravel/framework` or have an `artisan` file. It analyses the project statically in Rust (no
need to boot the application) and reloads when files change.

The status bar shows **Laravel 12** (the installed version); its tooltip counts routes, models,
views, components and config keys. Click it to open Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP |
Laravel.

## Blade

`*.blade.php` files are highlighted as Blade: HTML with echoes (`{{ }}`, `{!! !!}`), comments
(`{{-- --}}`), directives (`@foreach (...)`), `@php` blocks, components (`<x-alert :type="$t">`,
`<livewire:counter>`) and embedded `<script>`/`<style>`. PHP inside is highlighted as PHP.

![Blade](docs/screenshots/laravel-blade.png)

- Directives are completed, including the closing directive (`@foreach` … `@endforeach`).
- Custom directives registered with `Blade::directive()` or `Blade::if()` in the project are
  highlighted and completed like built-in ones. Add others in Settings | … | Laravel |
  **Additional Blade directives** (`laravel.blade.customDirectives`, names without `@`).

![Blade directives](docs/screenshots/laravel-blade-directives.png)

## Completion and Go to Declaration

In PHP and Blade files, Laravel completion appears next to the language server's, and
`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` tries Laravel targets first:

| Where | Completes | Ctrl+B goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `route('…')`, `to_route('…')` | route names | the route definition |
| `view('…')`, `@include('…')`, `@extends`, `View::make` | view names | the Blade file |
| `<x-…>` tags | Blade components (anonymous, class-based, Livewire) | the component |
| `config('…')` | config keys from `config/*.php` | the key in the config file |
| `env('…')` | keys from `.env` | the line in `.env` |
| `__('…')`, `trans('…')`, `@lang` | translation keys (PHP and JSON language files) | the translation |
| `->where('…')`, `orderBy`, `pluck` and other query builder calls | database columns, read from the migrations | the migration |
| `with('…')`, `load('…')` | Eloquent relations | the relation method |
| `$model->…` | model attributes (columns, `$fillable`, casts, accessors) and relations | the declaration |
| `Model::…` | local scopes | the `scope…` method |
| `[Controller::class, '…']` | controller methods | the method |
| custom Blade directives | | the `Blade::directive` call |

![Route completion](docs/screenshots/laravel-route-completion.png)

![Column completion](docs/screenshots/laravel-column-completion.png)

When a name has several targets (a view in two places, a component with a class and a
template), a **Choose Declaration** popup lists them.

![Go to view](docs/screenshots/laravel-goto-view.png)

Turn completion off with **Complete routes, views, config, translations and model attributes**
(`laravel.completion.enabled`) and **Complete database columns in query builder calls**
(`laravel.completion.columns`).

## Gutter icons

- **Route** icons next to controller actions that a route points to; click to go to the
  route definition (`laravel.gutter.routes`).
- **View** icons next to `view()` calls and Blade includes; click to open the template
  (`laravel.gutter.views`).

![Laravel gutter icons](docs/screenshots/laravel-gutter.png)

## Routes tool window

The **Routes** tool window (bottom) lists every route with **Method**, **URI**, **Name**,
**Action** and **Middleware**.

![Routes](docs/screenshots/laravel-routes.png)

- Type in the search field to filter by URI, name, action or middleware; `Up`/`Down` and
  `Enter` work in the list.
- Clicking a row opens the controller method (or the route definition for closures); the
  arrow button at the end of a row opens the route definition.
- **Refresh Routes** re-reads them.

Routes come from one of two sources, chosen with **Read routes from**
(`laravel.routes.source`, can be stored per project):

| Value | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | `php artisan route:list --json` when a `vendor/` folder exists, else static analysis |
| `artisan` | always `php artisan route:list --json`; also sees routes registered by packages, but needs a bootable application |
| `static` | Forge reads `routes/*.php` itself: verbs, `match`, `view`, `redirect`, `resource`/`apiResource`, groups with prefix/name/middleware/controller, included files and the `api` prefix |

With artisan, the source locations from static analysis are kept so navigation still works.

## Run Artisan Command

**Run Artisan Command…** (`Ctrl+Shift+X`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`) opens a popup listing the
project's artisan commands (from `php artisan list --format=json`, or a built-in list when the
application cannot boot) and your **Recently run** commands. Type a command with its
arguments and press `Enter`.

![Run Artisan Command](docs/screenshots/laravel-artisan.png)

The output appears in the popup; **Rerun** runs it again, `Enter` starts another command,
`Esc` closes.

![Artisan output](docs/screenshots/laravel-artisan-output.png)

For commands you run often, create an **Artisan** run configuration (Run | Edit
Configurations), which can also be debugged with Xdebug. See
[Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md).

## Database

Laravel's `DB_*` variables in `.env` are offered as a data source in the Database tool window.
See [Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md).

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Laravel

![Laravel settings](docs/screenshots/laravel-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read routes from | `laravel.routes.source` | `auto` |
| Complete routes, views, config, translations and model attributes | `laravel.completion.enabled` | on |
| Complete database columns in query builder calls | `laravel.completion.columns` | on |
| Show route icons for controller actions | `laravel.gutter.routes` | on |
| Show view icons for `view()` calls and Blade includes | `laravel.gutter.views` | on |
| Additional Blade directives | `laravel.blade.customDirectives` | empty |

## Remote projects

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the analysis runs in the Forge agent on the host
(completion, navigation and gutter icons cost one round trip), and artisan commands run on the
host.

![Laravel routes in a remote project](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-laravel-routes.png)

---
title: Symfony
description: Symfony support in PHPForge - services and parameters, routes, Twig completion and navigation, console commands, line markers, the Symfony tool window and settings.
order: 80

---

# Symfony

The Symfony plugin (`forge.symfony`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`symfony/framework-bundle` or have `bin/console` together with `config/bundles.php`. It reads
the project statically and, when present, the compiled container in
`var/cache/<env>/*Container.xml`, which also knows the services and parameters of every bundle.

The status bar shows **Symfony 7.2 · dev** (version and kernel environment). Its menu has
**Show Routes**, **Show Services**, **Run Console Command…**, **Refresh Symfony Index** and
**Symfony Settings…**.

![Symfony status menu](docs/screenshots/symfony-status-menu.png)

## What Forge knows about the project

| Area | Read from |
| --- | --- |
| Services, aliases, `_defaults`, autowired `resource:` folders | `config/services*.yaml`, merged with the compiled container XML |
| Parameters | the same files |
| Routes | `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and YAML route files |
| Templates | `templates/` (setting `symfony.templatesDirectory`), and which controller renders which template |
| Twig tags, filters, functions and tests | Twig core, the Symfony bridge and the project's Twig extensions |
| Console commands | the project's commands (`src/`), then framework and bundle commands |

The index is cached for a few seconds and rebuilt when files change; **Refresh Symfony Index**
rescans now.

## Completion and Go to Declaration

| Where | Completes and navigates to |
| --- | --- |
| `generateUrl('…')`, `redirectToRoute('…')`, `$router->generate('…')`, Twig `path('…')` / `url('…')` | route names |
| `render('…')`, `renderView`, Twig `{% extends %}`, `{% include %}`, `{% embed %}`, `{% import %}`, `{% from %}`, `{% use %}` | templates |
| `@service_id` in YAML, `#[Autowire(service: '…')]`, `$container->get('…')`, `service('…')` in PHP config | service ids |
| `%parameter%` in YAML, `getParameter('…')` | parameters |
| Twig files | tags, filters, functions, tests and variables |

![Twig completion](docs/screenshots/symfony-twig-completion.png)

![Twig filters](docs/screenshots/symfony-twig-filters.png)

`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` on any of these opens the declaration (the controller action, the
template, the service definition or class, the parameter).

In `config/services*.yaml` (file type "Symfony Services"), service ids, parameters and tags are
completed, and `@service` and `%parameter%` references are highlighted.

## Line markers

With **Show line markers for routes, templates and commands** (`symfony.gutterIcons`):

- a **route** marker on controller actions (click: the route);
- **go to template** next to `render()` calls;
- **rendered by** on Twig templates (click: the controller);
- a **run** marker on console commands (click: run it).

## Symfony tool window

The **Symfony** tool window (bottom) has three tabs:

| Tab | Columns | Filter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routes | Name, Method, Path, Controller | name, path or controller |
| Services | Service ID, Class, Tags (public/private icon) | id, class or tag |
| Parameters | Name, Value | parameter |

Clicking a row opens its definition.

![Symfony routes](docs/screenshots/symfony-routes.png)

![Symfony services](docs/screenshots/symfony-services.png)

## Run Console Command

**Run Console Command…** (Find Action, the status bar menu or the tool window) opens a popup:
type a command name, `Tab` completes it, arguments after the name are passed on, `Enter` runs
it with `bin/console` (setting `symfony.consolePath`) in the configured environment.

![Console command](docs/screenshots/symfony-console.png)

The output is shown in the Symfony tool window with **Rerun** and **Close**.

![Console output](docs/screenshots/symfony-console-run.png)

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Symfony

![Symfony settings](docs/screenshots/symfony-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment (`dev`, `test`, `prod`) — kernel environment for the compiled container and console commands | `symfony.environment` | `dev` |
| App directory — scanned for controllers, commands and Twig extensions | `symfony.appDirectory` | `src` |
| Templates directory | `symfony.templatesDirectory` | `templates` |
| Console — path to the console script | `symfony.consolePath` | `bin/console` |
| Container XML — empty: `var/cache/<environment>/*Container.xml` | `symfony.containerXml` | empty |
| Show line markers for routes, templates and commands | `symfony.gutterIcons` | on |
| Complete Twig tags, filters and functions | `symfony.twigCompletion` | on |

The project settings (environment, folders, console, container) can be stored per project.

## Doctrine

Symfony projects usually use Doctrine; see [Doctrine and DQL](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md). Symfony's
`DATABASE_URL` in `.env` is offered as a data source in the [Database](docs/guide/user/database.md) tool window.

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the analysis runs in the Forge agent on the host and
console commands run there as well.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/doctrine.md

---
title: Doctrine and DQL
description: Doctrine ORM support - entity mappings from attributes, annotations, XML and YAML, the Doctrine tool window, and DQL highlighting, completion, navigation and inspections in PHP strings.
order: 90
tags: [doctrine, dql, orm, entities, phpforge]
---

# Doctrine and DQL

The Doctrine plugin (`forge.doctrine`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`doctrine/orm`, with or without Symfony.

## Entity mappings

Forge reads entity mappings from:

- PHP 8 attributes (`#[ORM\Entity]`, `#[ORM\Column]`, `#[ORM\ManyToOne]`, …),
- legacy docblock annotations (`@ORM\Entity`, `@ORM\Column`, …) when a class has no mapping
  attributes (setting **Read legacy @ORM annotations**, `doctrine.annotations`),
- XML (`*.orm.xml`) and YAML (`*.orm.yml`) mapping files,

including embeddables, mapped superclasses, fields with type, column, length, nullable,
unique, id and generated flags, and associations (`ManyToOne`, `OneToMany`, `ManyToMany`,
`OneToOne`) with `mappedBy`/`inversedBy`. Repositories are linked to their entity.

## Doctrine tool window

The **Doctrine** tool window (right stripe) lists every entity with its table, fields and
associations. Filter by entity or field name; click an entry to open its declaration;
**Refresh** re-reads the mappings (also **Refresh Doctrine Entities** in Find Action).

![Doctrine entities](docs/screenshots/doctrine-entities.png)

## DQL in PHP strings

DQL is recognized inside:

- `createQuery('…')`, including concatenated strings, heredocs and `Entity::class`
  interpolation;
- QueryBuilder calls such as `select`, `from`, `join`/`leftJoin`/`innerJoin`, `where`/`andWhere`/
  `orWhere`, `orderBy`, `groupBy`, `having`, and `expr()` fragments, with the aliases that the
  builder chain declares (`createQueryBuilder('o')`, `join('o.customer', 'c')`).

There it provides:

| Feature | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| DQL highlighting of keywords, entities, aliases, fields, parameters | `doctrine.dqlInjection` |
| Completion of entities, aliases, fields, associations, embedded fields, keywords and functions | `doctrine.dqlCompletion` |
| Warnings for unknown entities and fields | `doctrine.dqlInspections` |
| `Ctrl+B` on an entity, alias or field opens its mapping | — |

![DQL completion in a QueryBuilder chain](docs/screenshots/symfony-dql-querybuilder.png)

![DQL completion in createQuery](docs/screenshots/symfony-dql-completion.png)

The highlighting is computed in the background shortly after each edit, so it may lag a
keystroke behind while you type.

## Line markers

Entities and repositories get gutter icons that link them: entity → repository and
repository → entity.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Doctrine

![Doctrine settings](docs/screenshots/doctrine-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity source directories — scanned for `#[ORM\Entity]` classes and repositories | `doctrine.sourceDirectories` | `src` |
| Mapping file directories — `*.orm.xml` and `*.orm.yml` | `doctrine.mappingDirectories` | `config/doctrine`, `src/Resources/config/doctrine` |
| Read legacy @ORM annotations | `doctrine.annotations` | on |
| Highlight DQL in createQuery() and QueryBuilder strings | `doctrine.dqlInjection` | on |
| Complete entities, aliases and fields in DQL | `doctrine.dqlCompletion` | on |
| Report unknown entities and fields | `doctrine.dqlInspections` | on |

The directory settings and annotations can be stored per project.

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the mappings are read by the Forge agent on the
host; everything above works the same.

---
title: WebForge
description: The WebForge pack - npm scripts and package managers, the npm tool window, Node.js and TypeScript settings, and React, Vue and Angular component navigation and line markers.

tags: [webforge, javascript, typescript, npm, react, vue, angular]

# WebForge

The **WebForge** pack brings web development to Forge. Its plugins activate per project:

| Plugin | Id | Active for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML, CSS & JavaScript | `forge.web` | projects with JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML or CSS |
| React | `forge.react` | `react` or `next` in `package.json` |
| Vue.js | `forge.vue` | `vue` or `nuxt` |
| Angular | `forge.angular` | `@angular/core` or `angular.json` |

Editing intelligence comes from the web language servers of the catalog: TypeScript
(`typescript-language-server` or `vtsls`), Vue (Volar), the Angular Language Service, HTML,
CSS, ESLint and Tailwind CSS. Install them from Settings | Languages & Frameworks |
**TypeScript** (the "Language Services" list) or the Language Servers page. See
[Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md).

## npm scripts

### npm tool window

The **npm** tool window (left stripe) lists every `package.json` of the project (also in
workspaces and sub-folders) with its scripts and the package manager it uses.

![npm tool window](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-tool-window.png)

- **Double-click** a script to run it. It runs as a temporary **npm** run configuration in the
  Run tool window.
- The toolbar has **Reload Scripts**, **Run**, **Debug**, **Expand All**, **Collapse All** and
  **Settings**; the context menu has **Jump to Source**.
- **Install Dependencies** (Find Action) runs the package manager's install in the root
  package.

![Running a script](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-run.png)

### Run icons in package.json

Every script in `package.json` gets a ▶ icon in the gutter (setting
`web.npm.gutterIcons`). Click it for **Run** and **Debug**.

![Gutter menu](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-gutter-menu.png)

### Package managers

The package manager of a package is chosen from, in this order:

1. Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js | **Package manager** (`web.packageManager`)
   when it is not `auto`;
2. the `packageManager` field of `package.json` (e.g. `pnpm@9.15.4`);
3. a lock file in the package's folder or a parent: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`,
   `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`, `package-lock.json`;
4. npm.

npm, pnpm, yarn and bun are supported. Script arguments are passed after `--` for npm only.

### Debugging scripts

**Debug** on an npm script sets `NODE_OPTIONS` to the value of **Node options when debugging
scripts** (`web.npm.debugArguments`, default `--inspect`). Attach Chrome DevTools
(`chrome://inspect`) or another inspector client to the printed port.

> **Note:** Forge has no built-in JavaScript debugger yet; Debug only starts Node with the
> inspector enabled.

### Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js

![Node.js settings](docs/screenshots/webforge-settings-node.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package manager (`auto`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`) | `web.packageManager` | `auto` |
| Show run icons next to scripts in package.json | `web.npm.gutterIcons` | on |
| Node options when debugging scripts | `web.npm.debugArguments` | `--inspect` |

## Component navigation

`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` resolves components through your imports (relative paths,
`tsconfig`/`jsconfig` `paths` aliases, index files, barrel re-exports and **workspace
packages** imported by name — resolved through their `package.json` `exports`, `module`, `main`
or `types`, falling back to the sources when `dist/` is not built) before the language server
is asked. Several targets open the **Choose Declaration** popup. Turn it off with Settings | Languages & Frameworks | TypeScript | **Navigate
from JSX and template tags to components, props and events** (`web.navigation.components`).

### React

- On `<UserCard` in JSX: opens the component (function or class component, also anonymous
  default exports such as `export default () => …`, which are named after their file).
- On a prop (`title=`): opens the prop's declaration.
- On a component's own name: lists the JSX tags that use it (**Usages of …**).

![React Go to Declaration](docs/screenshots/webforge-react-goto.png)

![React usages](docs/screenshots/webforge-react-usages.png)

### Vue.js

Single-file components with `<script setup>` or the Options API:

- `<UserCard>` and `<user-card>` resolve through the script's imports, barrel files, or
  project-wide (global registration, Nuxt auto-imports);
- `:title` and `@select` go to the prop or emit;
- on a component's own name or block tag: its usages.

![Vue navigation](docs/screenshots/webforge-vue-goto.png)

### Angular

- Element and attribute selectors in templates go to the component or directive.
- `[input]` and `(output)` bindings go to the input or output (decorators or signal
  functions).
- `| pipe` goes to the pipe.
- `templateUrl` and `styleUrls`/`styleUrl` strings open the files (**Choose Stylesheet** when
  there are several).
- **Line markers** link a component class with its template and styles, and a template back
  to its component (setting **Show line markers between components, templates and styles**,
  `angular.gutterIcons`).

![Angular gutter](docs/screenshots/webforge-angular-gutter.png)

![Angular template navigation](docs/screenshots/webforge-angular-template.png)

When several targets match, a **Choose Declaration** popup lists them.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | TypeScript

![TypeScript settings](docs/screenshots/webforge-settings-typescript.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigate from JSX and template tags to components, props and events | `web.navigation.components` | on |
| Show line markers between components, templates and styles (Angular) | `angular.gutterIcons` | on |

Below these options, **Language Services** shows the web language servers (JavaScript &
TypeScript, Vue, Angular, HTML & CSS) with the same controls as the Language Servers page.

## Browser Companion

Click a React, Vue, Angular or Svelte component in your running app and its source opens in
Forge: see [Browser Companion](docs/guide/user/browser-companion.md).

## New web projects

The New Project wizard creates Vite, React, Vue.js, Angular, Svelte and static HTML projects,
see [Opening and creating projects](docs/guide/getting-started/projects.md).

> **Note:** the npm tool window and framework navigation read the project through this
> machine's file system; they are not available in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) yet.

---
title: LuaForge
description: The LuaForge pack - Lua index with EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, navigation, structure, hover, lua-language-server, StyLua and Lua Script run configurations.
order: 110
tags: [lua, luaforge, love, neovim, stylua]
---

# LuaForge

**LuaForge** (plugin `forge.lua`) supports Lua 5.1–5.4 and LuaJIT, LÖVE games and Neovim
configurations and plugins. It activates in [Lua projects](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md):
Lua files in the root, two or more in a folder, `.luarc.json`, `.luacheckrc`, `stylua.toml`,
`selene.toml` or a `*.rockspec`. LÖVE is detected from `conf.lua` (or a `main.lua` using
`love.`), Neovim from `init.lua` next to `lua/`, or `lua/` + `plugin/`.

## The Lua index

Forge indexes every Lua file in Rust (also in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md)):
locals with their scopes, parameters, globals, table fields, functions and methods
(`function M.f`, `function M:f`, `M.f = function`), `require` calls and each module's `return`.
Doc comments (`---`) are parsed as EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations: `@class`, `@field`, `@param`,
`@return`, `@type`, `@alias` (with `---|` values), `@deprecated`, `@see`.

Types are followed across files: `---@class`, `---@type`, `---@param`, the `---@return` of
called functions (`Class.new()` without annotations returns the class), `setmetatable` and class
parents.

**Reindex Lua Files** (Find Action) rebuilds the index.

### Modules and `require`

`require("a.b")` is resolved through `package.path`-like templates, in this order:
Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua | **Module search paths** (`lua.requirePaths`, e.g.
`scripts/?.lua`), `runtime.path` from `.luarc.json`, then `?.lua`, `?/init.lua`, `lua/?.lua`,
`src/?.lua` and `lib/?.lua`.

## Navigation and search

- `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` on a local, global, field, method or `require` string opens its
  declaration (tried before lua-language-server).
- **Go to Class** (`Ctrl+N`) finds `---@class` types, aliases and modules; **Go to Symbol**
  (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N`) finds functions and fields.
- **Structure** (`Alt+7`) shows the functions, tables and classes of the current file.

![Go to require](docs/screenshots/lua-goto-require.png)

![Structure](docs/screenshots/lua-structure.png)

## Hover documentation

Hovering shows the signature and annotations of functions, classes and fields. When
lua-language-server runs and answers, its hover is shown instead.

![Lua hover](docs/screenshots/lua-hover.png)

## lua-language-server

lua-language-server comes from the [language server catalog](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md). Install it
with your package manager (`brew install lua-language-server`, `sudo pacman -S
lua-language-server`) or from its releases.

| Option (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua) | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lua environment: `auto`, `plain`, `love`, `neovim` — adds the APIs of LÖVE (`love.*`) or Neovim (`vim.*`); `auto` detects them from the project | `langservers.lua.environment` | `auto` |
| Lua version (Lua 5.1–5.4, LuaJIT), used with plain Lua; LÖVE and Neovim run LuaJIT | `langservers.lua.version` | Lua 5.4 |
| lua-language-server executable (empty: PATH, Mason or Forge's server folder) | `langservers.servers.lua-language-server.path` | empty |
| Library paths (`workspace.library`), e.g. `~/.luarocks/share/lua/5.4` | `langservers.lua.libraries` | empty |

## StyLua

**Reformat Code** (`Ctrl+Alt+L`) formats Lua files with StyLua when it is installed; the
project's `stylua.toml` is honoured. Settings: **Reformat Code with StyLua**
(`lua.stylua.enabled`, on) and **StyLua executable** (`lua.stylua.path`, `stylua`).

## Running Lua

Files with a main chunk get a ▶ icon in the gutter, and `Ctrl+Shift+F10` runs the current
file. Both create a **Lua Script** run configuration that runs
`<interpreter> <interpreter options> <file> <arguments>`. The interpreter defaults to
Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua | **Lua interpreter** (`lua.interpreter`, `lua`; e.g.
`luajit`, `love` or a full path). LÖVE games run as `love <dir>`.

![Run Lua](docs/screenshots/lua-run.png)

## Settings summary

![Lua settings](docs/screenshots/lua-settings.png)

See the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md#languages--frameworks--lua) for every key.

---
title: Git
description: Git integration - the Commit tool window, AI commit messages, diff viewer, change markers, blame, branches, push, update and the Git log.
order: 120

---

# Git

The Git plugin (`forge.git`) drives the `git` command line (no libgit2) and works in any project
that is a Git repository (also when the project is a sub-folder of the repository). The
current branch is shown in the main toolbar and the status bar.

## Commit tool window

**Commit…** (`Ctrl+K`, macOS `Cmd+K`) opens the **Commit** tool window (`Alt+0`, left stripe).

![Commit tool window](docs/screenshots/vcs-commit.png)

- **Changes** and **Unversioned Files** are listed as trees grouped by folder. Tick the files
  to include. Double-click a file (or **Show Diff**, `Ctrl+D`) to see its diff.
- Toolbar: **Refresh** (`Ctrl+F5`), **Rollback…** (`Ctrl+Alt+Z`, discards the changes of the
  selected files after a confirmation), **Show Diff**, **Expand All**, **Collapse All**.
- Write the **Commit Message**. **Amend** amends the last commit (its message is loaded).
- **Commit** (`Ctrl+Enter` in the message) or **Commit and Push…**.

> **Note:** the commit message inspections and commit options in Settings | Version Control |
> Git (subject length, blank line, right margin, CRLF warning, sign-off), "Commit Message
> History" (`Ctrl+M`) and the **Commit Options** gear are not applied yet.

### AI commit messages

Click **Generate Commit Message with AI** (the sparkle icon above the message). Forge sends the
diff of the **ticked** files (new files included), the file list and the branch name to your
default AI provider and fills in the message: an imperative subject of at most 72 characters,
optionally a blank line and a short body. Large diffs are shortened so every file keeps a share
(about 14,000 characters in total).

Configure the provider in Settings | Tools | AI Providers; you can pick a separate model for
commit messages there. See [AI](docs/guide/user/ai.md#providers).

## Diff viewer

![Diff viewer](docs/screenshots/vcs-diff.png)

| Action | Key |
| --- | --- |
| Next / Previous Difference | `F7` / `Shift+F7` |
| Compare Next / Previous File | `Alt+Right` / `Alt+Left` |
| Jump to Source | `F4` |
| Close | `Escape` |

The toolbar also has viewer, whitespace and highlighting options and **Collapse Unchanged
Fragments**. Each changed block has a "Revert" arrow that replaces your side with the left
side.

## In the editor

### Change markers

Lines that differ from `HEAD` are marked in the gutter: added, modified and deleted. Click a
marker to see the old text and choose **Rollback** (`Ctrl+Alt+Z`) or **Show Diff** (`Ctrl+D`).

### Blame

Right-click the gutter and choose **Annotate with Git Blame** (also in the editor context menu
under Git, and in Find Action). The gutter then shows author and date per line, colored by
age; click an entry for the commit details. **Close Annotations** hides it.

![Blame](docs/screenshots/vcs-blame.png)

The caret line also shows an inline blame hint at its end: "Marlon, 2 days ago • message".

## Branches

Click the branch widget in the toolbar (or **Branches…** in Find Action) to open **Git
Branches**:

![Branches](docs/screenshots/vcs-branches.png)

- At the top: **Update Project…** (`Ctrl+T`), **Commit…** (`Ctrl+K`), **Push…**
  (`Ctrl+Shift+K`), **New Branch…** and **Checkout Tag or Revision…**.
- **Local** and **Remote** branches with a search field ("Search for branches and actions").
- A branch's submenu: for the current branch **New Branch from '…'…**, **Push…** and
  **Update**; for other branches **Checkout**, **New Branch from '…'…**, **Rebase 'current'
  onto '…'**, **Merge '…' into 'current'** and, for local branches, **Delete** (with "Force
  delete" for unmerged branches).

**New Branch…** asks for the name and whether to check it out.

## Push, update and fetch

| Action | Shortcut | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push… | `Ctrl+Shift+K` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+K`) | pushes the current branch |
| Update Project… | `Ctrl+T` (macOS `Cmd+T`) | pulls the current branch |
| Fetch | Find Action | fetches all remotes |

Results appear as balloons ("Pushed", "Project updated", "All files are up to date", or the
error). Git runs with `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`, so SSH remotes need a key in your ssh-agent (or
without passphrase); Forge cannot answer password prompts.

> **Note:** the update method setting (`vcs.git.updateMethod`), automatic fetching and the
> Git executable path in Settings | Version Control | Git are not applied yet. Set the
> environment variable `FORGE_GIT` to use another git binary.

## Log

The **Git** tool window (`Alt+9`, bottom) has a **Log** tab with the commit graph and a
**Console** tab with the git commands Forge ran.

![Git log](docs/screenshots/vcs-log.png)

- Filter by text or hash, branch, user, date and paths; **Show all branches**.
- Select a commit to see its changed files; open their diffs from there.
- **Fetch All Remotes** and **Refresh** (`Ctrl+F5`) in the toolbar.

## Code review

Pull and merge requests, issues and CI pipelines of GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo/Gitea are in
[Code hosts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md).

## Not available yet

Get from VCS (clone), stash/unstash, cherry-pick, interactive rebase, file history, Local
History and merge conflict resolution are not implemented yet.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md

---
title: Code hosts
description: Review pull and merge requests with inline threads, browse issues and CI pipelines for GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo/Gitea, including self-hosted servers.
order: 130
tags: [github, gitlab, forgejo, gitea, pull requests, merge requests, code review, ci]
---

# Code hosts

The plugin **GitLab, Forgejo and GitHub** (`forge.code-hosts`) brings code review into Forge:

| Host | API | Number format | Self-hosted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitLab | REST v4 | `!12` | yes (self-managed, also with a relative URL root or SSH port) |
| Forgejo / Gitea | `/api/v1` | `#12` | yes (e.g. Codeberg) |
| GitHub | REST + GraphQL for review threads | `#12` | GitHub Enterprise Server |

The repository is detected from `git remote -v` (https, ssh and scp-style URLs, nested GitLab
groups). Wording follows the host: "merge request" on GitLab, "pull request" elsewhere.

## Logging in

Open Settings | Version Control | **GitLab**, **Forgejo / Gitea** or **GitHub** and click
**Log In with Token…**. Enter the **Server** (for self-hosted instances) and an access token:

| Host | Token permissions |
| --- | --- |
| GitLab | scopes `api`, `read_user` |
| Forgejo / Gitea | read/write for repository and issue, read for user |
| GitHub | scopes `repo`, `read:org`, `workflow` (or a fine-grained token with pull request, issue and actions access) |

![Accounts](docs/screenshots/forges-accounts.png)

The token is verified first and then stored in the operating system keychain (service
`forge-forges`), never in a settings file. Accounts themselves (server, user) are kept in
`forges.toml` in Forge's config folder. Without an account, the environment variables
`GITLAB_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `GITEA_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` are used for
the public servers ("Token from environment").

Errors are explained in plain words: a rejected token, missing permissions, rate limits (with
the reset time) or an unreachable server.

## Pull Requests tool window

The **Pull Requests** tool window (left stripe, **View Pull/Merge Requests** in Find Action)
has three tabs.

![Merge request list](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-list.png)

### Pull/Merge Requests

- Search, plus filters for **State** (Open, Merged, Closed, All), **Author**, **Label**,
  **Assignee** and **Reviewer**, and **Quick Filters** such as "Assigned to you" and
  "Review requests".
- Each row shows the title, number, author, age, CI status, comment count and avatar.
- Click a request to open it as an editor tab.
- **+** (or **Create Merge Request…** in Find Action) creates one.

### A pull/merge request tab

![Overview](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-overview.png)

- **Overview**: description (Markdown), comments and review threads with **Reply**,
  resolve/unresolve (where the host supports it; Forgejo cannot resolve threads through its
  API), reviewers and approvals, assignees, labels, the pipeline with its jobs, and the merge
  status ("No conflicts with main").
- **Files**: the changed files with their diffs; comment on a line to start a thread.
  **Show Diff (side by side)** opens the diff viewer.
- Actions: **Approve**, **Merge…** (merge commit, **Squash and merge**, **Rebase and
  merge**, "Mark as ready before merging" for drafts, the commit message), **Close**,
  **Check Out** (fetches the source branch and checks it out locally), **Open in Browser** and
  **Refresh**.

![Files](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-files.png)

### Create a pull/merge request

**Create Merge Request…** asks for the **Head branch** and **Base branch**, **Title**,
**Description** (Markdown), **Reviewers**, **Labels** and whether it is a draft.

![Create merge request](docs/screenshots/forges-create-mr.png)

### Issues

Search and filter issues, open one as a tab, read and add comments.

![Issues](docs/screenshots/forges-issues.png)

### Pipelines

CI runs of the repository (GitLab pipelines, GitHub Actions workflow runs, Forgejo/Gitea
Actions runs) with their status and jobs.

## CI status in the status bar

The status bar shows the CI status of the current branch ("CI: Running", "Passed", "Failed").
Settings (not shown in the Settings dialog; set them in `settings.toml`, see
[Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#settings-files)):

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vcs.hosts.statusBarPipeline` | `true` | show the CI status of the current branch |
| `vcs.hosts.refreshSeconds` | `120` | refresh requests and pipelines every N seconds; `0` turns automatic refresh off |

---
title: Run/Debug configurations
description: Create and run Run/Debug configurations for PHP scripts, PHPUnit, Artisan, Composer, npm, shell scripts and Lua, the run widget, the Run tool window and the PHPUnit test tree.
order: 140
tags: [run, debug, configurations, phpunit, tests, npm]

# Run/Debug configurations

A **run configuration** describes how to start something: a script, a test suite, a command.
Forge's configurations work like PHPStorm's.

## Run widget

The run widget in the main toolbar shows the selected configuration with **Run** (▶) and
**Debug** (🐞) buttons. Its dropdown lists all configurations and has **Edit
Configurations…**; without configurations it reads **Add Configuration…**.

![Run widget](docs/screenshots/run-toolbar-dropdown.png)

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run the selected configuration | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` |
| Debug the selected configuration | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` |
| Run… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` |
| Debug… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Alt+D` |
| Run Context Configuration (the test, script or Lua chunk at the caret) | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Shift+R` |
| Debug Context Configuration | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+D` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Rerun | `Ctrl+F5` | `Cmd+R` |
| Edit Configurations… | Find Action | |

In the **Run…** chooser, `Enter` runs and `Shift+Enter` (or holding `Shift`) debugs; it also
offers **Run Shell Command…** and **Edit Configuration…**.

## Run/Debug Configurations dialog

![Run/Debug Configurations](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-dialog.png)

- **+** (`Alt+Insert`) adds a configuration from a type; copy, remove and reorder with the
  toolbar. **Edit configuration templates…** sets the defaults for new configurations of a
  type.
- Common fields: **Name**, **Store as project file**, the type's own fields, **Interpreter**
  and **Interpreter options** (PHP and Lua types), **Arguments**, **Working directory**
  (default: the project root), **Environment variables** and **Before launch** tasks (another
  run configuration or a shell command).
- The **Command Line** preview shows exactly what will run.

### Configuration types

| Type | Fields | Runs | Debug |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP Script | File | `<php> <options> <file> <arguments>` | Xdebug |
| PHPUnit | Test scope: Directory, File, Class, Method or "Defined in the configuration file"; Configuration file (`phpunit.xml` detected); Test runner options | `phpunit --teamcity …` (from `vendor/bin`) | Xdebug |
| Artisan | Command (`migrate --seed`) | `<php> artisan <command>` | Xdebug |
| Composer Script | Script | `composer run <script>` with `php.composer.executable` | Xdebug |
| npm | package.json, Command (`run`, `install`, …), Scripts, Package manager | `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` | sets `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect` |
| Shell Script | Execute: Script file or Script text; Script path / text | the shell | — |
| Lua Script | File | `<lua> <options> <file> <arguments>`, LÖVE games as `love <dir>` | — |

The PHP interpreter defaults to `php.interpreter` (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP), the
Lua interpreter to `lua.interpreter`.

> **Note:** the types "PHP Built-in Web Server" and "PHP Remote Debug" are declared by the PHP
> plugins but not available yet. To debug a web request, use
> [Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#listening-for-connections).

### Where configurations are stored

| | File |
| --- | --- |
| Shared ("Store as project file") | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.toml` — commit it to share with your team |
| Local configurations, the selected one, templates | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.local.toml` |

## Temporary configurations

Gutter ▶ icons create temporary configurations: PHPUnit test classes and methods, `package.json`
scripts, Lua main chunks, scratch files and HTTP requests. A double-click in the npm tool
window does the same.

## Run tool window

The **Run** tool window (`Alt+4`) has one tab per run. Tabs can be pinned and closed (`Ctrl+Shift+F4`).

- Output is shown with ANSI colors; `\r` progress lines update in place.
- File references (`app/User.php:42`, stack traces) and URLs are clickable.
- Toolbar: **Rerun**, **Stop**, **Soft-Wrap**, **Scroll to the End**, **Clear All**.
- Typing sends input to the process (stdin).
- Stop sends SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after 2 seconds (`taskkill /T` on
  Windows).

Settings | Editor | General | Console: **Use soft wraps in console** (`run.console.softWrap`).

## Test results

Test runners that speak TeamCity service messages (PHPUnit with `--teamcity`, Pest, Jest)
show a **Test Results** tree next to the console:

![PHPUnit test tree](docs/screenshots/run-phpunit-tree.png)

- Pass/fail/ignored per test with durations; **Show Passed**, **Show Ignored**, **Sort
  Alphabetically**, **Sort by Duration**, **Expand/Collapse All**.
- **Previous/Next Failed Test** and **Rerun Failed Tests**.
- A failed assertion shows a **Comparison Failure** with Expected and Actual.
- Double-click a test to open it.

## Debugging

**Debug** on a PHP configuration (PHP Script, PHPUnit, Artisan, Composer) starts Forge's Xdebug
listener and runs the process with the Xdebug environment (`XDEBUG_MODE=debug`,
`XDEBUG_SESSION`, `XDEBUG_CONFIG`). See [Xdebug debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md).

> **Note:** Run/Debug configurations work in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md): the
> process runs on the remote host.
