---
title: Xdebug debugging
description: Step-debug PHP with Xdebug 3 - listening for connections, breakpoints and conditions, stepping, variables, watches, Evaluate Expression, servers and path mappings.
order: 150
tags: [debug, xdebug, php, breakpoints, dbgp]
---

# Xdebug debugging

The Xdebug plugin (`forge.xdebug`, PHPForge pack) is a DBGp server for **Xdebug 3**. It
accepts any number of connections at once, from the CLI, a web server, Docker containers or
another machine.

## Preparing PHP

Install Xdebug 3 and enable step debugging in your `php.ini` (or the container's):

```ini
zend_extension=xdebug
xdebug.mode=debug
xdebug.client_port=9003
; for web requests: start on every request, or use a browser extension / XDEBUG_SESSION cookie
xdebug.start_with_request=trigger
; when PHP runs in Docker or on another machine
; xdebug.client_host=host.docker.internal
```

Forge listens on port **9003** (`php.debug.port`).

## Two ways to start

### Debug a run configuration

Press **Debug** (`Shift+F9`) on a PHP Script, PHPUnit, Artisan or Composer configuration (or a
gutter ▶ menu). Forge starts listening and runs the process with:

```text
XDEBUG_MODE=debug
XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE
XDEBUG_CONFIG=client_host=127.0.0.1 client_port=9003 idekey=FORGE
PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<server>   (when a server is chosen)
```

so no `php.ini` change is needed for CLI scripts and tests.

### Listening for connections

For web requests, click the telephone icon **Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections** in
the main toolbar (action `PhpListenDebugAction`). The status bar shows that Forge is listening;
click again to stop. Then open the page with Xdebug triggered (`XDEBUG_SESSION` cookie, query
parameter or browser extension).

![Incoming connection](docs/screenshots/debugger-incoming.png)

When a connection comes from an unknown server whose script is not a project file, the
**Incoming Connection From Xdebug** dialog asks which project file the server file maps to and
creates a server with that path mapping. Turn on **Ignore external connections through
unregistered server configurations** (`php.debug.ignoreExternalConnections`) to detach such
connections silently.

## Breakpoints

- Click a line number in a PHP file, or press **Toggle Line Breakpoint** (`Ctrl+F8`, macOS
  `Cmd+F8`).
- Right-click a breakpoint to set a **condition** (a PHP expression; the script suspends only
  when it is true) or disable it.
- **View Breakpoints…** (`Ctrl+Shift+F8`) lists all breakpoints, including **PHP Exception
  Breakpoints** (an exception class, or `*` for any).
- **Mute Breakpoints** turns all of them off temporarily.

![Breakpoint condition](docs/screenshots/debugger-condition-popup.png)

![Breakpoints dialog](docs/screenshots/debugger-breakpoints.png)

Breakpoints are stored in `<project>/.forge/breakpoints.json`.

## The Debug tool window

![Paused](docs/screenshots/debugger-paused.png)

While paused, the execution point is highlighted in the editor and variable values are shown
inline at the end of lines (`php.debug.showInlineValues`). The **Debug** tool window (`Alt+5`)
has a tab per session with:

- **Threads & Variables**: the frames on the left (click to switch), variables on the right.
  Arrays and objects expand lazily.
- **Console**: the script's output.
- The evaluate field at the top: type an expression and press `Enter` to evaluate it, or
  `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` to add it as a watch.

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resume Program | `F9` | `Cmd+Alt+R` |
| Pause Program | toolbar | toolbar |
| Step Over | `F8` | `F8` |
| Step Into | `F7` | `F7` |
| Smart Step Into | `Shift+F7` | `Shift+F7` |
| Force Step Into | `Alt+Shift+F7` | `Alt+Shift+F7` |
| Step Out | `Shift+F8` | `Shift+F8` |
| Run to Cursor | `Alt+F9` | `Alt+F9` |
| Force Run to Cursor | `Ctrl+Alt+F9` | `Cmd+Alt+F9` |
| Evaluate Expression… | `Alt+F8` | `Alt+F8` |
| Quick Evaluate Expression | `Ctrl+Alt+F8` | `Cmd+Alt+F8` |
| Show Execution Point | `Alt+F10` | `Alt+F10` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Add to Watches | context menu | context menu |

![Evaluate Expression](docs/screenshots/debugger-evaluate.png)

Smart Step Into currently behaves like Step Into. Pause depends on the engine and may
report "Pause is not supported by this engine".

## Servers and path mappings

When PHP runs in a container or on another machine, its file paths differ from yours. Define a
**server** in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | **Servers**: **Name**, **Host**,
**Port**, **Debugger** (Xdebug) and **path mappings** (project file or directory → absolute
path on the server).

![Servers](docs/screenshots/debugger-servers.png)

A session finds its server from `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<name>`, otherwise from
`$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME']` and `SERVER_PORT`. Servers are stored in
`<project>/.forge/php-servers.json`.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Debug

![Debug settings](docs/screenshots/debugger-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debug port | `php.debug.port` | 9003 |
| Ignore external connections through unregistered server configurations | `php.debug.ignoreExternalConnections` | off |
| Break at first line in PHP scripts | `php.debug.breakAtFirstLine` | off |
| Step out of files that are not mapped into the project | `php.debug.ignoreUnmappedFiles` | on |
| Show variable values in editor while debugging | `php.debug.showInlineValues` | on |
| Max. children (array elements / properties per page) | `php.debug.maxChildren` | 100 |
| Max. depth (levels fetched at once) | `php.debug.maxDepth` | 1 |
| Max. string length (bytes) | `php.debug.maxData` | 65536 |

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md), **Start Listening** listens on a free local port
and asks the remote host, over SSH, to listen on `127.0.0.1:<php.debug.port>` (9003) and forward
connections to Forge (a reverse tunnel, re-established after reconnects). Configure Xdebug on
the host with `xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1`. Xdebug's paths are the host's paths, which are the
project's, so no path mappings are needed. The status bar shows that the listener goes through
the host.

![Listening through the host](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-debug-listening.png)

![Remote debug session](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-debug-session.png)

> **Note:** JavaScript and Node.js debugging are not built in; see
> [WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#debugging-scripts).

# Terminal

The **Terminal** tool window (`Alt+F12`, bottom stripe) runs your shell on a real pseudo
terminal (xterm.js in the UI, a PTY in Rust), so interactive programs such as `vim`, `htop`,
`git rebase -i` or `php artisan tinker` work.

![Terminal tabs](docs/screenshots/terminal-tabs.png)

## Tabs

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show/hide the terminal | `Alt+F12` | `Alt+F12` |
| New tab | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `Cmd+T` |
| Close tab | `Ctrl+Shift+F4` | `Cmd+Shift+F4` |

Tabs are named "Local", "Local (2)", …; double-click a tab or use **Rename Session** to rename
it. A tab's context menu has **New Tab**, **Rename Session**, **Close Tab** and **Close Other
Tabs**. The terminal area's context menu has **Copy** (`Ctrl+Shift+C`), **Paste**
(`Ctrl+Shift+V`), **Select All** and **Clear Buffer**.

## Keyboard

While the terminal has focus, plain `Ctrl`+letter, `Alt`+letter and `Escape` go to the shell
(so `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+R`, `Alt+B` behave as in any terminal). Function keys, `Alt`+digit,
`Ctrl+Shift` and `Ctrl+Alt` combinations still reach the IDE, so `Alt+1` or `Shift+Escape`
work from the terminal.

## Links

URLs and file references such as `app/Models/User.php:42` in the output are clickable; files
open in the editor at that line.

## Shell and start directory

The shell is, in this order: Settings | Tools | Terminal | **Shell path**
(`terminal.shellPath`), `$SHELL` on Linux/macOS (then bash, zsh, sh), on Windows PowerShell 7
(`pwsh.exe`), Windows PowerShell or `%ComSpec%`. bash, zsh and fish start as login shells.

New tabs start in the project root unless **Start directory** (`terminal.startDirectory`) is
set; **Environment variables** (`terminal.environment`, one `NAME=value` per entry) are added.

## Settings | Tools | Terminal

| Option | Setting | Default | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shell path | `terminal.shellPath` | system default | user |
| Default tab name | `terminal.tabName` | `Local` | user |
| Audible bell | `terminal.audibleBell` | off | not applied yet |
| Copy to clipboard on selection | `terminal.copyOnSelection` | off | user |
| Shell integration | `terminal.shellIntegration` | on | not applied yet |
| Start directory | `terminal.startDirectory` | project root | user, project |
| Environment variables | `terminal.environment` | empty | user, project |

## Other terminals

The Services tool window opens terminals into Docker containers and Kubernetes pods
(`docker exec`, `kubectl exec`), and in a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the terminal
runs on the remote host.

![Remote terminal](docs/screenshots/remote-terminal.png)

---
title: Database tools and SQL console

# Database tools and SQL console

The plugin **Database Tools and SQL** (`forge.database`) is Forge's DataGrip part. It supports
**MySQL/MariaDB**, **PostgreSQL** and **SQLite** (through `sqlx`, no JDBC drivers to download).

## Database tool window

The **Database** tool window (right stripe) shows your data sources as a tree:
data source → schema → tables (with comments) → columns, keys and indexes.

![Database tree](docs/screenshots/database-tree.png)

Toolbar: **+** (add data source), **Refresh**, **Data Source Properties** (`Shift+Enter`),
**Jump to Query Console…** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`), **Collapse All**. Context menu of a node: **New
Query Console**, **Edit Data** (tables), **Go to DDL**, **Copy Name**, **Properties**,
**Refresh**, **Disconnect**, **Delete**.

## Data sources

**New Data Source…** (the **+** button or Find Action) opens **Data Sources and Drivers**:

![Data source dialog](docs/screenshots/database-data-source-dialog.png)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name, Comment | |
| Driver | MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite |
| Host, Port, Database / SQLite file | SQLite files are chosen with a file picker |
| Authentication | User & Password, or none |
| Password | stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-db`), never in project files |
| SSL mode | Disable, Prefer, Require |
| Options | read-only, transaction control (Auto / Manual), connect timeout, startup script |
| Scope | **Project Data Sources** (`<project>/.forge/dataSources.toml`, shareable) or **Global Data Sources** (`dataSources.toml` in Forge's config folder) |

**Test Connection** shows success with the server version, or the error.

### From `.env`

When a project's `.env` has Laravel's `DB_*` variables or Symfony's `DATABASE_URL`, Forge shows
a balloon "Database found in .env" with **Add data source**; the tree also offers **Data
Source from .env**. Turn this off with Settings | Tools | Database | **Suggest data sources
from .env files** (`database.suggestFromEnv`).

## Query console

**New Query Console** on a data source (or **Open Query Console**) opens a console tab:

![Query console](docs/screenshots/database-console.png)

- SQL highlighting for the data source's dialect and completion of keywords, tables and
  columns.
- **Execute** (`Ctrl+Enter`, macOS `Cmd+Enter`) runs the statement at the caret, or the
  selection. Several statements separated by `;` run one after another.
- Results appear below in tabs (**Output** plus one tab per result set), paged by
  **Result set page size** (`database.pageSize`, 500).
- **Cancel Running Statements** stops a long query.
- **Tx: Auto / Manual** switches the transaction mode; in manual mode use **Commit** and
  **Rollback**.
- The schema selector at the top right sets the current schema.

SQL [scratch files](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md) attached to a data source open as consoles too.

## Data grid and table editor

**Edit Data** (or double-click a table) opens the table in an editor tab with paging (**First,
Previous, Next, Last Page**), a **WHERE** filter and an **ORDER BY** field.

![Editing data](docs/screenshots/database-grid-edit.png)

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edit a cell | double-click or `Enter` | same |
| Add Row | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| Delete Rows | `Ctrl+Y` | `Cmd+Backspace` |
| Revert Selected | `Ctrl+Alt+Z` | `Cmd+Alt+Z` |
| Submit | `Ctrl+Enter` | `Cmd+Enter` |
| Reload Page | toolbar | toolbar |

Cell context menu: **Copy**, **Copy with Header**, **Set NULL**. Changes are applied in one
transaction on **Submit**. Tables without a primary key cannot identify changed rows: only new
rows can be submitted there.

NULL is displayed as `<null>` (**Show NULL as**, `database.showNullAs`). Binary values are shown
as hex.

## Export

**Export Data** (the download icon in a result or table) writes the rows as **CSV**, **JSON**
or SQL **INSERT** statements for the dialect.

## Settings | Tools | Database

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result set page size | `database.pageSize` | 500 |
| Show NULL as | `database.showNullAs` | `<null>` |
| Suggest data sources from .env files | `database.suggestFromEnv` | on |

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md), project data sources (and the `.env`
suggestions) are read from the host, and Forge connects to them through an SSH tunnel to their
host and port **as the remote host sees them** — `localhost:3306` means the database on the
server. The data source shows which host it goes through. Global data sources connect directly
from your machine.

![Remote data source](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-data-source-dialog.png)

![Remote database](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-database.png)

> **Note:** SQLite files on the remote host cannot be opened.

title: Scratches, consoles and HTTP client
description: Scratch files and buffers in any language, running PHP/JS/TS/Python/shell/Lua scratches, SQL scratches as database consoles, and .http request files with variables and environments.
order: 180

# Scratches, consoles and HTTP client

**Scratch files** are throw-away files for experiments, like PHPStorm's "Scratches and
Consoles". They are **global**: they do not belong to a project and are kept in Forge's config
folder (`<config dir>/forge/scratches/`), so they are available in every project.

## Creating scratches

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Scratch File… | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+N` |
| New Scratch Buffer | Find Action | Find Action |

**New Scratch File** asks for the language: type to filter (fuzzy), recently used languages
come first. Every file type with an extension is available.

![New Scratch File](docs/screenshots/scratches-new-popup.png)

New scratches are numbered `scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, …; HTTP scratches start as
`rest-api.http`. **Scratch buffers** are plain text files `buffer1.txt` … `buffer5.txt`; after
five, the oldest is reused.

## Scratches and Consoles in the Project view

The bottom of the Project tool window has a **Scratches and Consoles** node with **Scratches**
and **Database Consoles**. A scratch's context menu has **Rename…**, **Delete** and, for SQL
scratches, **Attach Data Source…**.

![Scratches in the Project view](docs/screenshots/scratches-project-view.png)

## Running scratches

Scratches with a runner get a ▶ icon in the gutter; `Ctrl+Shift+F10` runs the current one.
The output appears in the Run tool window.

| Language | Runs with |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `php.interpreter`, with `-d auto_prepend_file=<project>/vendor/autoload.php` when the open project has an autoloader, so your classes are available |
| JavaScript | `node` |
| TypeScript | `node --experimental-strip-types` (Node 22.6+) |
| Python | `python3` (`python` on Windows) |
| Shell (`.sh`, `.bash`) | `sh` |
| Lua | `lua` |

![PHP scratch run](docs/screenshots/scratches-php-run.png)

Other languages show "Scratches of this language have no runner."

## SQL scratches

A `.sql` scratch can be attached to a data source (**Attach Data Source…**); it then opens as a
query console of that data source with execution, results and transactions. See
[Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md).

![SQL scratch](docs/screenshots/scratches-sql-console.png)

## HTTP client (`.http` files)

`.http` files hold one or more requests in PHPStorm's HTTP Client format. They work as
scratches (New Scratch File → HTTP Request) and as files in your project. Each request gets a ▶
icon in the gutter; click it to send the request. The response (status, headers, body) appears
in the Run tool window, followed by the report of its response handler. Project `.http` files
run as an `http-request` run configuration.

![HTTP request](docs/screenshots/scratches-http-request.png)

### Syntax

```http
@host = localhost:8000

### List users
GET http://{{host}}/api/users?page=1
Accept: application/json

###
# @name createUser
POST http://{{host}}/api/users
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
X-Request-Id: {{$uuid}}

{ "name": "Ada", "age": {{$random.integer(18, 99)}} }

> {%
  client.global.set("userId", response.body.id);
  client.test("User was created", function () {
    client.assert(response.status === 201, "Expected 201 but got " + response.status);
  });
%}

### Body from a file
POST http://{{host}}/api/import
Content-Type: application/json

< ./import.json

### Long query strings can continue on indented lines
GET https://{{host}}/search
    ?q=forge
    &limit=10
```

- `###` separates requests; text after it names the request. `# @name x` also names one.
- A request is a request line `METHOD URL [HTTP/version]` (the method defaults to `GET`;
  `http://` is added when the URL has no scheme), optional indented `?`/`&` lines continuing the
  query string, headers, a blank line and the body.
- `@name = value` defines a file variable; `{{name}}` uses it in the URL, headers and body.
  Variables may refer to other variables. Unknown variables are left as they are.
- **Body files**: a body line `< ./file.json` inserts the file as it is, `<@ ./file.json` also
  substitutes variables in it. Paths are relative to the `.http` file.
- Comments start with `#` or `//`.

![Body from a file](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-body-file.png)

### Dynamic variables

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{$uuid}}`, `{{$random.uuid}}` | a random UUID |
| `{{$timestamp}}` | Unix time in seconds |
| `{{$isoTimestamp}}` | the current time in ISO 8601 |
| `{{$randomInt}}` | a random integer 0–1000 |
| `{{$random.integer(from, to)}}` | a random integer in the range |

### Environments

Put environment files in the project root, as in PHPStorm:

```json
// http-client.env.json (commit it)
{
  "dev":  { "host": "localhost:8000" },
  "prod": { "host": "shop.example.com" }
}
```

```json
// http-client.private.env.json (keep it out of Git)
{
  "dev": { "token": "s3cret" }
}
```

Every `.http` editor has a toolbar with an **environment selector** listing the environments of
these files. The choice is stored per project in `httpClient.environment` (Settings | Tools |
**HTTP Client**): empty means `dev`, else the first environment; `$none` runs without an
environment. Private values win over public ones.

![Environment selector](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-environments.png)

Variable precedence, lowest first: environment < `client.global` (set by handlers) < in-file
`@name = value`.

### Response handlers

A handler after a request, inline `> {% … %}` or in a file `> ./handler.js`, runs when the
response arrives. Forge implements a safe subset of PHPStorm's HTTP Client API without a
JavaScript engine:

- `client.global.set(name, value)`, `get`, `clear`, `clearAll`, `isEmpty` — globals live for
  the IDE session and can be used as `{{name}}` in later requests;
- `client.test(name, function () { … })`, `client.assert(condition, message?)`,
  `client.log(…)`;
- `response.status`, `response.body` (parsed JSON, else text) with `.a.b`, `["a"]`, `[0]`,
  `response.headers.valueOf(name)` / `valuesOf(name)`, `response.contentType.mimeType` /
  `charset`;
- `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse`, string and array helpers (`length`, `includes`,
  `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `indexOf`, `toLowerCase`, `toUpperCase`, `trim`);
- `var`/`let`/`const`, `if`/`else`, `return`, functions and arrow functions, literals,
  arithmetic, comparisons, `&&`, `||`, `??` and `?:`.

Loops and anything else stop the script with an error that names the unsupported construct.
Test results and log lines are printed after the response.

![Handler report](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-handler.png)

> **Note:** response references (`<> file`) are skipped. HTTP requests read the environment
> files through the local project; they are not available in
> [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) yet.

Source: docs/guide/user/services.md

---
title: Services
description: The Services tool window - Docker containers, images, volumes and networks, Docker Compose projects, Kubernetes workloads, logs, exec terminals, image pulls, registries and gutter run icons.
order: 190
tags: [docker, compose, kubernetes, services, containers]
---

# Services

The plugin **Docker and Kubernetes** (`forge.services`) fills the **Services** tool window
(`Alt+8`, macOS `Cmd+8`). It talks to the Docker Engine API directly (Unix socket, Windows
named pipe or TCP with TLS) and to the Kubernetes API with your kubeconfig. The docker CLI is
only used for `docker compose`, image builds and interactive terminals; `kubectl` only for pod
terminals.

![Services](docs/screenshots/services-docker-dashboard.png)

The tree has three roots:

| Root | Children |
| --- | --- |
| **Docker** | Containers, Images, Networks, Volumes |
| **Docker Compose** | compose projects found in the project root and one folder below, with their services and containers |
| **Kubernetes** | contexts → namespaces → Pods, Deployments, Services |

The status bar shows the Docker connection ("Docker 27.3.1", "Docker: connecting…",
"Docker: not connected"). Forge follows Docker's event stream, so the tree updates by itself,
and retries the connection every 10 seconds.

## Details pane

Selecting a node shows its details on the right, in tabs:

| Tab | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard | status, image, ports, mounts, networks, environment, labels; tables for compose and Kubernetes objects |
| Log | the log, following new lines; starts with the last `docker.logs.tail` lines (500) |
| Attached Console | output of compose Up/Down, builds and pulls |
| Inspection | the raw JSON (`docker inspect`) |

![Logs](docs/screenshots/services-docker-logs.png)

## Actions

The toolbar and the context menu offer what applies to the selected node:

| Node | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Docker (not connected) | Connect, Refresh |
| Running container | Stop, Restart, Delete, Show Log, Exec (open a terminal in the container), Pull Image |
| Stopped container | Start, Delete, Show Log, Pull Image |
| Image | Pull, Delete |
| Images group | Pull Image…, Refresh |
| Volume, network | Delete |
| Compose project | Up (Run all services), Stop, Restart, Down (`docker compose down`), Show Log |
| Compose service | Up, Stop, Restart, Down, Show Log, Exec |
| Pod | Delete, Show Log, Exec (`kubectl exec`), Forward Ports… |
| Deployment | Restart Rollout, Show Log (all pods and containers) |

**Exec** opens a terminal tab in the Terminal tool window running `docker exec -it` (or
`kubectl exec -it`) with bash when the container has it, else sh. Containers started with a
TTY also offer an attached console (`docker attach`).

![Exec terminal](docs/screenshots/services-exec-terminal.png)

![Compose](docs/screenshots/services-compose.png)

![Kubernetes pod log](docs/screenshots/services-kubernetes-pod-log.png)

## Kubernetes pods and deployments

- **Container picker**: a pod with several containers (including init containers) shows a
  container selector on its details. Log, Exec and the Attached Console use the picked container;
  the default is the one named by the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container` annotation, else
  the first container. The Dashboard lists the containers' declared ports.
- **Deployment logs** follow every container of every pod that matches the deployment's
  selector, each line prefixed like `kubectl logs --prefix` (`[pod/<pod>/<container>]`).

![Container picker](docs/screenshots/services-container-picker.png)

![Deployment logs](docs/screenshots/services-deployment-logs.png)

### Port forwarding

**Forward Ports…** on a pod opens a dialog: enter `local:pod` pairs separated by commas, for
example `8080:80, 9000, :5432` (a single port forwards the same port; `:80` picks a free local
port). The pod's declared container ports are offered.

![Forward Ports dialog](docs/screenshots/services-port-forward-dialog.png)

Forge listens on `127.0.0.1:<local>` and opens one connection to the pod per accepted
connection (the Kubernetes port-forward API over WebSocket, no `kubectl` needed). Active
forwards appear in the tree (`⇄ 8080→80`) and on the pod and Kubernetes details, under **Port
Forwarding**, each with **Stop Port Forwarding**.

![Port forwards](docs/screenshots/services-port-forwards.png)

## Compose files and Dockerfiles in the editor

- `compose.yaml` / `docker-compose.yml` get a ▶ in the gutter on `services:` (**Run all
  services**) and on each service (`docker compose up` for that service).
- A `Dockerfile` gets a ▶ on its first `FROM`: **Run on 'Docker'** builds the image and runs a
  container; output appears in Attached Console.

![Compose gutter](docs/screenshots/services-compose-gutter.png)

Compose files support profiles, env files, `${VAR}` interpolation from the project's `.env`
and override files.

## Pulling images and registries

**Pull Image…** (Find Action **Docker.PullImage**, or the Images group) asks for
`repository[:tag]`, e.g. `redis:7-alpine`, and shows the progress.

![Pull image](docs/screenshots/services-pull-image.png)

Private registries: Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Docker | **Docker Registry**.
Add the registry (`docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, …), user name and password or access token. The
password goes to the OS keychain (service `forge-containers`); the setting
`docker.registries` only keeps `server<TAB>user`. Without accounts, public images are pulled
anonymously.

## Settings

### Build, Execution, Deployment | Docker

![Docker settings](docs/screenshots/settings-docker.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect to Docker daemon with (`auto`, `unix`, `pipe`, `tcp`, `ssh`, `context`) | `docker.connection` | `auto` |
| SSH host: `ssh://user@host[:port]` or a `Host` alias of `~/.ssh/config` | `docker.ssh.url` | empty |
| Docker socket on the host (empty: `/var/run/docker.sock`) | `docker.ssh.socketPath` | empty |
| Docker context (`docker context ls`) | `docker.context` | empty |
| Socket path (Unix socket or named pipe; empty: the first existing default) | `docker.socketPath` | empty |
| Engine API URL (TCP) | `docker.tcp.url` | `tcp://localhost:2375` |
| Use TLS (verify the daemon certificate) | `docker.tcp.tls` | off |
| Certificates folder (`ca.pem`, `cert.pem`, `key.pem`) | `docker.tcp.certPath` | empty |
| Docker executable (compose, builds, exec) | `docker.cliPath` | `docker` |
| Show the last log lines | `docker.logs.tail` | 500 |

With `auto`, Forge uses `DOCKER_HOST` when set (also `ssh://` hosts), else the current Docker
context (`DOCKER_CONTEXT` or `currentContext` in `~/.docker/config.json`), else the platform
default socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`, Docker Desktop's `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`, rootless
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock` or Podman's socket; `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` on Windows).
**Test Connection** checks the settings.

**Docker over SSH** (`ssh`): Forge connects with its own SSH client (keys from ssh-agent and
`~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/config` aliases) and talks to the remote Docker socket through the SSH
connection; nothing is installed on the host. The host key must already be in `known_hosts`;
unknown keys are refused with their fingerprint. Compose, builds and terminals use the docker
CLI, which reaches `ssh://` hosts itself.

![Docker over SSH](docs/screenshots/settings-docker-ssh.png)

**Docker contexts** (`context`): the page lists the contexts of the Docker CLI
(`~/.docker/contexts`) with **Use**; Forge then connects to that context's endpoint.

![Docker contexts](docs/screenshots/settings-docker-contexts.png)

### Build, Execution, Deployment | Kubernetes

![Kubernetes settings](docs/screenshots/settings-kubernetes.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kubeconfig file (empty: `$KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config`) | `kubernetes.kubeconfig` | empty |
| Default context (empty: the kubeconfig's current-context) | `kubernetes.defaultContext` | empty |
| Default namespace (empty: the context's namespace, else `default`) | `kubernetes.defaultNamespace` | empty |
| kubectl executable | `kubernetes.kubectlPath` | `kubectl` |

Kubernetes authentication supports CA certificates, bearer tokens, client certificates, basic
auth and exec credential plugins (as used by EKS, GKE and AKS).

> **Note:** the Services tool window always talks to the Docker daemon and cluster configured
> on this machine, also when a remote project is open; use Docker over SSH to reach the remote
> host's daemon. Port forwarding is available for Kubernetes pods, not for Docker containers.

Source: docs/guide/user/remote-development.md

---
title: Remote development
description: Open a project on a Linux server over SSH - connections, authentication, host keys, the Forge agent, what runs on the host, reconnects and current limitations.
order: 200
tags: [remote, ssh, agent, gateway]
---

# Remote development

Forge can open a project that lives on another machine, like JetBrains Gateway. It connects over
SSH, installs a small headless **Forge agent** on the host and runs indexing, the PHP language
server, Git, terminals and run configurations **next to the files**. Only the UI runs on your
machine.

## Requirements

| Side | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| Remote host | **Linux** on x86_64 or aarch64, an SSH server, a POSIX shell, write access to `~/.cache`. PHP, Git, Intelephense etc. installed on the host as you would need them locally. |
| Forge | a build that bundles the agents (`pnpm release`), or agent binaries in `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR` / an `agents/` folder next to the `forge` binary. See [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md). |

Nothing needs to be installed on the host in advance: Forge uploads the agent itself.

## Connecting

Welcome screen → **Remote Development** → **New Connection** (or **New SSH Connection…** in
Find Action).

![Remote Development on the Welcome screen](docs/screenshots/remote-welcome.png)

**Step 1 – Connect to SSH**

![New SSH Connection](docs/screenshots/remote-ssh-dialog.png)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| SSH configuration | a saved configuration, a host from `~/.ssh/config` (with `Include`s), or **New connection** |
| Host, Port, Username | |
| Authentication type | **Password**, **Key pair (OpenSSH or PuTTY)** with an optional passphrase, or **OpenSSH config and authentication agent** (ssh-agent plus the `IdentityFile`s of `~/.ssh/config`) |
| Save password / passphrase | stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-ssh`), never in a file |

**Test Connection** shows the host's system and the latency. **Check Connection and Continue**
moves to step 2.

**Step 2 – Choose Project**: browse the host's folders (home, parent, show hidden files) and
double-click the project folder, or type its path, then **Open Project**.

![Choose the project folder](docs/screenshots/remote-folder-chooser.png)

![Project step](docs/screenshots/remote-project-step.png)

### Jump hosts and proxy commands

Hosts from `~/.ssh/config` keep their `ProxyJump` and `ProxyCommand`:

- **ProxyJump**: Forge connects through each hop in turn, tunnelling the next connection
  through the previous one; every hop's host key is checked like the target's.
- **ProxyCommand**: Forge runs the command (with `%h`, `%p`, `%r` and `%n` expanded) and speaks
  SSH over its input and output.

```text
Host shop
    HostName 10.0.0.12
    User deploy
    ProxyJump bastion.example.com
```

### Host keys

Host keys are checked against `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. An **Unknown Host** shows the key type and
fingerprint ("Are you sure you want to continue connecting?"); **Accept New Key** adds it to
`known_hosts`. A **changed** key is reported prominently ("Host Key Has Changed") and must be
confirmed explicitly before the stored key is replaced.

![Fingerprint](docs/screenshots/remote-fingerprint.png)

## The Forge agent

After connecting, Forge probes the host with one shell command (OS, architecture, home folder,
installed agent), uploads the matching agent to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` when it is
missing or differs (checked by SHA-256), and starts it in a login shell. The agent then serves
the project over the SSH channel.

Set `FORGE_AGENT_LOG=debug` in the host's environment for verbose agent logs (stderr).

## Working in a remote project

![Remote project](docs/screenshots/remote-workbench.png)

The project's root is shown as `user@host:/path`. Recent Projects keeps remote projects with an
**SSH** badge; clicking one reconnects.

![Recent remote projects](docs/screenshots/remote-open-recent.png)

| Works on the host | |
| --- | --- |
| Project view, editing, saving, file operations, file watching | yes |
| Go to File, Search Everywhere | yes |
| Git (status, commit, diff, blame, branches, log) | yes; output is parsed locally |
| Find in Files | yes, searched on the host |
| PHP index, Structure, Generate, Intelephense/Phpactor | yes; Intelephense indexes the remote files itself |
| Catalog language servers (TypeScript, YAML, Python, …) | yes: scan, detection and the servers run on the host (install them there) |
| Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine analysis | yes, in the agent; artisan and `bin/console` run on the host |
| LuaForge index | yes |
| Project settings (`.forge/settings.toml`) and other `.forge/` files | yes, read and written on the host |
| Terminal | yes, a shell on the host |
| Run/Debug configurations (run) | yes, processes run on the host |
| Database tools | project data sources connect through an SSH tunnel, see [Database](docs/guide/user/database.md#remote-projects) |
| Xdebug | through a reverse SSH tunnel, see [Xdebug](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#remote-projects) |
| AI Chat (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) | the CLI runs on the host |

![Remote terminal](docs/screenshots/remote-terminal.png)

> **Note:** still local-only, reporting "not available in remote projects yet": WebForge's npm
> tool window and component navigation, StyLua formatting, code hosts (pull requests), the
> Services tool window's project compose files, and HTTP request environments. Installing
> language servers from the settings page is refused (install on the host). The Browser
> Companion opens files of local projects only.

## Connection status and reconnects

The status bar shows the host and latency (pinged every 5 seconds). Click it for the
connection popup.

![Status popup](docs/screenshots/remote-status-popup.png)

When the connection drops, Forge reconnects automatically with a backoff from 1 to 30 seconds
and re-attaches the project ("Reconnecting…", with the next attempt). Host key and
authentication errors stop the retries. **Reconnect to Remote Host** (Find Action) retries now.

![Reconnecting](docs/screenshots/remote-reconnecting.png)

## Saved configurations

Settings | Tools | **SSH Configurations** lists, adds, edits and removes saved configurations.
They are stored in `ssh.toml` in Forge's config folder; secrets stay in the keychain.

![SSH Configurations](docs/screenshots/remote-ssh-settings.png)

## Troubleshooting

See [Troubleshooting: remote agent upload](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#remote-agent-upload).

---
title: AI
description: AI in Forge - model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, any OpenAI-compatible server), AI commit messages, and the AI Chat with Claude Code and Gemini CLI including permission modes.
order: 210
tags: [ai, llm, claude, claude code, gemini, ollama, openai, chat]
---

# AI

AI is part of Forge's core and works with **your own** providers and tools; Forge ships no
credentials and no subscription. There are two parts:

- **AI providers**: language model APIs Forge calls itself, used for AI commit messages and
  available to plugins.
- **AI Chat**: Claude Code or Gemini CLI, installed on your machine with your own login, run
  headless and rendered as a native chat.

## Providers

Settings | Tools | **AI Providers**:

![AI Providers](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-settings.png)

**Add Provider** offers presets:

| Kind | Default base URL | API key | Default model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic (Claude, Messages API) | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` | required (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as fallback) | Forge's current Claude default |
| OpenAI | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | required (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) | `gpt-4.1` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | required (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | not required | pick one |
| LM Studio | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | not required | pick one |
| llama.cpp (`llama-server`) | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | not required | pick one |
| OpenAI-compatible (custom) | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | optional | pick one |

![Add a preset](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-add-preset.png)

For each provider set **Name**, **Base URL**, **API key** and **Default model**. **Fetch
Models** lists the models the server offers (for local servers: "Fetch models from the running
server"). **Test Connection** reports latency and the number of models, or a hint such as "is
Ollama running? Start it with `ollama serve`".

![Test connection](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-test-connection.png)

- API keys are stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-ai`), never in files ("Will be stored
  in the system keychain on Apply"). Without a stored key, the environment variables above are
  used.
- The provider list lives in `ai.toml` in Forge's config folder.
- **Set as Default Provider** chooses the provider used by features without their own choice.
- **Models per feature**: pick the provider/model for **Chat**, **Code completion** ("prefer a
  fast local model") and **Commit messages** separately.

> **Note:** among the features listed under "Models per feature", only AI commit messages use
> a provider on this version; inline code completion and a provider-based chat are not
> implemented yet. The AI Chat uses the agent CLIs below. The "Google Gemini" provider kind
> declared in the AI plugin manifest has no implementation yet; use Gemini through Gemini CLI
> or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## AI commit messages

In the Commit tool window, **Generate Commit Message with AI** writes a message for the ticked
changes. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#ai-commit-messages).

## AI Chat

The **AI Chat** tool window (right stripe, or the ✨ button in the main toolbar) runs an
agentic coding CLI in your project and renders its output as a chat: text, thinking, tool calls
as cards, file edits as diffs, permission questions as buttons. No terminal is involved.

![AI Chat](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-streaming.png)

### Agents

| Agent | Needs | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Claude Code** | the `claude` CLI, logged in (subscription or API key) | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
| **Gemini CLI** | the `gemini` CLI, logged in | `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` |

Pick the agent in the chat header. If the CLI is not found, the chat says "Not installed" with
the install command; set its path in Settings | Tools | **AI Agents** (`agents.<id>.path`;
empty = find it on `PATH`).

![Agent picker](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-agent-picker.png)

![Agents settings](docs/screenshots/settings-ai-agents.png)

### Writing messages

- `Enter` sends, `Shift+Enter` inserts a line break, `Esc` stops the running turn.
- **Attach context** (`@`) attaches the current file, the current selection
  (`file:12-20`), or another open file.
- Slash commands: `/clear` starts a new chat; for Claude Code also `/compact`, `/review`,
  `/init` and `/cost`. `Tab` completes them.
- Suggested prompts appear in an empty chat.

![Attach context](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-attach.png)

### Models and modes

The header has a **Model** and a **Permission mode** selector; defaults come from Settings |
Tools | AI Agents (`agents.<id>.model`, `agents.<id>.permissionMode`).

| Claude Code mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Ask before edits (default) | confirm every edit and command |
| Auto-accept edits | apply file edits without asking; commands still ask |
| Plan mode | explore and plan, no changes |
| Bypass permissions | never ask — trusted projects only |

Gemini CLI cannot ask inside the IDE, so its mode decides which tools it gets:

| Gemini CLI mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only (default) | read and search, no edits or commands |
| Auto-accept edits | edit files without asking, no commands |
| YOLO | edits and commands, never asks |

![Gemini modes](docs/screenshots/gemini-modes.png)

### Permission requests

With Claude Code in "Ask before edits", each edit or command shows a card: **Allow once**,
**Allow for this session** ("Don't ask again for this exact command until the chat ends") or
**Deny**. Edit cards show the diff; **Open diff** opens it in a dialog.

![Permission for a command](docs/screenshots/chat-permission-command.png)

![Edit diff](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-diff-dialog.png)

Files changed by the agent are reloaded in open editor tabs automatically.

### History

**Chat history** lists the previous chats of this Forge session (the list is not kept after a
restart); selecting one resumes the CLI's conversation. **New chat** starts over. The end of a turn shows duration, tokens and cost when
the CLI reports them.

![Finished turn](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-finished.png)

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the agent CLI runs **on the host**: install and log
in to `claude` or `gemini` there. Forge finds the executable on the host and the agent works
next to the files.

## Privacy

Forge sends data only to the providers you configure and the CLIs you run: commit diffs to the
commit message provider, your chat messages and attached context to the agent CLI (which talks
to its own service). Nothing is sent anywhere by default.

---
title: Browser Companion
description: Click a component in your running web app to open its source in Forge, pair the Forge Companion browser extension, and make error pages and dev overlays open files through forge:// links and the forge launcher.
order: 220
tags: [browser, extension, react, vue, angular, svelte, forge links, ignition]
---

# Browser Companion

The Browser Companion (`forge.browser-companion`) connects Forge with the outside world:

- the **Forge Companion** browser extension: click a React, Vue, Angular or Svelte component in
  your running app and its source opens in Forge at the right line;
- **`forge://` links** from error pages (Laravel Ignition, Symfony, Whoops, Xdebug);
- the **`forge` launcher** used by Vite, Vue DevTools and other "open in editor" features.

## The browser extension

![Extension in inspect mode](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-extension.png)

- **Inspect mode**: press `Alt+Shift+F` in the page (or use the toolbar popup), hover to see the
  component and its file, click to open it. `Esc` stops.
- **Alt+Click** opens the component under the cursor directly.
- **Context menu**: "Open Component in Forge", and "Open “…” in Forge" on selected text with a
  `file:line` reference (stack traces, compiler output).
- **Popup**: connection status, pairing, inspect toggle, recently opened files, the Forge port
  and **path mappings** for apps running in Docker or on another machine
  (`/var/www/html => /home/me/shop`).

Supported: Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave 111+ and Firefox 128+ (Manifest V3).

| Framework | Source of the location | Precision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React ≤ 18 (dev) | `_debugSource` from the development JSX transform | element, line and column |
| React 19 (dev) | component name; Forge finds the declaration | component |
| Vue 3 / Vue 2 (dev) | the component's `__file` | component file |
| Angular (`ng serve`) | `ng.getComponent` → class name; Forge finds the class | component class |
| Svelte 4/5 (dev) | `__svelte_meta.loc` | element, line and column |
| Any | `data-source-file`/`data-source-line`, react-dev-inspector, vite-plugin-vue-inspector, code-inspector-plugin attributes | element |

### Installing the extension

The extension is not in the browser stores yet. Build and load it unpacked:

```sh
cd browser-extension
pnpm install
pnpm build            # dist/chrome and dist/firefox
```

- **Chrome, Edge, Brave**: `chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** →
  `browser-extension/dist/chrome`.
- **Firefox**: `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` → **Load Temporary Add-on…** →
  `browser-extension/dist/firefox/manifest.json`, then allow access to `127.0.0.1` in the
  extension's permissions.

### Pairing

1. In Forge open Settings | Tools | **Browser Companion** and click **Pair New Browser…**.
2. Click the Forge icon in the browser toolbar and type the 6-digit code.

![Pairing code](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-pairing.png)

The code works once and expires after five minutes. The browser then keeps a random token;
Forge stores only its SHA-256 hash (in `browser-companion.json` in Forge's config folder) and
lists the browser under **Paired Browsers** with its last use. **Unpair Browser** revokes it
immediately.

![Browser Companion settings](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-settings.png)

### What happens when a file is requested

The request is matched against the open project and your recent projects:

- a file of the **open project** opens right away (and Forge comes to the front, setting
  `browserCompanion.focusWindow`);
- a file of a **recent project** or **outside any project** asks first ("Open the project in
  this window?", **Open Project**, **Open Folder**, **Open File Outside Projects**), because
  links can come from any web page.

![Confirmation](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-confirm.png)

### Security

The built-in server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, port **63342** (`browserCompanion.port`; if it
is taken, for example by PhpStorm, the next nine ports are tried). It accepts requests only with
a loopback `Host`, no web-page `Origin` (extension origins only) and, except for ping and
pairing, a valid token. Turn it off with **Accept open requests from paired browsers**
(`browserCompanion.enabled`).

## Framework integrations

The settings page lists ready-made snippets, the ones for frameworks detected in the open
project first (**Show detected only**). Some have an **Apply** button that writes one variable
into `.env` / `.env.local` ("An existing value of the variable is replaced; nothing else in the
file changes").

![Integrations](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-integrations.png)

| Integration | Setup |
| --- | --- |
| Laravel error page (Ignition) | `.env`: `IGNITION_EDITOR=forge`, plus a `forge` entry in `config/ignition.php` `editor_options` with URL `forge://open?file=%path&line=%line` |
| Symfony error page and profiler | `.env.local`: `SYMFONY_IDE="forge://open?file=%f&line=%l"` (or `framework.ide` in `framework.yaml`) |
| Xdebug | `php.ini`: `xdebug.file_link_format = "forge://open?file=%f&line=%l"` |
| Whoops | `$handler->addEditor('forge', 'forge://open?file=%file&line=%line'); $handler->setEditor('forge');` |
| Vite, Vue DevTools, dev overlays (launch-editor) | `export LAUNCH_EDITOR=forge` (Next.js: `REACT_EDITOR=forge`); the `forge` command must be on your `PATH` |
| React 19, Preact, Solid | a dev-only Babel plugin that adds `data-source-file`/`data-source-line` (shown on the page) |
| Angular | nothing to configure with `ng serve` |

## forge:// links and the launcher

```text
forge://open?file=/home/me/shop/app/Models/User.php&line=42&column=5
forge://open-symbol?name=UserCardComponent&kind=component
```

```sh
forge app/Models/User.php:42
forge --line 42 --column 5 app/Models/User.php
forge app/Models/User.php 42 5
```

The scheme is registered by the installers (and at runtime for AppImages and development
builds). A second launch is forwarded to the running Forge window. Files given on the command
line are trusted and open without asking. Full syntax:
[CLI arguments and forge:// links](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md).

> **Note:** in a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the settings page reads the project's
> frameworks and applies `.env` changes on the host, but files requested by the browser are
> only opened in local projects.

# Reference

Tables derived from Forge's sources. They list everything, including options that exist but are
not applied yet (marked as such).

| Page | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [Keymap](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) | every PHPStorm action with Windows/Linux and macOS shortcuts, plugin actions, implementation status |
| [Main menu](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md) | every main menu entry, menu by menu, with shortcut and status |
| [Settings](docs/guide/reference/settings.md) | every setting key: type, default, scope, Settings page |
| [File types](docs/guide/reference/file-types.md) | bundled and plugin file types, template data languages |
| [Language servers](docs/guide/reference/language-servers.md) | the catalog: servers, commands, install options, licences |
| [CLI arguments and forge:// links](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md) | the `forge` launcher, `forge://open`, the Browser Companion HTTP API |

---
title: Keymap reference
description: Every action of Forge's PHPStorm keymap with its default shortcuts on Windows/Linux and macOS, grouped like PHPStorm's keymap, and whether Forge implements it.
order: 10
tags: [keymap, shortcuts, reference]
---

# Keymap reference

Forge's default keymaps are PHPStorm's (`crates/forge-keymap/data/phpstorm.json`), keyed by
PHPStorm's action ids. This page is the complete list. To learn the shortcuts the way the
JetBrains help teaches them, start with:

- [Keymap reference card](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/reference-card.md): the 60 most important shortcuts
  on one printable page;
- [Shortcuts by topic](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md): one page per area (editing, navigation,
  search, refactoring, run and debug, Git, tool windows, general) that explains every
  implemented action, where it is in the menus, and shows its result;
- [Main menu reference](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md): every menu entry with its shortcut and status;
- [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md): changing shortcuts, chords and focus contexts.

## How to read the tables

Actions are grouped as in Settings | Keymap. The **In Forge** column says whether the action does
something on this version (checked against the commands the UI registers):

- **yes**: implemented;
- **native**: handled by the editor or the operating system (undo, clipboard, caret movement);
- **—**: not implemented yet; the shortcut stays reserved and shows "*Action* is not available
  yet", and its main menu entry is disabled.

Shortcuts marked `Fn+…` in PHPStorm are left out. Several Forge commands implement PHPStorm
actions under another id (aliases): `search.everywhere` → `SearchEverywhere`, `settings.open` →
`ShowSettings`, `run.run` → `Run`, `run.debug` → `Debug`, `run.editConfigurations` →
`editRunConfigurations`, `git.branches` → `Git.Branches`, `git.commit` → `CheckinProject`,
`git.push` → `Vcs.Push`, `git.update` → `Vcs.UpdateProject`, `git.fetch` → `Git.Fetch`,
`git.newBranch` → `Git.CreateNewBranch`, `git.log` → `Vcs.Show.Log`, `git.annotate` →
`Annotate`, `php.generate` → `Generate`, `workspace.open` → `OpenFile`, `workspace.close` →
`CloseProject`, `ExtractVariable` → `IntroduceVariable`. `Exit` exists only in the desktop app.

## Commands without shortcuts

Forge also registers commands that are not PHPStorm actions. They have no default shortcut but
appear in Find Action and can be bound in Settings | Keymap, for example: Show Git Log
(`git.log`), Fetch (`git.fetch`), New Branch… (`git.newBranch`), Show Diff (`git.showDiff`),
Create Merge Request… (`forges.createMergeRequest`), View Pull/Merge Requests
(`forges.showMergeRequests`), Refresh Pull/Merge Requests (`forges.refresh`), Detect Project
Type (`project.redetect`), Reindex PHP Files (`php.reindex`), Generate PHPDoc Comment
(`php.generatePhpDoc`), Reindex Lua Files (`lua.reindex`), Refresh Symfony Index
(`symfony.refresh`), Refresh Doctrine Entities (`doctrine.refresh`), Refresh Services
(`Services.Refresh`), Pull Image… (`Docker.PullImage`), New SSH Connection…
(`Remote.NewSshConnection`), Reconnect to Remote Host (`Remote.Reconnect`), SSH
Configurations… (`remote.settings`), Language Servers… (`langservers.settings`), AI Providers…
(`ai.settings`), Open AI Chat (`AIChat.Focus`), New AI Chat (`AIChat.NewChat`), Browser
Companion Settings (`BrowserCompanion.Settings`), Keymap Settings (`settings.keymap`).

---
title: Main menu reference
description: Every entry of Forge's main menu, menu by menu, with its shortcut, whether it is implemented and what it does.
order: 15
tags: [main menu, reference, menus]
---

# Main menu reference

Forge's main menu has PHPStorm's structure. Open it with the ☰ button or `Alt+\`, or show it as a
menu bar (Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Main menu**); see
[Workbench: Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

Entries Forge has not implemented yet are visible but **disabled**, so the menu doubles as a map
of what is there and what is still to come. Plugins add their own entries (Tools | Docker,
Tools | Laravel, Tools | Symfony, Run | Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections) while they are
active.

| Menu | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [File](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/file.md) | projects, new files and scratches, settings, Save All |
| [Edit](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/edit.md) | undo, clipboard, find and replace, Find in Files, selection, line editing |
| [View](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/view.md) | tool windows, appearance, Parameter Info, Recent Files |
| [Navigate](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/navigate.md) | back/forward, Search Everywhere, Go to Class/File/Symbol/Line, declarations, problems |
| [Code](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/code.md) | completion, Generate, folding, comments, Reformat Code, moving lines |
| [Refactor](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/refactor.md) | refactorings (not implemented yet) |
| [Run](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/run.md) | run configurations, debugging actions, breakpoints, Xdebug listener |
| [Tools](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/tools.md) | terminal, Docker, Laravel, Symfony |
| [Git](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/git.md) | commit, push, update, branches, log, blame |
| [Window](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/window.md) | active tool window, editor tabs |
| [Help](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/help.md) | Find Action, Keymap Reference, About |

The menu structure, labels, mnemonics and enabled states are computed in Rust
(`crates/forge-keymap/src/menu.rs`); an entry is enabled when a command implements its action.
These pages were generated from the menu of the browser-mode Laravel demo project.

# File menu

Projects, new files and scratches, settings and saving. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![File menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-file.png)

| New › Project from Version Control… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |

# Edit menu

Undo, clipboard, find and replace, selection and line editing. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![Edit menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-edit.png)

**Available**: *yes* — implemented; *not yet* — shown disabled until Forge implements it; *dynamic* — filled at runtime. Shortcuts are the Windows/Linux and macOS defaults.

| Entry | Windows / Linux | macOS | Available | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Undo | `Ctrl+Z`, `Alt+Backspace` | `Cmd+Z` | yes | Undoes the last edit in the editor. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Redo | `Ctrl+Shift+Z`, `Alt+Shift+Backspace` | `Cmd+Shift+Z` | yes | Redoes the last undone edit. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Cut | `Ctrl+X`, `Shift+Delete` | `Cmd+X` | yes | Cuts the selection, or the whole line when nothing is selected. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Copy | `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+Insert` | `Cmd+C` | yes | Copies the selection, or the whole line when nothing is selected. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| **Copy Path/Reference** | | | | submenu |
| Copy Path/Reference › Absolute Path | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Shift+C` | yes | Copies the absolute path of the current file. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Copy Path/Reference › File Name | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Copy Path/Reference › Path From Content Root | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Copy Path/Reference › Reference | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+C` | yes | Copies a reference to the caret position (`path:line`). [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Paste | `Ctrl+V`, `Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+V` | yes | Pastes from the clipboard. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| **Paste Special** | | | | submenu |
| Paste Special › Paste from History… | `Ctrl+Shift+V` | `Cmd+Shift+V` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Paste Special › Paste as Plain Text | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+V` | yes | Pastes the clipboard as plain text. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Delete | `Delete` | `Delete`, `Backspace` | yes | Delete |
| **Find** | | | | submenu |
| Find › Find… | `Ctrl+F` | `Cmd+F` | yes | Opens the find panel of the editor for the current file. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-find-in-file.png)) |
| Find › Replace… | `Ctrl+R` | `Cmd+R` | yes | Opens the find panel with the replace field. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file) |
| Find › Find Next / Move to Next Occurrence | `F3` | `Cmd+G` | yes | Moves to the next match of the current search. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file) |
| Find › Find Previous / Move to Previous Occurrence | `Shift+F3` | `Cmd+Shift+G` | yes | Moves to the previous match. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-and-replace-in-a-file) |
| Find › Find Word at Caret | `Ctrl+F3` | `Alt+Cmd+F3` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find › Select All Occurrences | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Cmd+G` | yes | Selects every occurrence of the selected text. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Find › Add Selection for Next Occurrence | `Alt+J` | `Ctrl+G` | yes | Adds the next occurrence of the selected text as another selection (multiple carets). [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Find › Unselect Occurrence | `Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` | yes | Removes the occurrence added last. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Find › Find in Files… | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `Cmd+Shift+F` | yes | Searches the text of all project files, with match case, whole words, regular expressions, file masks and a folder scope. [More](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-find-in-files.png)) |
| Find › Replace in Files… | `Ctrl+Shift+R` | `Cmd+Shift+R` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find › Search Structurally… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| **Find Usages** | | | | submenu |
| Find Usages › Find Usages | `Alt+F7` | `Alt+F7` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find Usages › Find Usages Settings… | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F7` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F7` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find Usages › Show Usages | `Ctrl+Alt+F7` | `Cmd+Alt+F7` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find Usages › Find Usages in File | `Ctrl+F7` | `Cmd+F7` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Find Usages › Highlight Usages in File | `Ctrl+Shift+F7` | `Cmd+Shift+F7` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Select All | `Ctrl+A` | `Cmd+A` | yes | Selects the whole document. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Extend Selection | `Ctrl+W` | `Alt+Up` | yes | Extends the selection to the next larger syntactic unit (word, expression, statement, block). [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |
| Shrink Selection | `Ctrl+Shift+W` | `Alt+Down` | yes | Shrinks the selection back. [More](docs/guide/user/editor.md#editing-actions) |

# Run menu

Run/Debug configurations, debugging actions and breakpoints. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![Run menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-run.png)

**Available**: *yes* — implemented; *not yet* — shown disabled until Forge implements it; *dynamic* — filled at runtime. Shortcuts are the Windows/Linux and macOS defaults.

| Entry | Windows / Linux | macOS | Available | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Run | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` | yes | Runs the configuration selected in the run widget. [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md) |
| Debug | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` | yes | Debugs the selected configuration (Xdebug for PHP, `--inspect` for npm). [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#debugging) |
| Run… | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` | yes | Lists the run configurations to run one; hold `Shift` to debug instead. [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#run-widget) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-run-chooser.png)) |
| Debug… | `Alt+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Alt+D` | yes | Lists the run configurations to debug one. [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#run-widget) |
| Attach to Process… | `Ctrl+Alt+F5` | `Cmd+Alt+F5` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Edit Configurations… | — | — | yes | Opens the Run/Debug Configurations dialog. [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#rundebug-configurations-dialog) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-run-configurations.png)) |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` | yes | Stops the running process or debug session. [More](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#run-tool-window) |
| **Debugging Actions** | | | | submenu |
| Debugging Actions › Step Over | `F8` | `F8` | yes | Executes the current line and stops at the next one. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Step Into | `F7` | `F7` | yes | Steps into the function called on the current line. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Force Step Into | `Alt+Shift+F7` | `Alt+Shift+F7` | yes | Steps into the call even in code that is normally skipped. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Smart Step Into | `Shift+F7` | `Shift+F7` | yes | Steps into the call on the current line (currently like Step Into). [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Step Out | `Shift+F8` | `Shift+F8` | yes | Runs to the end of the current function and stops in the caller. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Run to Cursor | `Alt+F9` | `Alt+F9` | yes | Continues until the line with the caret. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Force Run to Cursor | `Ctrl+Alt+F9` | `Cmd+Alt+F9` | yes | Continues until the caret line, ignoring breakpoints on the way. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Pause Program | — | — | yes | Asks the debugger to pause the script (if the engine supports it). [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Resume Program | `F9` | `Cmd+Alt+R` | yes | Continues until the next breakpoint. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Evaluate Expression… | `Alt+F8` | `Alt+F8` | yes | Evaluates a PHP expression in the current frame. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Quick Evaluate Expression | `Ctrl+Alt+F8` | `Cmd+Alt+F8` | yes | Evaluates the selection or the expression at the caret. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| Debugging Actions › Show Execution Point | `Alt+F10` | `Alt+F10` | yes | Shows the line where the debugger is paused. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| **Toggle Breakpoint** | | | | submenu |
| Toggle Breakpoint › Line Breakpoint | `Ctrl+F8` | `Cmd+F8` | yes | Adds or removes a line breakpoint at the caret. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#breakpoints) |
| Toggle Breakpoint › Temporary Line Breakpoint | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| View Breakpoints… | `Ctrl+Shift+F8` | `Cmd+Shift+F8` | yes | Lists all breakpoints, with conditions and exception breakpoints. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#breakpoints) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-view-breakpoints.png)) |
| Mute Breakpoints | — | — | yes | Turns all breakpoints off temporarily, or on again. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#breakpoints) |
| Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections | — | — | yes | Starts or stops listening for incoming Xdebug connections on port 9003. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#listening-for-connections) |

**Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections** is added by the Xdebug plugin (`forge.xdebug`) in PHP projects; it is a toggle with a check mark while Forge listens.

tags: [main menu, reference, tools]

# Tools menu

Terminal and the tools of plugins (Docker, Laravel, Symfony). Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![Tools menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-tools.png)

**Available**: *yes* — implemented; *not yet* — shown disabled until Forge implements it; *dynamic* — filled at runtime. Shortcuts are the Windows/Linux and macOS defaults.

| Entry | Windows / Linux | macOS | Available | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Run Anything… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Save as Live Template… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Save File as Template… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Open in Terminal | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `Cmd+T` | yes | Opens a new terminal tab (Tools | Open in Terminal). [More](docs/guide/user/terminal.md#tabs) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-terminal.png)) |
| IDE Scripting Console | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| **Docker** | | | | submenu |
| Docker › Pull Image… | — | — | yes | Pulls a Docker image. [More](docs/guide/user/services.md#pulling-images-and-registries) |
| Docker › Refresh Services | — | — | yes | Refreshes the Services tree. [More](docs/guide/user/services.md) |
| **Laravel** | | | | submenu |
| Laravel › Run Artisan Command… | `Ctrl+Shift+X` | `Cmd+Shift+X` | yes | Runs an artisan command of the Laravel project. [More](docs/guide/user/laravel.md#run-artisan-command) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-artisan.png)) |
| Laravel › Show Routes | — | — | yes | Shows the Laravel Routes tool window. [More](docs/guide/user/laravel.md#routes-tool-window) |

## Entries of plugins

Tools collects the actions of active plugins; the screenshot shows a Laravel project.

| Submenu | Entries | Appears in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Docker | Pull Image…, Refresh Services | always (plugin `forge.services`) |
| Laravel | Run Artisan Command… (`Ctrl+Shift+X`), Show Routes | Laravel projects (`forge.laravel`) |
| Symfony | Run Console Command…, Show Routes, Refresh Symfony Index | Symfony projects (`forge.symfony`) |

# Git menu

Commit, push, update, branches, the log and file actions. In projects without Git the menu is called VCS. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![Git menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-git.png)

**Available**: *yes* — implemented; *not yet* — shown disabled until Forge implements it; *dynamic* — filled at runtime. Shortcuts are the Windows/Linux and macOS defaults.

| Entry | Windows / Linux | macOS | Available | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Commit… | `Ctrl+K` | `Cmd+K` | yes | Opens the Commit tool window to commit the selected changes. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#commit-tool-window) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-commit.png)) |
| Push… | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | `Cmd+Shift+K` | yes | Pushes the current branch. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#push-update-and-fetch) |

| Pull… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Fetch | — | — | yes | Fetches all remotes. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#push-update-and-fetch) |

| Rebase… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |

| New Branch… | — | — | yes | Creates a branch from the current one and optionally checks it out. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#branches) |
| New Tag… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Reset HEAD… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Show Git Log | — | — | yes | Opens the Log tab of the Git tool window. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#log) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/docs-git-log.png)) |
| **Uncommitted Changes** | | | | submenu |
| Uncommitted Changes › Shelve Changes… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Uncommitted Changes › Show Shelf | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Uncommitted Changes › Stash Changes… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Uncommitted Changes › Unstash Changes… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Uncommitted Changes › Rollback… | `Ctrl+Alt+Z` | `Cmd+Alt+Z` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Uncommitted Changes › Show Local Changes | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| **Current File** | | | | submenu |
| Current File › Commit File… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Current File › Add | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Current File › Annotate with Git Blame | — | — | yes | Shows Git blame (author and date per line) in the editor gutter. [More](docs/guide/user/git.md#blame) ([screenshot](docs/screenshots/vcs-blame.png)) |
| Current File › Show Diff | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Current File › Compare with Revision… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Current File › Compare with Branch… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Current File › Show History | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |

| Manage Remotes… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Clone… | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| VCS Operations… | `` Alt+` `` | `Ctrl+V` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |

In a project without a Git repository the menu is called **VCS** and offers the version control entries that do not need a repository.

# Window menu

Layouts, the active tool window, editor tabs and project windows. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

![Window menu](docs/screenshots/docs-menu-window.png)

**Available**: *yes* — implemented; *not yet* — shown disabled until Forge implements it; *dynamic* — filled at runtime. Shortcuts are the Windows/Linux and macOS defaults.

| Entry | Windows / Linux | macOS | Available | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Layouts** | | | | submenu |
| Layouts › Store Current Layout as Default | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Layouts › Restore Default Layout | `Shift+F12` | `Shift+F12` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| **Active Tool Window** | | | | submenu |
| Active Tool Window › Hide Active Tool Window | `Shift+Escape` | `Shift+Escape` | yes | Hides the tool window that has the focus and returns to the editor. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Hide Side Tool Windows | — | — | yes | Hides the left and right tool windows. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Jump to Last Tool Window | `F12` | `F12` | yes | Shows and focuses the tool window used last. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Maximize Tool Window | `Ctrl+Shift+'` | `Cmd+Shift+'` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Active Tool Window › Stretch to Left | `Ctrl+Shift+Left` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left` | yes | Makes the focused tool window wider or narrower towards the left. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Stretch to Right | `Ctrl+Shift+Right` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Right` | yes | Makes the focused tool window wider or narrower towards the right. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Stretch to Top | `Ctrl+Shift+Up` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up` | yes | Makes the focused bottom tool window taller. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Stretch to Bottom | `Ctrl+Shift+Down` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` | yes | Makes the focused bottom tool window lower. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Active Tool Window › Close Active Tab | `Ctrl+Shift+F4` | `Cmd+Shift+F4` | yes | Closes the active tab of the focused tool window (Run, Terminal). [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| Hide All Tool Windows | `Ctrl+Shift+F12` | `Cmd+Shift+F12` | yes | Hides all tool windows; press again to bring them back. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#managing-tool-windows) |
| **Editor Tabs** | | | | submenu |
| Editor Tabs › Select Next Tab | `Alt+Right` | `Ctrl+Right`, `Cmd+Shift+]` | yes | Selects the next editor tab. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Select Previous Tab | `Alt+Left` | `Ctrl+Left`, `Cmd+Shift+[` | yes | Selects the previous editor tab. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Pin Tab | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Editor Tabs › Split Right | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Editor Tabs › Split Down | — | — | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Editor Tabs › Goto Next Splitter | — | `Alt+Tab` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Editor Tabs › Goto Previous Splitter | — | `Alt+Shift+Tab` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Editor Tabs › Close Tab | `Ctrl+F4` | `Cmd+W` | yes | Closes the current editor tab. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Close Other Tabs | — | `Cmd+Alt+W` | yes | Closes all editor tabs except the current one. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Close All Tabs | — | — | yes | Closes all editor tabs. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Close Unmodified Tabs | — | — | yes | Closes the editor tabs without unsaved changes. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Editor Tabs › Reopen Closed Tab | — | — | yes | Reopens the editor tab closed last. [More](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#editor-tabs) |
| Next Project Window | `Ctrl+Alt+]` | `` Cmd+` `` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
| Previous Project Window | `Ctrl+Alt+[` | `` Cmd+Shift+` `` | not yet | Not available yet; the entry is disabled. |
