title: Settings reference
description: Every setting key Forge's plugins declare, with type, default, scope and where it appears in the Settings dialog.
order: 20
tags: [settings, reference, configuration]
---

# Settings reference

All settings are declared by plugin manifests (`[[contributions.settings]]` in
`app/src-tauri/plugins/*.toml`) and shown on the Settings page whose id is their `group`. Values
are layered: default < user (`<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`) < project
(`<project>/.forge/settings.toml`). See [Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md).

- **Type**: `bool`, `int`, `number`, `string`, `enum` (allowed values listed), `path` or
  `list` (a list of strings). Ranges are given as (min–max).
- **Scope**: `user` settings are global; `user, project` settings can also be stored per
  project ("For current project" in the dialog).
- *(not applied yet)*: the option is declared and shown, but no code reads it on this version.

Settings written by Forge itself and not declared in a manifest:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `plugins.disabled` | list of disabled plugin ids (Settings \| Plugins) |
| `project.announcedFrameworks` | `<root>#<framework>` pairs whose "project detected" balloon was shown |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.enabled` | per-server toggle on the Language Servers page |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.path` | custom executable of a language server |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.settings` | extra JSON settings of a language server |
| `langservers.hints.dismissed` | servers whose install banner was turned off (also declared below) |

### Appearance & Behavior | Appearance

Page id `appearance`.

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Section | Title and description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appearance.theme` | enum: `dark`, `light`, `solarized-dark`, `solarized-light` | `dark` | user |  | Theme |
| `appearance.uiFont.family` | enum: `Inter`, `system-ui`, `Segoe UI`, `Roboto` | `Inter` | user | Font | Font — Font used for menus, tool windows and dialogs. |
| `appearance.uiFont.size` | int (10–20) | `13` | user | Font | Size |
| `appearance.mainMenu` | enum: `hamburger`, `merged`, `toolbar` | `hamburger` | user | UI Options | Main menu — Hamburger menu: behind the button at the left of the main toolbar. Merged: the menu names in the main toolbar. Separate toolbar: a classic menu bar above the main toolbar. |
| `appearance.compactMode` | bool | `false` | user | UI Options | Compact mode — Reduces paddings and the height of toolbars and tool window headers. |
| `appearance.smoothScrolling` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | UI Options | Smooth scrolling — Animate scrolling in lists and trees. |
| `appearance.showSplash` | bool | `true` | user | UI Options | Show splash screen on startup — The Forge wordmark fills with molten metal while the IDE loads, and offers updates. |
| `appearance.windowControls` | enum: `auto`, `windows`, `macos`, `gnome`, `kde`, `linux`, `native` | `auto` | user | Window | Window controls — Look of the title bar buttons of the main window and dialogs. "Native" lets the operating system draw the title bar. |
| `appearance.showToolWindowBars` | bool | `true` | user | Tool Windows | Show tool window bars — The stripes with tool window buttons along the window edges. |
| `appearance.showToolWindowNumbers` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Tool Windows | Show tool window numbers |
| `projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick` | bool | `true` | user | Project View | Open files with single click — In the Project tool window a single click opens files and expands folders. Turn it off to select with a single click and open with a double click, like PHPStorm. |

### Appearance & Behavior | System Settings

Page id `system`.

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Section | Title and description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system.reopenLastProject` | bool | `true` | user | Project | Reopen projects on startup — the last local project, when Forge starts without a project argument |
| `system.confirmExit` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Project | Confirm before exiting the IDE |
| `system.openProjectIn` | enum: `new`, `same`, `ask` | `ask` | user *(not applied yet)* | Project | Open project in |
| `system.defaultProjectDirectory` | path | `~/Projects` | user | Project | Default project directory — New projects are created here unless you pick another location. |
| `system.autosave.onFrameDeactivation` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Autosave | Save files if the IDE is switched to a different application |
| `system.autosave.onIdle` | bool | `false` | user *(not applied yet)* | Autosave | Save files if the IDE is idle |
| `system.autosave.idleSeconds` | int (1–600) | `15` | user *(not applied yet)* | Autosave | Idle time (seconds) |
| `system.syncExternalChanges` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Synchronization | Synchronize external changes when switching to the IDE window |

### Appearance & Behavior | System Settings | Updates

Page id `system.updates`. The page also shows whether this build can update, the current
version, the last check, **Check Now** and a skipped version with **Offer Again** (stored in
`updates.json`, see [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)).

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Section | Title and description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `updates.checkOnStartup` | bool | `true` | user | Automatic Checks | Check for updates on startup — The splash screen checks at most once a day. Help \| Check for Updates… checks at any time. |
| `updates.channel` | enum: `stable`, `beta` | `stable` | user | Automatic Checks | Update channel — Beta also offers pre-releases. |
| `updates.endpoint` | string | `""` | user | Advanced | Update feed URL — The latest.json of the update feed. Empty: the GitHub releases of Forge for the selected channel. Updates must be signed with the key this build was made with. |

### Keymap

Page id `keymap`. The override lists are edited through the Keymap page, not as text.

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Section | Title and description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keymap.active` | enum: `auto`, `$default`, `macOS` | `auto` | user |  | Keymap |
| `keymap.overrides.default` | list | `[]` | user |  | Changed shortcuts (Windows / Linux) — One entry per action: the action id, then its shortcuts, separated by tabs. |
| `keymap.overrides.macOS` | list | `[]` | user |  | Changed shortcuts (macOS) — One entry per action: the action id, then its shortcuts, separated by tabs. |

### Editor | General

| `editor.softWraps` | bool | `false` | user | Soft Wraps | Soft-wrap files — Wrap long lines visually in files matching the patterns below. |
| `editor.softWrapFiles` | string | `*.md; *.txt; *.rst; *.adoc` | user | Soft Wraps | File patterns |
| `editor.showWhitespace` | bool | `false` | user | Appearance | Show whitespaces |
| `editor.showLineNumbers` | bool | `true` | user | Appearance | Show line numbers |
| `editor.highlightCurrentLine` | bool | `true` | user | Appearance | Highlight caret row |

| `editor.ensureNewlineAtEof` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | On Save | Ensure every saved file ends with a line break |
| `run.console.softWrap` | bool | `false` | user | Console | Use soft wraps in console |
| `run.console.cycleBufferKb` | int (100–100000) | `1024` | user *(not applied yet)* | Console | Override console cycle buffer size (KB) |

| `vcs.git.updateMethod` | enum: `merge`, `rebase`, `branchDefault` | `merge` | user *(not applied yet)* |  | Update method |
| `vcs.git.autoFetch` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* |  | Fetch remotes automatically |
| `vcs.git.commit.subjectMaxLength` | int (20–200) | `72` | user *(not applied yet)* | Commit Message Inspections | Limit subject line length |
| `vcs.git.commit.blankLineAfterSubject` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Commit Message Inspections | Require blank line between subject and body |
| `vcs.git.commit.bodyRightMargin` | int (40–200) | `72` | user *(not applied yet)* | Commit Message Inspections | Right margin for body (columns) |
| `vcs.git.commit.warnOnCrlf` | bool | `true` | user *(not applied yet)* | Commit | Warn if CRLF line separators are about to be committed |
| `vcs.git.commit.signOff` | bool | `false` | user *(not applied yet)* | Commit | Sign-off commits |

# File types reference

Detection order: file names and path patterns, then the longest matching extension, then the
interpreter of a `#!` line. File names may contain `*` anywhere and `/` to match a path suffix
(`config/services*.yaml`). Bundled types indent with 4 spaces unless a plugin type says
otherwise. See [File types and syntax highlighting](docs/guide/user/file-types.md).

## Bundled file types

| Id | Name (status bar) | Extensions | File names | Template |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `php` | PHP | `.php`, `.phtml`, `.inc` |  |  |
| `blade` | Blade | `.blade.php` |  |  |
| `json` | JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, `.lock`, `.webmanifest`, `.geojson`, `.har` | `.prettierrc`, `.babelrc`, `.eslintrc`, `composer.lock`, `.php-cs-fixer.cache` |  |
| `yaml` | YAML | `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.neon` |  |  |
| `sql` | SQL | `.sql`, `.ddl` |  |  |
| `markdown` | Markdown | `.md`, `.markdown` |  |  |
| `javascript` | JavaScript | `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.es6` |  |  |
| `jsx` | JavaScript React | `.jsx` |  |  |
| `typescript` | TypeScript | `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts` |  |  |
| `tsx` | TypeScript React | `.tsx` |  |  |
| `css` | CSS | `.css`, `.pcss`, `.postcss` |  |  |

## Template data languages

Template types (marked *Template* above) highlight the content between their tags in a data
language: `html` (default), `xml`, `latex`, `css`, `scss`, `less`, `javascript`, `typescript`,
`json`, `sql`, `yaml`, `ini`, `shell`, `go`, `text`.

Chosen from the setting `templates.dataLanguages` (`pattern=language` entries), then from a
compound file name, then HTML. Compound inner extensions:

| Inner extension | Data language |
| --- | --- |
| `html`, `htm`, `xhtml` | HTML |
| `xml`, `svg`, `rss`, `atom` | XML |
| `tex`, `latex`, `sty`, `cls` | LaTeX |
| `css` / `scss` / `less` | CSS / SCSS / Less |
| `js`, `mjs` | JavaScript |
| `ts` | TypeScript |
| `json` | JSON |
| `sql` | SQL |
| `yml`, `yaml` | YAML |
| `ini`, `env`, `conf` | INI / Properties |
| `sh` | Shell Script |
| `go` | Go |
| `txt`, `md`, `csv`, `eml` | Plain text |

Example: `invoice.tex.twig` → LaTeX, `report.sql.twig` → SQL, `style.css.tpl` → CSS.

## Soft wraps

Files matching `editor.softWrapFiles` (default `*.md; *.txt; *.rst; *.adoc`) are soft-wrapped
when `editor.softWraps` is on.

title: Language servers reference
description: The catalog of language servers Forge knows - languages, commands, install options, licences and start conditions.

# Language servers reference

Generated from `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml` and `pack_servers.toml`. Servers are
grouped as on Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers. See
[Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) for how detection, installation and per-server
settings work.

- **Install**: npm commands (`npm install -g …`) become managed installs into Forge's server
  folder, never global ones; Forge downloads Node.js itself when none (>= 18) is installed.
  Commands with `sudo` are only shown for you to run. Links are download pages.
- **Alternative group**: only the first enabled and installed server of a group starts.
- **Needs plugin**: the server starts only while that plugin is enabled and active.
- The PHP servers are started by the PHP pack (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP), not by
  the catalog.

## Servers

### JavaScript & TypeScript

| Server | Id | Languages | Command | Install | Licence | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [TypeScript Language Server](https://github.com/typescript-language-server/typescript-language-server) | `typescript-language-server` | TypeScript, JavaScript | `typescript-language-server --stdio` | `npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript`<br>`brew install typescript-language-server` (macos, linux)<br>`sudo pacman -S typescript-language-server` (linux) | MIT | alternative group `typescript`; needs plugin `forge.web`; Uses the project's TypeScript (node_modules) or a global one. Serves .vue files too when the Vue language server is installed (hybrid mode). |
| [vtsls](https://github.com/yioneko/vtsls) | `vtsls` | TypeScript, JavaScript | `vtsls --stdio` | `npm install -g @vtsls/language-server` | MIT | alternative group `typescript`; needs plugin `forge.web`; Alternative to typescript-language-server built on VS Code's TypeScript extension. Starts only when typescript-language-server is missing or disabled. |
| [ESLint](https://github.com/hrsh7th/vscode-langservers-extracted) | `vscode-eslint-language-server` | JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue, Svelte, Astro | `vscode-eslint-language-server --stdio` | `npm install -g vscode-langservers-extracted`<br>`brew install vscode-langservers-extracted` (macos, linux) | MIT | needs plugin `forge.web`; only when the project has files `eslint.config.*`, `.eslintrc*` or packages `eslint`; Starts in projects with an ESLint configuration or an eslint dependency. |

## Languages

Languages the catalog detects in a project (the project scan reads up to
`langservers.scanLimit` files, skipping ignored files, `node_modules` and `vendor`).

| Language id | Name | Extensions | File names |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `javascript` | JavaScript | `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx` |  |
| `typescript` | TypeScript | `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx` |  |
| `vue` | Vue | `.vue` |  |
| `svelte` | Svelte | `.svelte` |  |
| `astro` | Astro | `.astro` |  |
| `html` | HTML | `.html`, `.htm`, `.xhtml` |  |
| `css` | CSS | `.css` |  |
| `scss` | SCSS | `.scss` |  |
| `less` | Less | `.less` |  |
| `json` | JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5` | `.babelrc`, `.eslintrc`, `.prettierrc` |
| `yaml` | YAML | `.yml`, `.yaml` |  |
| `toml` | TOML | `.toml` | `Cargo.lock`, `Pipfile` |
| `xml` | XML | `.xml`, `.xsd`, `.xsl`, `.xslt`, `.wsdl`, `.xliff`, `.xlf`, `.svg` | `phpunit.xml.dist`, `phpcs.xml.dist`, `psalm.xml.dist` |
| `markdown` | Markdown | `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx` |  |
| `dockerfile` | Dockerfile | `.dockerfile` | `Dockerfile`, `Containerfile` |
| `dockercompose` | Docker Compose |  | `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, `compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.override.yml`, `docker-compose.override.yaml` |
| `shellscript` | Shell Script | `.sh`, `.bash`, `.ksh`, `.zsh` | `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.profile` |

| `twig` | Twig | `.twig` |  |

| `python` | Python | `.py`, `.pyi`, `.pyw` |  |

| `java` | Java | `.java` |  |
| `csharp` | C# | `.cs`, `.csx` |  |
| `ruby` | Ruby | `.rb`, `.rake`, `.gemspec`, `.ru`, `.erb` | `Gemfile`, `Rakefile`, `Guardfile` |
| `kotlin` | Kotlin | `.kt`, `.kts` |  |
| `zig` | Zig | `.zig`, `.zon` |  |
| `php` | PHP | `.php`, `.phtml` |  |
| `php` | PHP | `.php`, `.phtml` |  |

---
title: CLI arguments and forge:// links
description: Command-line forms of the forge launcher, the forge://open and forge://open-symbol links, and the Browser Companion's local HTTP API.
order: 50
tags: [cli, launcher, forge links, deep links, reference]
---

# CLI arguments and forge:// links

## The `forge` launcher

```text
forge [PROJECT_DIR | FILE[:LINE[:COLUMN]] | forge://…] …
```

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `forge` | start with the Welcome screen |
| `forge ~/Projects/shop` | open a directory as the project |
| `forge src/App.tsx` | open a file (in the project it belongs to) |
| `forge src/App.tsx:12` / `forge src/App.tsx:12:3` | at line 12 (column 3) |
| `forge --line 12 --column 3 src/App.tsx` | JetBrains style; short `-l`, `-c` |
| `forge src/App.tsx 12 3` | `launch-editor` style: numbers after a file are its line and column |
| `forge 'forge://open?file=…&line=…'` | a link (treated like a link from a web page) |

- Relative paths are resolved against the current directory. Arguments that name nothing on
  disk are skipped with a warning (in the log).
- Other options starting with `-` are ignored.
- If Forge is already running, the arguments are handed to the running window
  (single instance) and the new process exits.
- Files given on the command line are **trusted**: they open without a confirmation, also
  outside known projects.
- Log output: set `RUST_LOG` (e.g. `RUST_LOG=debug forge`).

The deb and rpm packages put `forge` on the `PATH`. For the AppImage, create a link yourself,
e.g. `ln -s ~/Applications/Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/forge`.

## forge:// links

Registered as a URL scheme by the installers; AppImages and development builds register it when
they start (Linux, Windows).

### `forge://open`

```text
forge://open?file=/home/me/shop/app/Models/User.php&line=42&column=5
```

| Parameter | Aliases | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `path`, `url` | absolute path, `file://` URL, or a path relative to `project` (required) |
| `line` | `l` | 1-based line |
| `column` | `col`, `c` | 1-based column |
| `project` | | project root for relative paths |
| `symbol` | | symbol to locate when no line is given |

`forge:open?…` (without `//`) works too. Values are percent-decoded. Absurd line/column numbers
and over-long paths are rejected.

### `forge://open-symbol`

```text
forge://open-symbol?name=UserCardComponent&kind=component
```

Finds the declaration of a component (`kind=component`) or class (`kind=class`) by name in the
open and recent projects and opens it.

### Confirmation

Links can come from any web page, so files outside the open project ask first: a file of a
recent project offers to open that project; a file outside any project asks before it opens.

## Browser Companion HTTP API

A small HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:63342` (or the next nine ports; setting
`browserCompanion.port`) serves the browser extension:

| Request | Body | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/forge/ping` | — | none |
| `POST /api/forge/pair` | `{ "code": "123456", "name": "Chrome" }` → token | none (one-time code) |
| `POST /api/forge/open` | `{ "file", "line"?, "column"?, "project"?, "symbol"? }` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| `POST /api/forge/open-symbol` | `{ "name", "kind"? }` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |

Requests need a loopback `Host` header and no web-page `Origin` (browser extension origins
only). Pairing codes are 6 digits, valid for five minutes and for one use. See
[Browser Companion](docs/guide/user/browser-companion.md).

---
title: Config, cache and data locations
description: Where Forge stores user settings, project files, caches, language servers, scratches and secrets on Linux, macOS and Windows.
order: 60
tags: [files, paths, config, cache, keychain, reference]
---

# Config, cache and data locations

Forge uses the platform's standard folders (Rust's `dirs` crate):

| Placeholder | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<config dir>` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config` | `~/Library/Application Support` | `%APPDATA%` (`C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming`) |
| `<cache dir>` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` | `~/Library/Caches` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%` |
| `<data dir>` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share` | `~/Library/Application Support` | `%APPDATA%` |

## User configuration — `<config dir>/forge/`

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.toml` | user settings (including keymap changes and disabled plugins) |
| `recent-projects.json` | the Welcome screen's recent projects |
| `ai.toml` | AI providers and model choices (no keys) |
| `forges.toml` | GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo accounts (no tokens) |
| `ssh.toml` | saved SSH configurations (no passwords) |
| `dataSources.toml` | global database data sources (no passwords) |
| `browser-companion.json` | paired browsers (SHA-256 hashes of their tokens only) |
| `dialog-windows.json` | size and position of dialog windows |
| `updates.json` | update checks: time of the last check, the skipped version and a postponed ("Later") version |
| `scratches/` | scratch files and buffers |
| `scratches.json` | per-scratch options (the data source of SQL scratches) |

## Caches — `<cache dir>/forge/`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `php-index/<project>-<hash>.json` | PHP index cache per project |
| `intelephense/` | Intelephense's storage (`storagePath`) |
| `jdtls/…` | workspace data of the Java language server |

Caches can be deleted at any time; Forge rebuilds them. Without a platform cache folder the PHP
index falls back to `<project>/.forge/cache/php-index.json`.

## Data — `<data dir>/forge/`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `langservers/` | language servers installed by Forge (`node_modules/.bin`, `package.json`, `.forge-update-check.json`) |
| `runtimes/node-<version>/` | the Node.js build Forge downloaded for language servers (only when no Node.js 18+ was installed) |

## In the project — `<project>/.forge/`

| File | Content | Commit? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.toml` | project settings ("For current project") | yes |
| `runConfigurations.toml` | shared run configurations ("Store as project file") | yes |
| `runConfigurations.local.toml` | local run configurations, the selection, templates | no |
| `breakpoints.json` | Xdebug breakpoints | optional |
| `php-servers.json` | PHP servers and path mappings | yes |
| `dataSources.toml` | project data sources (no passwords) | yes |

Add `.forge/runConfigurations.local.toml` (and `.forge/cache/` if it appears) to your
`.gitignore`. In the project root, `http-client.env.json` and `http-client.private.env.json` are
read by the [HTTP client](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md#environments).

## Secrets — the OS keychain

Secrets are stored with the system keychain (Secret Service/GNOME Keyring/KWallet on Linux,
Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows), never in files:

| Service | Account | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forge-ai` | provider id | AI provider API key |
| `forge-lsp` | `intelephense` | Intelephense licence key |
| `forge-forges` | account id | GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo token |
| `forge-ssh` | SSH configuration id | SSH password or key passphrase |
| `forge-db` | data source id | database password |
| `forge-containers` | `registry:<server>` | Docker registry password |

## Remote hosts

| Path on the host | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` | the uploaded Forge agent |
| `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (local) | host keys you accepted |

## WebView data

The desktop app's WebView keeps its own storage in the app's data folder (identifier
`dev.forge.ide`, e.g. `~/.local/share/dev.forge.ide` on Linux). Forge keeps only conveniences
there (the last theme while settings load); everything that matters is in the files above.

## Clean slate

To reset Forge completely, quit it and delete `<config dir>/forge`, `<cache dir>/forge` and
`<data dir>/forge`, and remove the `forge-*` entries from your keychain.

# Environment variables

## Read by Forge

### Forge's own

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_GIT` | git executable to use instead of `git` on the `PATH` (e.g. a bundled git on Windows) |
| `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR` | folder with the remote agent binaries (`forge-remote-agent-<arch>-linux[.gz]`), searched before the bundle's `agents/` folder |
| `FORGE_AGENT_LOG` | log filter of the remote agent on the host (e.g. `debug`); the agent logs to stderr |
| `RUST_LOG` | log filter of the desktop app (e.g. `RUST_LOG=forge_lsp=debug`; `forge_app_lib::startup=debug` logs the splash steps) |
| `FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE` | e.g. `0.2.0`: the splash and Help \| Check for Updates… offer this version as a simulated update with a fake download; nothing is installed (for development, works in any build) |
| `APPIMAGE` | set by the AppImage runtime; Forge then registers the `forge://` scheme at startup |
| `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN` | read by the AppImage runtime: `1` runs without FUSE (see [Installation](docs/guide/getting-started/installation.md#running-the-appimage-without-fuse)) |

### Credentials (fallbacks when nothing is stored in the keychain)

| Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic provider |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI provider |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter provider |
| `GITLAB_TOKEN` | gitlab.com |
| `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN` | Forgejo / Gitea (public servers) |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` | github.com |

### Tools and environment

| Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `PATH`, `PATHEXT` | finding git, php, composer, node, language servers, agent CLIs |
| `SHELL` | the terminal's default shell (Linux/macOS) |
| `ComSpec` | the last-resort terminal shell on Windows |
| `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA` | home and config folders |
| `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` | npm's global folder when looking for language servers |
| `VIMRUNTIME` | Neovim runtime for lua-language-server's Neovim environment |
| `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT` | the Docker daemon (also `ssh://` hosts) or Docker context when `docker.connection` is `auto` |
| `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` | rootless Docker socket |
| `KUBECONFIG` | kubeconfig when `kubernetes.kubeconfig` is empty |
| `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` | kept if set; otherwise Forge runs git with `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` |
| `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `KDE_FULL_SESSION`, `GNOME_DESKTOP_SESSION_ID` | detecting the desktop for "Window controls: Match the system" |
| `USER`, `USERNAME`, `HOSTNAME` | default values (SSH user, display names) |

## Set by Forge for processes it starts

| Variable | When |
| --- | --- |
| `XDEBUG_MODE=debug`, `XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE`, `XDEBUG_CONFIG=client_host=127.0.0.1 client_port=<port> idekey=FORGE`, `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<server>` | Debug of a PHP run configuration |
| `NODE_OPTIONS=<web.npm.debugArguments>` | Debug of an npm script |
| the entries of `terminal.environment` | new terminal tabs |
| the configuration's **Environment variables** | run configurations |
| `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -o BatchMode=yes` | git commands, unless already set |

## Build and development

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` | `cargo test -p forge-app` rewrites the browser-mode snapshots of the plugin manifests and project generators |
| `FORGE_URL` | base URL of the dev server for `scripts/screenshots.mjs` (default `http://localhost:1420`) |
| `CHROMIUM_PATH` | Chromium for the screenshot script |
| `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` | separate target folder per git worktree |
| `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` | smaller debug builds |
| `CC_<triple>`, `CFLAGS_<triple>`, `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER` | cross-compiling the remote agents (`pnpm agents`) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` | at build time: the updater public key compiled into the app; without it the build never checks for updates (see [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#updates-and-signing)) |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | at build time: sign the updater artifacts; `pnpm tauri build` / `pnpm release` turn on `createUpdaterArtifacts` only when the key is set |

# Plugins reference

Generated from the manifests in `app/src-tauri/plugins/*.toml`. A plugin is active when it is
enabled (Settings | Plugins) and, if it lists project types, when the open project uses one of
them (a language, framework, pack or tool id from
[project detection](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md)). Disabling a plugin also disables
the plugins that depend on it.

Pack ids: `core`, `phpforge`, `webforge`, `luaforge`, and `scriptforge` / `configforge` for the
script and config language plugins.

| Plugin | Id | Pack | Depends on | Active for (project types) | Contributes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser Companion | `forge.browser-companion` | core |  | always | 1 commands; 3 settings |
| GitLab, Forgejo and GitHub | `forge.code-hosts` | core | `forge.git` | always | tool windows: Pull Requests; 2 commands; 2 settings |
| Forge Platform (required) | `forge.core` | core |  | always | tool windows: Project; 2 commands; 49 settings; 3 keybindings |
| Database Tools and SQL | `forge.database` | core |  | always | tool windows: Database; 2 commands; 3 settings |
| Git | `forge.git` | core |  | always | tool windows: Commit, Git; 2 commands; 8 settings; 1 keybindings |
| Bash | `forge.bash` | scriptforge |  | always | file types: Shell Script |
| Python | `forge.python` | scriptforge |  | always | file types: Python |
| YAML | `forge.yaml` | configforge |  | always | file types: YAML |
| JSON | `forge.json` | configforge |  | always | file types: JSON |
| .env | `forge.dotenv` | configforge |  | always | file types: Dotenv |
| Ignore Files | `forge.ignore` | configforge |  | always | file types: Ignore File |
| Docker | `forge.docker` | configforge |  | always | file types: Dockerfile, Docker Compose |
| Postfix | `forge.postfix` | configforge |  | always | file types: Postfix main.cf, Postfix master.cf |
| E-Mail | `forge.eml` | configforge |  | always | file types: E-Mail |
| INI | `forge.ini` | configforge |  | always | file types: INI |
| Config Files | `forge.conf` | configforge |  | always | file types: Config |
| Language Servers | `forge.langservers` | core | `forge.core` | always | 1 commands; 9 settings |
| Lua | `forge.lua` | luaforge |  | `luaforge` | 1 commands; 6 settings; file types: Lua; 1 LSP servers; run types: Lua Script |
| AI Assistant | `forge.ai` | core |  | always | tool windows: AI Chat; 3 AI providers; 1 chat agents; 2 code generators |
| Claude Code | `forge.claude-code` | core | `forge.ai` | always | 3 settings; 1 AI providers; 1 chat agents |
| Gemini CLI | `forge.gemini-cli` | core | `forge.ai` | always | 3 settings; 1 AI providers; 1 chat agents |
| PHP | `forge.php` | phpforge |  | `php` | 1 commands; 18 settings; 1 LSP servers; run types: PHP Script, PHP Built-in Web Server; 4 code generators |
| Composer | `forge.composer` | phpforge | `forge.php` | `composer` | 2 commands; 5 settings; run types: Composer Script |
| PHPUnit | `forge.phpunit` | phpforge | `forge.php` | `phpunit`, `pest` | run types: PHPUnit; 1 code generators |
| Xdebug | `forge.xdebug` | phpforge | `forge.php` | `php` | tool windows: Debug; 1 commands; 8 settings; run types: PHP Remote Debug; 1 main menu entries |
| Laravel | `forge.laravel` | phpforge | `forge.php`, `forge.composer` | `laravel` | tool windows: Routes; 1 commands; 6 settings; run types: Artisan; 1 code generators; 1 keybindings; 1 main menu entries |
| Symfony | `forge.symfony` | phpforge | `forge.php`, `forge.composer` | `symfony` | tool windows: Symfony; 2 commands; 7 settings; 1 main menu entries |
| Symfony Services | `forge.symfony-services` | phpforge | `forge.yaml` | `symfony` | file types: Symfony Services |
| Doctrine | `forge.doctrine` | phpforge | `forge.php` | `doctrine` | tool windows: Doctrine; 1 commands; 6 settings |
| Run/Debug | `forge.run` | core |  | always | tool windows: Run; 3 commands; 2 settings; run types: Shell Script |
| Docker and Kubernetes | `forge.services` | core |  | always | tool windows: Services; 2 commands; 15 settings; 1 main menu entries |
| Terminal | `forge.terminal` | core |  | always | tool windows: Terminal; 1 commands; 7 settings; 1 keybindings |
| HTML, CSS & JavaScript | `forge.web` | webforge |  | `webforge` | tool windows: npm; 2 commands; 4 settings; 3 LSP servers; run types: npm |
| React | `forge.react` | webforge | `forge.web` | `react`, `next` |  |
| Vue.js | `forge.vue` | webforge | `forge.web` | `vue`, `nuxt` | 1 LSP servers |
| Angular | `forge.angular` | webforge | `forge.web` | `angular` | 1 settings; 1 LSP servers |

> **Note:** some contributions are declared ahead of their implementation: the "PHP Built-in
> Web Server" and "PHP Remote Debug" run configuration types, the "Google Gemini" AI provider
> kind, the "Assistant" chat agent and the AI code generators ("Tests with AI", "Documentation
> with AI"), the PHPUnit "Test Method" and Laravel "Eloquent Model" generators, and the commands
> `composer.install`, `composer.update` and `php.runFile` have no implementation on this
> version.

# Developer guide

Forge is a Rust + Tauri 2 desktop application with a SolidJS + TypeScript + CodeMirror 6 UI.
These pages explain how the code is organized and how to extend it. The binding rules for
humans and coding agents are in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md); step-by-step recipes are the
skills in [`.claude/skills/`](.claude/skills); the detailed IPC contracts are in
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

---
title: Architecture overview
description: How Forge is put together - the Tauri shell, Rust crates and packs, the SolidJS UI, IPC, project backends, browser mode and plugins.
order: 10
tags: [architecture, tauri, rust, solidjs, ipc]
---

# Architecture overview

This page is the map. [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) is the detailed contract
(every IPC command and event, payload shapes, conventions per area); read it before larger
changes.

```text
┌──────────────────────────── Forge desktop app (one native binary) ───────────────────────────┐
│  SolidJS UI (app/ui) ── WebView ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│    features/<name>/  register tool windows, commands, settings pages, editor extensions …    │
│    src/ipc/          typed clients ──invoke/listen──┐                                         │
│                                                      ▼                                        │
│  Tauri shell (app/src-tauri)   commands/<area>.rs  (thin: parse args, call crates, emit)      │
│                                                      │                                        │
│  Rust crates (crates/forge-*)  core, plugin-api, lsp, vcs, keymap, fuzzy, filetypes, ai, …    │
│  Packs (packs/<pack>/<plugin>) phpforge, webforge, luaforge                                   │
│                                                      │                                        │
│  forge-backend: Backend trait ── LocalBackend (this machine)                                  │
│                              └─ RemoteBackend ──SSH── forge-remote-agent on a Linux host      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Layers

**The shell** (`app/src-tauri`, crate `forge-app`, binary `forge`) creates the window, holds
the application state, registers IPC commands (`src/commands/<area>.rs`, listed in
`src/lib.rs`) and forwards events. It is kept thin: it parses arguments, calls library crates and
emits events. Built-in plugin manifests are TOML files in `app/src-tauri/plugins/`.

**Rust crates** (`crates/forge-*`) hold the logic: workspace and settings (`forge-core`), the
plugin contract (`forge-plugin-api`), project detection and generators (`forge-project`), LSP
client (`forge-lsp`) and server catalog (`forge-langservers`), git (`forge-vcs`), code hosts
(`forge-forges`), AI providers and agent CLIs (`forge-ai`, `forge-agent-cli`), processes and run
output (`forge-process`, `forge-output`), the debugger (`forge-debug`), databases (`forge-db`,
`forge-sql`), containers (`forge-containers`), the keymap engine (`forge-keymap`), fuzzy search
(`forge-fuzzy`), file types (`forge-filetypes`), remote development (`forge-backend`,
`forge-remote`, `forge-remote-agent`) and more. Each crate has its own unit tests.

**Packs** (`packs/<pack>/<plugin>`) are language and framework crates: PHPForge (`lang-php`,
`fw-laravel`, `fw-symfony`, `orm-doctrine`, `dql`), WebForge (`lang-web`, `fw-react`,
`fw-vue`, `fw-angular`), LuaForge (`lang-lua`). They depend on core crates, never on the app.

**The UI** (`app/ui`, SolidJS + TypeScript + CodeMirror 6, icons from `lucide-solid`) renders
and forwards events. A feature is a folder `src/features/<name>/` whose `index.ts` registers its
contributions (tool windows, commands, settings pages, editor extensions, …); see
[Contribution points](docs/guide/developer/contribution-points.md).

## IPC

The UI calls Rust with `invoke("<command>", args)` and subscribes to events with
`listen("<area>://<event>")`, always through a typed client in `app/ui/src/ipc/<area>.ts`.
Commands return `forge_core::Result<T>`; errors arrive as strings. Long work streams progress
as events (`run://<id>`, `lsp://diagnostics`, `agent://<session>`, …). See
[IPC commands and browser mocks](docs/guide/developer/ipc-and-mocks.md).

## Browser mode

The whole UI also runs in a plain browser (`pnpm dev`): every IPC command has a mock in
`app/ui/src/mock/`, and pure Rust crates run as WebAssembly (`crates/forge-wasm`) so the mocks
do not duplicate logic. Demo projects make every feature explorable and screenshot-able. See
[The WebAssembly bridge](docs/guide/developer/wasm-bridge.md).

## Plugins

Plugins declare contributions as data in TOML manifests: commands, keybindings, tool windows,
typed settings, file types, LSP servers, run configuration types, AI providers, chat agents and
code generators (`forge_plugin_api::Contributions`). `PluginRegistry` tracks enablement
(cascading over `depends`). Plugins with `projectTypes` activate only for projects that use
them. Browser mode reads a snapshot of the manifests, `app/ui/src/mock/builtinPlugins.json`. See
[Writing a plugin or pack](docs/guide/developer/plugins-and-packs.md).

## Settings

Layered settings (defaults < user `settings.toml` < project `.forge/settings.toml`) with a schema
from the manifests; the UI reads them with `getSetting(key)`, Rust with
`read_settings().get_as::<T>(key)`; changes are broadcast as `settings://changed`. Secrets go to
the OS keychain. See [Settings](docs/guide/developer/settings.md).

## Project backends and remote development

Every project command goes through the open project's `forge_backend::Backend`: files, search,
git, watching, terminals, processes, language server launching, the PHP index, Find in Files,
framework analysis (`framework(FrameworkCall)` for Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine), catalog
language server planning (`langservers`), executable lookup (`find_executable`, used for the AI
agent CLIs) and SSH port forwarding (`tunnels()`, used for database tunnels and the Xdebug
reverse tunnel). Project `.forge/` files go through `forge_core::ProjectFiles`.
`LocalBackend` serves a local folder; `RemoteBackend` talks to `forge-remote-agent` over SSH
with a length-prefixed MessagePack protocol (calls, events and byte channels; protocol 2). The
few features that still only work locally (WebForge sources, StyLua, code hosts, Docker
services, HTTP scratch environments) use `AppState::with_workspace`, which fails for remote
projects with "not available in remote projects yet".

## Keymap

The keymap engine is Rust (`forge-keymap`): PHPStorm's default keymaps, overrides from
settings, conflicts and a resolver state machine for chords, double taps and focus contexts.
The UI captures key events and runs the resolved action. The resolver runs synchronously as
WebAssembly in both desktop and browser mode because `preventDefault` must be decided before the
handler returns. See [Keymap actions](docs/guide/developer/keymap-actions.md).

## Windows

All windows are undecorated; Forge draws title bars itself, styled per desktop
(`forge-window`). Large dialogs open as separate native windows (`registerDialog` /
`openDialogWindow`); in browser mode they open in-page.

## Conventions

- Layout, wording and shortcuts follow PHPStorm; colors are Forge's own (CSS variables in
  `app/ui/src/theme/theme.css`, dark and light).
- Rust computes, TypeScript renders ([details](docs/guide/developer/rust-computes.md)).
- Shortcuts only through the keymap; settings through the schema; secrets in the keychain; no
  `localStorage` for persistent state.
- Caches in the user cache dir, never in the project; mocks never write to real projects.

---
title: Repository layout
description: Where code, manifests, UI features, mocks, scripts, docs and skills live in the Forge repository.

# Repository layout

```text
Cargo.toml                 workspace: crates/*, packs/*/*, app/src-tauri
rust-toolchain.toml        pinned stable Rust with rustfmt and clippy
crates/forge-*             Rust libraries (one page each under developer/crates/)
packs/<pack>/<plugin>      language and framework crates, package name <pack>-<plugin>
  phpforge/                lang-php, fw-laravel, fw-symfony, orm-doctrine, dql
  webforge/                lang-web, fw-react, fw-vue, fw-angular
  luaforge/                lang-lua
app/
  src-tauri/               the Tauri shell (crate forge-app, binary forge)
    src/lib.rs             builder, state, event wiring, generate_handler![…]
    src/commands/<area>.rs IPC commands per area
    src/companion.rs       launcher arguments, forge:// links, Browser Companion server
    plugins/*.toml         built-in plugin manifests
    capabilities/          Tauri permissions (window labels)
    tauri.conf.json        app config (identifier dev.forge.ide, deep-link scheme forge)
    tauri.agents.conf.json bundles target/agents/ as the agents/ resource folder
  ui/                      SolidJS UI (package @forge/ui)
    src/App.tsx            Welcome screen or workbench
    src/shell/             workbench frame: toolbar, stripes, tool window panels, editor area,
                           status bar, Welcome screen, window chrome and dialog windows
    src/features/<name>/   UI features, each with an index.ts that registers contributions
    src/editor/            CodeMirror setup, languages, file type cache, template overlay,
                           line markers, theme
    src/keymap/            key capture and dispatch (engine: crates/forge-keymap)
    src/ipc/               typed clients for IPC commands
    src/mock/              browser-mode backend: mocks, demo projects, manifest snapshot
    src/state/             global state: workspace, editor tabs, layout, settings, commands
    src/theme/theme.css    CSS variables for both themes
    src/wasm/              loader and generated bindings of crates/forge-wasm (pkg/ committed)
    scripts/               screenshots.mjs, scenarios/*.mjs, build-wasm.mjs, build-agents.mjs
browser-extension/         Forge Companion (Chrome/Firefox, Manifest V3)
docs/
  ARCHITECTURE.md          contribution points and IPC contracts
  ROADMAP.md               milestones and planned branches
  screenshots/             PNGs produced by the scenarios
  guide/                   this guide
.claude/skills/<name>/     step-by-step recipes (also Claude Code skills)
.github/workflows/ci.yml   CI, manual dispatch only
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md       rules for coding agents and humans
CONTRIBUTING.md            contributor quick start
```

## Naming

- Rust crates: `forge-<area>` in `crates/`, `<pack>-<plugin>` in `packs/` (e.g.
  `phpforge-fw-laravel`).
- Plugin ids: `forge.<name>` (`forge.laravel`, `forge.web`).
- IPC commands: `<area>_<verb>` (`laravel_routes`, `db_execute`); events `<area>://<event>`.
- Action ids: PHPStorm's (`GotoClass`) or `<Plugin>.<Action>` (`Laravel.RunArtisan`).
- Settings keys: dotted (`php.debug.port`); settings page ids like `lang.php.laravel`.

title: Development setup
description: Install the toolchains, run Forge in browser mode or as a desktop app, use the demo projects and keep builds fast.

# Development setup

Recipe: [`.claude/skills/forge-dev-setup`](.claude/skills/forge-dev-setup/SKILL.md).

## Toolchains

- **Rust** stable, pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` (with rustfmt and clippy).
- **Node 22** and **pnpm 10**.
- **Linux**: the Tauri system libraries.

```sh
# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev libxdo-dev libssl-dev build-essential
# Arch/EndeavourOS
sudo pacman -S --needed webkit2gtk-4.1 libayatana-appindicator librsvg xdotool openssl base-devel
```

macOS needs the Xcode command line tools, Windows the MSVC build tools and WebView2 (see
Tauri's prerequisites).

## Install and run

```sh
cd app/ui
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # browser mode: http://localhost:1420 (mocked backend, demo Laravel project)
pnpm tauri dev    # desktop app with the real Rust backend
```

| URL (browser mode) | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | the Laravel demo project `acme-shop` with `app/Models/User.php` |
| `/?project=symfony` | Symfony + Doctrine demo |
| `/?project=react`, `vue`, `angular` | WebForge demos |
| `/?project=lua` | the LÖVE demo game `pixel-dungeon` |
| `/?project=remote` | a remote project `deploy@shop.example.com:/var/www/shop` |
| `/?welcome` | the Welcome screen |
| `/?welcome=remote` | Welcome › Remote Development |
| `?windowControls=gnome` (also `windows`, `macos`, `kde`, `linux`) | force a title bar style |
| `/?splash` | the startup splash with the mocked loading steps, then the workbench |
| `/?splash&simulateUpdate=0.2.0` | the splash offering a simulated update (fake download, nothing installed) |
| `/?splash&splashPause=40` | the splash held at about 40 % (screenshots) |
| `/?simulateUpdate=0.2.0` | Help \| Check for Updates… offers a simulated update |

Desktop development builds never check for real updates. `FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE=0.2.0 pnpm
tauri dev` shows the update panel on the splash with a fake download instead; see
[Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#updates-and-signing).

Browser mode is the fastest loop for UI work and screenshots. Use `pnpm tauri dev` to test the
real file system, git, language servers, PTYs, databases and Docker.

## Useful scripts (`app/ui`)

| Script | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `pnpm test` | vitest |
| `pnpm build` | typecheck + production build into `app/ui/dist` |
| `pnpm screenshots [scenario…]` | Playwright screenshots into `docs/screenshots/` |
| `pnpm wasm` | rebuild `crates/forge-wasm` into `src/wasm/pkg` |
| `pnpm agents [x86_64\|aarch64]` | build the static remote agents into `target/agents/` |
| `pnpm langservers install [--accept-intelephense-licence] [package…]` | pre-install npm language servers (and Node.js if missing) into Forge's data directory, like the IDE does; also `updates`, `where` |
| `pnpm release …` | agents + `tauri build` with bundled agents |
| `pnpm tauri …` | the Tauri CLI (runs from `app/` through `scripts/tauri.mjs`, which adds the updater signing settings to `tauri build`) |

## Keeping Rust builds manageable

- `export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` saves a lot of disk space and link time.
- With several git worktrees, give each its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; a shared target dir can
  return stale builds of workspace crates.
- Test one crate at a time while iterating: `cargo test -p forge-keymap`.

## Debugging

- Rust logs: `RUST_LOG=debug pnpm tauri dev` (or a filter such as `RUST_LOG=forge_lsp=trace`).
- The WebView's developer tools open with the usual shortcut in debug builds (right-click →
  Inspect on Linux).
- In browser mode, commands can be run from the console: `window.__forgeRunCommand("settings.open")`.

Source: docs/guide/developer/rust-computes.md

---
title: Rust computes, TypeScript renders
description: Forge's central design rule - logic, models and parsers in Rust crates with tests, the UI renders and forwards events - and how to apply it.
order: 40
tags: [architecture, rust, typescript, design]
---

# Rust computes, TypeScript renders

Logic, data models and parsers belong in Rust crates with unit tests. The SolidJS UI renders what
Rust computed and forwards user events. `app/src-tauri` stays thin: it wires crates to IPC.

## Why

- **One implementation**: the desktop app (IPC) and browser mode (WebAssembly) run the same code,
  so mocks never drift from the real behaviour.
- **Testable without a UI**: parsers, rankers and state machines are plain Rust functions with
  `cargo test`.
- **Memory safety and speed** for the heavy parts: indexing, fuzzy ranking, output parsing.

## What lives where

| In Rust | In TypeScript |
| --- | --- |
| parsing (PHP, Lua, DQL, `.http`, compose files, kubeconfig, git output, TeamCity messages, ANSI) | rendering components |
| ranking (Search Everywhere, Go to File, popups' speed search) | highlighting the positions Rust returned |
| models of complex views (Services tree and details, run console lines and test trees, chat conversation) | applying model updates to signals |
| keymap resolution, settings search and validation, file type detection | capturing DOM events |
| completion, navigation and gutter data of frameworks | CodeMirror extensions that show them |

**Exception:** per-keystroke editor work — CodeMirror tokenizers and decorations — stays in
TypeScript because an IPC round trip per token would be too slow. Even there, data that is not
needed per keystroke comes from Rust (DQL injection highlighting is computed by the backend
shortly after each edit; old spans are mapped through changes meanwhile).

## Examples in the codebase

| Feature | Rust | UI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search Everywhere | `forge_fuzzy::everywhere` ranks candidates of all providers (`search_rank`) | providers collect candidates; the popup renders groups |
| Settings dialog | `forge_plugin_api::settings_model` builds the page tree, filters it and splits texts into highlighted segments (`settings_search`) | renders the tree and controls |
| Run tool window | `forge-output` turns process output into styled console lines and test tree updates | `Console.tsx` and `TestTree.tsx` apply deltas |
| AI Chat | `forge_agent_cli::conversation` folds agent events into rendered blocks (Markdown AST, diffs, permission summaries) | `features/ai-chat/model.ts` applies updates |
| Markdown | `forge-markdown` produces a safe AST (no raw HTML) | Solid components render the AST |
| Services | `forge_containers::tree` builds the tree, details and toolbar state | `ServicesView.tsx` renders them |

## Applying the rule

1. Put the logic in a crate (`crates/forge-<area>` or a pack) and test it there.
2. Keep the pure part free of file system, processes, network and tokio, so it can be built to
   WebAssembly. Split runtime parts into a separate crate (`forge-output` for `forge-process`,
   `forge-sql` for `forge-db`, `phpforge-dql` for `phpforge-orm-doctrine`) or behind a cargo
   feature (`runtime` in `forge-agent-cli` and `forge-containers`, `client` in `forge-remote`
   and `forge-scratches`, `fs` in `webforge-lang-web`).
3. Expose it through an IPC command ([IPC commands and mocks](docs/guide/developer/ipc-and-mocks.md)) and, for browser
   mode, through `forge-wasm` ([The WebAssembly bridge](docs/guide/developer/wasm-bridge.md)).
4. In the UI, call the typed client and render the answer. Avoid re-implementing decisions in
   TypeScript.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/wasm-bridge.md

---
title: The WebAssembly bridge
description: How crates/forge-wasm compiles pure Rust crates to WebAssembly for browser mode, how mocks call it, and how to add a module.
order: 50
tags: [wasm, webassembly, browser mode, mocks]
---

# The WebAssembly bridge

In browser mode (`pnpm dev`, screenshots, vitest) there is no Tauri backend. Instead of
re-implementing logic in TypeScript mocks, Forge compiles its **pure** crates to WebAssembly with
`crates/forge-wasm` and the mocks call them.

## How it works

- `crates/forge-wasm` depends on the pure crates (`forge-fuzzy`, `forge-filetypes`,
  `forge-keymap`, `forge-markdown`, `forge-output`, `forge-sql`, `forge-window`,
  `forge-plugin-api`, `forge-scratches` without `client`, `forge-remote` without `client`,
  `forge-containers` without `runtime`, `forge-agent-cli` without `runtime`, `luaforge-lang-lua`,
  `phpforge-dql`, the WebForge crates).
- Each area is a module `crates/forge-wasm/src/<area>.rs` with `#[wasm_bindgen]` functions that
  take and return **JSON strings**, mirroring the matching IPC command:

  ```rust
  #[wasm_bindgen]
  pub fn keymap_resolve(request_json: &str) -> String { … }
  ```

- Stateful models are exposed through numeric handles (`run_output_new` / `run_output_handle`,
  `chat_new` / `chat_apply`); parser bridges live in `crates/forge-wasm/src/parsers/`.
- The generated package `app/ui/src/wasm/pkg` is **committed**, so `pnpm dev` works without a Rust
  toolchain.

## Calling it from the UI

```ts
import { callWasm, forgeWasm } from "@/wasm";
import { registerMock } from "@/ipc";

registerMock("search_rank", async ({ request }) => {
  const wasm = await forgeWasm();
  return callWasm(wasm.search_rank, request);
});
```

- `forgeWasm()` loads the module once.
- `callWasm(fn, input)` serializes the input, calls the function and parses the result.
- `callWasmSync(fn, input)` is for code that cannot wait (editor setup); it is valid once
  `forgeWasm()` has resolved. `mock/index.ts` waits for the module before the UI starts.

The keymap resolver is special: it runs from WebAssembly in **both** desktop and browser mode,
because a key handler must decide synchronously whether to call `preventDefault`.

## Rebuilding

After changing Rust code that the bundle uses:

```sh
pnpm --dir app/ui wasm
```

This needs the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target (`rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`) and
`wasm-bindgen-cli` at the version pinned in `crates/forge-wasm/Cargo.toml`. Commit the updated
`app/ui/src/wasm/pkg`.

## Adding a module

1. Make sure the crate (or its pure part) builds without file system, processes, network and
   tokio.
2. Add the dependency to `crates/forge-wasm/Cargo.toml` (with the runtime feature off).
3. Add `src/<area>.rs` with JSON-in/JSON-out functions and declare it in `lib.rs`.
4. Rebuild with `pnpm --dir app/ui wasm` and call it from the mock.
5. Add a test in `forge-wasm` (they run natively with `cargo test -p forge-wasm`) and, if useful,
   a vitest that loads the bundle (`app/ui/src/wasm/wasm.test.ts`).

Source: docs/guide/developer/contribution-points.md

---
title: Contribution points
description: Every UI extension API of Forge (registerToolWindow, registerCommand, registerSettingsPage, registerEditorExtension, registerSearchProvider, registerLanguage, registerKeymapActions and more) with examples.
order: 60
tags: [ui, extension points, solidjs, api]
---

# Contribution points

Features plug into the UI through `register*` functions. A feature is a folder
`app/ui/src/features/<name>/` whose `index.ts` calls them; add one import line to
`app/ui/src/features/index.ts`. Registrations with the same `id` replace earlier ones (that is
how real tool windows replace placeholders, and how the Blade pack replaces a syntax mode).

On the Rust side, plugins contribute **data** through their manifest (see
[Writing a plugin or pack](docs/guide/developer/plugins-and-packs.md)); this page is about the UI.

> **Note:** the examples are shortened sketches; helper names such as `laravelApi.goto` stand
> for a feature's typed IPC client. The modules in the table are the reference.

## Overview

| Function | Module | Contributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `registerToolWindow` | `features/registry.ts` | a panel on a stripe |
| `registerCommand` | `state/commands.ts` | an action with an id (Find Action, keymap, menus) |
| `registerKeymapActions` | `keymap/store.ts` | plugin actions with default shortcuts |
| `registerSettingsPage` | `features/settingsPages.ts` | a page in the Settings dialog |
| `registerMainMenuEntries` | `features/mainMenu` | entries in the main menu (`"Tools"`, `"Tools/_Laravel"`, `"View/Tool Windows"`) with `before`/`after`/`when` |
| `registerMainMenuDynamic` / `registerMainMenuToggle` | `features/mainMenu` | dynamic lists (`recentProjects`, `toolWindows`) and check marks |
| `chooseDeclarationAt` | `features/navigation/chooseDeclaration.ts` | the shared "Choose Declaration" popup for several targets |
| `registerStatusItem` | `features/statusItems.ts` | a status bar widget |
| `registerToolbarItem` | `features/toolbarItems.ts` | a main toolbar widget left of the run widget |
| `registerEditorExtension` | `editor/extensions.ts` | CodeMirror extensions per file |
| `registerLanguage` | `editor/languages.ts` | the syntax mode of a file type id |
| `registerLineMarkerProvider` | `editor/lineMarkers.ts` | gutter icons |
| `registerDeclarationProvider` | `features/lsp/goto.ts` | framework targets for Go to Declaration (tried before the LSP) |
| `registerFormatProvider` | `features/lsp/format.ts` | a formatter tried before the language server |
| `registerCompletionKind` | `features/lsp/completion.ts` | icons/colors for custom completion kinds |
| `registerSearchProvider` | `features/search/providers.ts` | candidates for a Search Everywhere tab |
| `registerStructureProvider` | `features/php/StructureView.tsx` | the Structure tool window for another language |
| `registerContextMenu` | `features/contextMenu/state.ts` | entries of a context menu (e.g. `"editor"`) |
| `registerProjectViewSection` | `features/project/ProjectView.tsx` | top-level nodes below the project tree |
| `registerFileSystem` | `state/editor.ts` | editor tabs for a URI prefix (`scratch://`) |
| `openCustomTab` | `state/editor.ts` | an editor tab that shows a feature view (`forge:<kind>/<id>`) |
| `registerEditorView` | `shell/editorViews.ts` | non-file editor tabs opened with `openViewTab` (consoles, table editors) |
| `registerRunConfigurationType` | `features/run/types.ts` | a Run/Debug configuration type |
| `registerDebugLauncher` | `features/run/types.ts` | a debugger for Debug (`Shift+F9`) |
| `registerDialog` / `openDialogWindow` | `shell/window/dialogs.ts` | a large dialog in its own window |
| `registerChatAgent` | `features/ai-chat/agents.ts` | an agent in the AI Chat picker |
| `claimFrameworkStatus` | `features/project-type` | hide the generic framework status widget |
| `registerMock` | `ipc/index.ts` | a browser-mode handler for an IPC command |

## Tool windows

```tsx
import { Container } from "lucide-solid";
import { registerToolWindow } from "@/features/registry";

registerToolWindow({
  id: "services",            // same id as a placeholder replaces it
  title: "Services",
  icon: Container,           // lucide-solid
  anchor: "bottom",          // "left" | "right" | "bottom"
  order: 30,                 // position in the stripe
  shortcut: "Alt+8",         // tooltip only; the binding comes from the keymap
  component: ServicesView,
  actions: () => <HeaderButtons />,   // optional header buttons
  headerContent: () => <Tabs />,      // optional, e.g. tabs next to the title
  when: () => usesFramework("docker"), // optional: only for matching projects
});
```

Recipe: [`add-tool-window`](.claude/skills/add-tool-window/SKILL.md).

## Commands

```ts
import { registerCommand } from "@/state/commands";

registerCommand({ id: "ActivateStructureToolWindow", title: "Structure", category: "View",
  run: () => toggleToolWindow("left", "structure") });
```

Use a PHPStorm action id when one exists: the command then gets PHPStorm's default shortcut and
appears in Settings | Keymap. Otherwise use `<area>.<verb>` and, if it needs a shortcut, register
a keymap action ([Keymap actions](docs/guide/developer/keymap-actions.md)). `runCommand(id)` runs any command.

## Settings pages

```tsx
registerSettingsPage({
  id: "lang.lua", title: "Lua", group: "Languages & Frameworks", parent: undefined, order: 30,
  keywords: ["love", "stylua"],
  component: () => <SchemaPage pageId="lang.lua" />,
});
```

`SchemaPage` renders every setting whose `group` is the page id. See [Settings](docs/guide/developer/settings.md).

## Status bar and toolbar items

```ts
registerStatusItem({ id: "framework.laravel", align: "right", order: 80,
  component: LaravelStatus, when: () => laravelActive() });
registerToolbarItem({ id: "php.debug.listen", order: 10, component: ListenButton });
```

## Editor extensions and languages

```ts
registerEditorExtension(({ path }) =>
  path.endsWith(".php") ? [myCompletion(path), myGutter(path)] : null);

registerLanguage({ id: "neon", load: () => yaml() });
```

Factories run per opened file and return CodeMirror extensions (or `null`). `registerLanguage`
maps a **file type id** (decided in Rust by `forge-filetypes`) to a syntax mode. See
[Adding a language](docs/guide/developer/adding-a-language.md).

## Line markers

```ts
registerLineMarkerProvider({
  appliesTo: (p) => p.endsWith(".php"),
  watch: () => laravelActive(),                 // recompute when this changes
  markers: async (path, text) => [{ line: 12, icon: Route, title: "GET /orders",
    className: "marker-route", onClick: (view, e) => openRoute() }],
});
```

## Go to Declaration and formatting

```ts
registerDeclarationProvider(async (path, view, pos) => {
  const targets = await laravelApi.goto(path, view.state.doc.toString(), pos);
  if (!targets.length) return false;   // let the next provider or the LSP try
  await openFileAt(targets[0].path, targets[0].line + 1);
  return true;
});

registerFormatProvider(async (path, view) => path.endsWith(".lua") && (await formatWithStyLua(path, view)));
```

When a provider finds several targets, show the shared popup instead of guessing:

```ts
import { chooseDeclarationAt } from "@/features/navigation/chooseDeclaration";

chooseDeclarationAt(view, pos, targets /* { path, line, column?, preview? }[], 0-based */,
  { title: "Choose Declaration" });
```

## Main menu

The menu structure, labels, mnemonics (`_` before the letter), shortcuts and enabled states are
computed in Rust (`forge-keymap::menu`, IPC `keymap_main_menu`); an entry is enabled when some
command implements its action. Add entries from a manifest:

```toml
[[plugin.contributions.mainMenu]]
path = "Tools/_Laravel"            # submenus are created as needed
items = [
  { type = "action", id = "Laravel.RunArtisan", label = "Run _Artisan Command..." },
  { type = "separator" },
]
# optional: before = "<action id>", after = "<action id>"; items may be checkable = true
```

or from the UI with `registerMainMenuEntries(path, entries, { before?, after?, when? })`.
`registerMainMenuToggle(actionId, isOn)` reports the check mark of a checkable item.

## Search Everywhere

```ts
registerSearchProvider({
  id: "php.classes", tab: "classes", title: "Classes", order: 0,
  async search(query, { limit }) {
    const hits = await phpApi.searchSymbols(query, "class", limit);
    return hits.map((h) => ({ id: h.fqn, label: h.name, detail: h.namespace, kind: "class",
      score: h.score, matches: h.positions, run: () => openFileAt(h.path, h.line) }));
  },
});
```

Providers only **collect** candidates. Ranking happens in Rust (`search_rank`): items with a
`match` spec are matched there; pre-ranked items (`score` + `matches`) are taken as they are.

## Run configuration types and debuggers

```ts
registerRunConfigurationType({
  id: "artisan", name: "Artisan", icon: Terminal, interpreter: "php", debuggable: true,
  fields: [{ key: "command", label: "Command", required: true, placeholder: "migrate --seed" }],
});

registerDebugLauncher({
  id: "xdebug",
  canDebug: (cfg) => PHP_TYPES.has(cfg.type),
  launch: async (cfg, ctx) => { const env = await debugLauncher.prepare(); await ctx.run({ env }); },
});
```

Without `buildCommand`, the backend's kind registry (`forge_process::config`) builds the command
line. A manifest type with `fields` and a `command` template (see `lua-script`) needs no UI code.

## Dialog windows

```ts
registerDialog({ id: "run-configurations", title: "Run/Debug Configurations",
  width: 960, height: 640, component: ConfigurationsDialog,
  prepare: () => loadConfigurations(), onClosed: (result) => reload() });

const result = await openDialogWindow("run-configurations", { select: "UserTest" });
```

In the desktop app the dialog opens as a native window owned by the caller (geometry remembered
in `dialog-windows.json`); in browser mode it opens in-page. The dialog ends with
`closeDialog(id, result)`. Small popups stay in-page.

## Editor tabs that are not files

- `openCustomTab({ id: "forge:mr/41", title: "#41 …", icon, component })` — feature views such as
  merge requests and issues. `activeTab()` stays file-only; check `isCustomTab(id)`.
- `registerEditorView` + `openViewTab` — database consoles and table editors.
- `registerFileSystem({ prefix: "scratch://", read, write, icon, breadcrumbs })` — files that
  live elsewhere (scratches).

## Project awareness

Use `projectInfo()`, `usesFramework("laravel")` and `isPluginActive("forge.laravel")` from
`src/state/project.ts` to activate a feature only when the project uses it, and
`isRemoteProject()` from `state/workspace.ts` to hide local-only features.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/ipc-and-mocks.md

---
title: IPC commands and browser mocks
description: Adding a backend command - the Rust handler in app/src-tauri, the typed TypeScript client, events, and the browser-mode mock or WebAssembly bridge.
order: 70
tags: [ipc, tauri, mocks, commands]
---

# IPC commands and browser mocks

Every backend call has three parts: a Rust command, a typed client and a browser mock. Recipe:
[`add-ipc-command`](.claude/skills/add-ipc-command/SKILL.md). The list of existing
contracts is in [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and, per crate, in the
[crate pages](docs/guide/developer/crates/index.md).

## 1. Rust

Put the logic in a crate with tests, then add a thin handler to
`app/src-tauri/src/commands/<area>.rs` (new modules go into `commands/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[tauri::command]
pub fn routes_list(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> Result<Vec<Route>> {
    state.with_workspace(|ws| forge_laravel::routes(ws.root()))
}
```

- Return `forge_core::Result<T>`; errors serialize to strings for the UI.
- Resolve user paths with `Workspace::resolve`, which rejects paths outside the project.
- Project operations that must also work remotely go through `AppState::backend()` (the
  `forge_backend::Backend` of the open project) and run on a blocking thread
  (`commands::workspace::blocking`). `with_workspace` is for local-only features; it fails for
  remote projects with "not available in remote projects yet".
- Long work: make the command `async` or spawn a task; stream progress with
  `app.emit("<area>://<event>", payload)`.
- Feature state: a struct registered with `.manage(...)` in `lib.rs`, not more fields in
  `AppState`.
- Register the command in `tauri::generate_handler![...]` in `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`.
- Arguments arrive camelCased from JS (`fooBar` → `foo_bar`).

## 2. Typed client

`app/ui/src/ipc/<area>.ts`:

```ts
import { invoke, listen } from "./index";

export interface Route { methods: string[]; uri: string; name?: string }

export const routesApi = {
  list: () => invoke<Route[]>("routes_list"),
  onChanged: (cb: (r: Route[]) => void) => listen<Route[]>("routes://changed", cb),
};
```

Features never call `invoke` with string literals directly; they use the client.

## 3. Browser mock

If the logic is pure (no file system, processes, network), expose the same Rust function through
`crates/forge-wasm` and call it from the mock ([The WebAssembly bridge](docs/guide/developer/wasm-bridge.md)).
Otherwise write a mock in `app/ui/src/mock/<area>Mock.ts` and import it from `mock/index.ts`:

```ts
import { registerMock, emitMock } from "@/ipc";

registerMock("routes_list", () => [{ methods: ["GET"], uri: "/orders/{order}", name: "orders.show" }]);
```

- Mocks load only in browser mode and must **never write to a real project**; keep changes in
  memory.
- Use the demo projects (`mock/demoProject.ts`, `demoLaravel.ts`, `demoSymfonyProject.ts`,
  `demoWebProjects.ts`, `demoLuaProject.ts`, `demoConfigFiles.ts`) so screenshots look real.
- `emitMock("<area>://<event>", payload)` simulates events.

## Events

Events are named `<area>://<event>` (`settings://changed`, `fs://changed`, `lsp://diagnostics`,
`run://<runId>`, `agent://<sessionId>`, `services://event`, `remote://status`, …). Subscribe
before you start the work that emits them (pass your own id where the API allows it, e.g.
`terminal_open({ options: { id } })`).

## Conventions

- Paths across IPC are workspace-relative; positions are 0-based lines and UTF-16 columns
  (JavaScript string offsets) unless documented otherwise.
- Shared or cross-feature contracts are documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → "Shared IPC
  contracts".
- Secrets never travel back to the UI: commands return masked values (`maskedKey`) or booleans.

Source: docs/guide/developer/plugins-and-packs.md

---
title: Writing a plugin or pack
description: A walkthrough for adding a Forge plugin - manifest, Rust crate, IPC, UI feature, settings, activation per project, browser mock, tests and docs.
order: 80
tags: [plugins, packs, manifest, walkthrough]
---

# Writing a plugin or pack

A **pack** groups plugins (`core`, `phpforge`, `webforge`, `luaforge`; AI plugins live in
`core`). A **plugin** is a manifest, plus an optional Rust crate, plus an optional UI feature.
Recipe: [`add-plugin-or-pack`](.claude/skills/add-plugin-or-pack/SKILL.md).

This walkthrough builds a small plugin, "Makefile targets": a tool window that lists the targets
of the project's `Makefile` and runs them.

## 1. Manifest

Create `app/src-tauri/plugins/make.toml` (or add a `[[plugin]]` table to an existing file):

```toml
id = "forge.make"
name = "Make"
version = "0.1.0"
pack = "core"
vendor = "Forge"
description = "Makefile targets: list and run them."
depends = ["forge.run"]
projectTypes = ["make"]          # activate only for projects that use it

[[contributions.commands]]
id = "make.reload"
title = "Reload Makefile Targets"
category = "Tools"

[[contributions.toolWindows]]
id = "make"
title = "Make"
anchor = "left"
icon = "hammer"
order = 40

[[contributions.settings]]
key = "make.executable"
title = "make executable"
type = "path"
default = "make"
group = "tools.make"             # settings page id
order = 0
```

Contribution types (`crates/forge-plugin-api/src/contributions.rs`): `languages`, `fileTypes`,
`commands`, `keybindings`, `toolWindows`, `settings`, `lspServers`, `runConfigurationTypes`,
`aiProviders`, `chatAgents`, `codeGenerators`, `mainMenu` (see [Contribution points](docs/guide/developer/contribution-points.md#main-menu)). A run configuration type with `fields` and a
`command` template works without UI code (see `lua-script` in `luaforge.toml`).

Project types are ids from `forge-project` detection (languages, frameworks, packs, tools).
`make` is not detected yet, so you would add it to `crates/forge-project/src/detect.rs` (a
`Makefile` in a scanned folder → `c.tool("make")`) with a test. Without `projectTypes` a plugin is
always active.

Regenerate the browser snapshot and run the manifest tests:

```sh
FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app
```

## 2. Rust crate

If the plugin has logic (parsing the Makefile), create a crate:

- `crates/forge-make` (or `packs/<pack>/<plugin>`, package name `<pack>-<plugin>`);
- add it to `members` and `[workspace.dependencies]` in the root `Cargo.toml` and depend on it
  from `app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`;
- depend only on `forge-core` / `forge-plugin-api` (and other library crates), never on
  `forge-app`;
- keep the parser pure so it can run as WebAssembly;
- unit-test with fixture projects; no network, no installed tools.

```rust
/// Targets of a Makefile with their 0-based line.
pub fn targets(makefile: &str) -> Vec<Target> { … }
```

## 3. IPC

Add `make_targets` to `app/src-tauri/src/commands/make.rs`, read the file through the project's
backend so remote projects work, register it in `lib.rs`, and write the typed client
`app/ui/src/ipc/make.ts`. See [IPC commands and browser mocks](docs/guide/developer/ipc-and-mocks.md).

## 4. UI feature

`app/ui/src/features/make/index.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Hammer } from "lucide-solid";
import { registerToolWindow } from "@/features/registry";
import { registerCommand } from "@/state/commands";
import { registerSettingsPage } from "@/features/settingsPages";
import { SchemaPage } from "@/features/settings/SchemaPage";
import { isPluginActive } from "@/state/project";

const active = () => isPluginActive("forge.make");

registerToolWindow({ id: "make", title: "Make", icon: Hammer, anchor: "left", order: 40,
  component: MakeView, when: active });
registerCommand({ id: "make.reload", title: "Reload Makefile Targets", category: "Tools",
  run: () => void reload() });
registerSettingsPage({ id: "tools.make", title: "Make", group: "Tools",
  component: () => <SchemaPage pageId="tools.make" /> });
```

Add `import "./make";` to `app/ui/src/features/index.ts`. Running a target can reuse the Run tool
window with a temporary `shell` configuration.

UI rules: PHPStorm layout and wording, CSS variables from `src/theme/theme.css` only (both
themes), icons from `lucide-solid`, shortcuts only through the keymap.

## 5. Browser mock

Expose `targets` through `crates/forge-wasm` and call it from `app/ui/src/mock/makeMock.ts` on a
demo `Makefile` (add one to the demo project). The feature must work in `pnpm dev`.

## 6. Check and document

- Tests: `cargo test -p forge-make`, vitest for UI logic.
- A screenshot scenario in `app/ui/scripts/scenarios/` ([Screenshots](docs/guide/developer/screenshots.md)); look
  at the images in both themes.
- [Quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md).
- Docs: add the plugin to the README table and `docs/ROADMAP.md`, new IPC contracts to
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and a user page under `docs/guide/user/` (plus the reference tables
  if you added settings, actions or file types).

## Packs

A new pack is a new `pack` value in manifests plus a folder `packs/<pack>/`. Packs appear as
groups in Settings | Plugins, and `forge-project` maps languages to packs (`php` → `phpforge`)
in `pack_for_language` in `detect.rs`.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/adding-a-language.md

---
title: Adding a language
description: Add a file type, a syntax mode, editor features, a language server and template data languages to Forge.
order: 90
tags: [languages, syntax highlighting, file types, codemirror]
---

# Adding a language

Recipe: [`add-language-support`](.claude/skills/add-language-support/SKILL.md).

A language has up to four parts:

| Part | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **File type** (names, extensions, shebangs, label, indentation) | Rust: `crates/forge-filetypes/src/builtin.rs` (bundled) or a manifest's `[[contributions.fileTypes]]` |
| **Syntax mode** (highlighting) | UI: `app/ui/src/editor/languages.ts` or `registerLanguage` |
| **Editor features** without a server (completion, hover, folding, checks) | UI: `app/ui/src/features/languages/<name>.ts` |
| **Language server** | catalog: `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml` |

## 1. File type

```toml
[[plugin.contributions.fileTypes]]
id = "neon"
name = "NEON"                      # status bar label
extensions = ["neon"]              # longest match wins: "html.twig" beats "html"
fileNames = ["phpstan.neon*"]      # exact names, `*` anywhere, `/` for path suffixes
interpreters = ["neon"]            # optional: `#!` lines of extensionless scripts
indentSize = 2                     # optional, default 4
```

A plugin type with the id of a bundled type replaces it while the plugin is active. After
changing a manifest run `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`. Add detection tests
to `crates/forge-filetypes/src/tests.rs` (bundled) or `file_types_detect_like_phpstorm` in
`app/src-tauri/src/plugins.rs` (manifests).

The UI asks Rust for a file's type (`filetypes_detect`) and caches it per path; use
`languageIdFor`, `languageLabel` and `indentFor` from `editor/languages.ts`, and
`await ensureFileType(path)` before building something synchronous.

## 2. Syntax mode

Pick, in this order: an official Lezer package (`@codemirror/lang-<x>`), a legacy mode
(`@codemirror/legacy-modes`) wrapped with `StreamLanguage.define`, or your own `StreamParser`
(use `streamLanguage` from `src/editor/tokens.ts` to map token names to Lezer tags). Then:

```ts
registerLanguage({ id: "neon", load: () => yaml() });
```

Token colors come from `forgeHighlight` in `src/editor/forgeTheme.ts` (Lezer tags → `--syn-*`
CSS variables). Add a style there instead of hard-coding colors. Add a file icon in
`src/shell/FileIcon.tsx`.

## 3. Editor features without a server

Language packs for config and script formats live in `app/ui/src/features/languages/` (see
`bash.ts`, `compose.ts`, `postfix.ts`). Each file calls `registerLanguage` and
`registerEditorExtension`; `shared.ts` provides hover docs, folding and `syntaxDiagnostics`,
which feeds the Problems view unless a listed language server runs for the file. Parsers are
unit-tested without an editor (`testkit.ts`).

## 4. Language server

Add a `[[language]]` and a `[[server]]` entry to `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml`:
command and args, `languages`, `group`, `install` options (npm commands are rewritten to
Forge's own prefix), `license`, `homepage`, optional `alternative`, `plugin` and `when`. Server
settings and initialization options go into the entry; project-specific values are added in
`crates/forge-langservers/src/config.rs`. If a file uses a feature only the server provides, add
an install hint to `SERVER_HINTS` (`features/langservers/serverHint.ts`).

## Template languages and data languages

HTML-based template engines (Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja, Handlebars, Go templates) are a
`TemplateSyntax` for the shared template parser in `src/editor/templates.ts`, drawn as a
decoration layer (`templateOverlay.ts`) over the data language's real editor support. The data
language is chosen in Rust (`crates/forge-filetypes/src/data.rs`): the
`templates.dataLanguages` setting, then compound names (`invoice.tex.twig`), then HTML.

- Another data language: add it to `DATA_LANGUAGES` and `COMPOUND` in `data.rs`, and to
  `DATA_LANGUAGES` in `src/editor/templateData.ts` with a `parser` (and a `support` factory if
  one exists).
- Another template engine: describe it as a `TemplateSyntax` (delimiters, keywords, builtins)
  and register it with the `template(...)` helper in `languages.ts`; mark its type as a template
  in `builtin.rs` (`TEMPLATES`).

## Check

Add a sample to `app/ui/src/mock/demoConfigFiles.ts`, a scenario to
`app/ui/scripts/scenarios/syntax.mjs`, capture it and look at it in both themes.
