Source: docs/guide/developer/settings.md

---
title: Settings
description: Declaring settings in plugin manifests, reading them in Rust and the UI, settings pages, project scope, validation and secrets.
order: 100
tags: [settings, manifest, schema]
---

# Settings

Recipe: [`add-setting`](.claude/skills/add-setting/SKILL.md). User documentation:
[Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md); every key:
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

## Model

`forge_core::Settings` merges three layers: schema defaults < user
(`<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`) < project (`<project>/.forge/settings.toml`). Keys are
dotted (`editor.font.size`) and stored as nested TOML tables. Values are JSON so they cross IPC
unchanged. Writing a value persists its layer and notifies subscribers with the new effective
value (`SettingsChange { key, value, scope }`), which the shell forwards as `settings://changed`.

IPC: `settings_get_all`, `settings_set(key, value, scope)`, `settings_schema`,
`settings_search`, `settings_validate`, `plugins_list`, `plugin_set_enabled`.

## Declaring a setting

```toml
[[contributions.settings]]
key = "projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick"
title = "Open files with single click"
description = "Shown under the option."
type = "bool"            # bool | int | number | string | enum | path | list
default = true
group = "appearance"     # settings page id
section = "Project View" # optional heading on the page
order = 40
project = true           # optional: may be stored per project
# int/number: min = 10, max = 20 (number: step)
# enum: options = [{ value = "auto", label = "Platform default" }, …]
```

Regenerate the snapshot: `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`.

## Pages

`group` is a page id. Pages generated from the schema are listed in `schemaPages` in
`app/ui/src/features/settings/index.tsx`; features register their own pages with
`registerSettingsPage` and usually render `<SchemaPage pageId="…" />` (optionally with extra
content, see the Docker page's Test Connection). Custom pages (tables, test buttons) are plain
components that use `draftValue`/`setDraft` from `features/settings/dialogState.ts` so OK,
Cancel and Apply work. Open a page programmatically with `openSettings("<page id>")`.

The dialog's search, highlighting and validation are computed in Rust
(`forge_plugin_api::settings_model`, `settings_validate`).

## Reading settings

- UI: `getSetting<boolean>("projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick", false)` from
  `src/state/settings.ts`; reactive in effects and JSX. `saveSetting(key, value, scope)` writes.
- Rust: `state.read_settings().get_as::<bool>("…")`; subscribe with `Settings::subscribe`
  (listeners run under the settings lock — do work on another thread, as `lib.rs` does).

## Rules

- Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, licence keys) never go into settings: store them with the
  `keyring` crate (see `forge-ai`, `forge-db`, `forge-forges`, `forge-langservers::licence`).
- Do not keep persistent state in `localStorage`; use settings.
- A declared setting should be applied; if it is not yet, the user docs must say so.

---
title: Keymap actions
description: How the Rust keymap engine works, implementing PHPStorm actions, aliases, plugin actions with default shortcuts, focus contexts and conflict tests.
order: 110
tags: [keymap, shortcuts, actions]
---

# Keymap actions

Recipe: [`add-keymap-action`](.claude/skills/add-keymap-action/SKILL.md). Every
shortcut goes through the keymap engine. **Never** add a `keydown` listener for a shortcut: it
breaks user overrides, focus contexts and conflict detection, and causes double toggles.

## The engine

`crates/forge-keymap` (pure Rust):

- `shortcut`: parsing (`Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`, `Shift Shift`, `Cmd+,`), canonical ids, display strings
  (`Ctrl+Shift+A` / `⇧⌘A`) and physical key names of DOM events;
- `catalog`: PHPStorm's default keymaps from `data/phpstorm.json` (id, title, group,
  Windows/Linux and macOS shortcuts, `native` flag) and `ACTION_ALIASES`;
- `engine`: bindings, conflicts and the `Resolver` state machine (chords, double taps, focus
  contexts `editor`, `input`, `toolwindow`, `global`, `terminal`);
- `keymap`: `KeymapService` combining the catalog, plugin actions, registered commands and user
  overrides from the `keymap.*` settings.

The UI (`app/ui/src/keymap/`) captures key events, classifies the focus context and asks the
resolver — synchronously, through the WebAssembly build, in desktop and browser mode alike —
then runs the returned action with `runAction`. Unimplemented actions show "not available yet".
IPC: `keymap_actions`, `keymap_register_actions`, `keymap_set_override`, `keymap_conflicts`,
`keymap_find_by_shortcut`, `keymap_resolve`, `keymap_import_legacy`.

## Implementing a PHPStorm action

Most actions already exist with the right default keys. Register a command with that id:

```ts
registerCommand({ id: "ActivateStructureToolWindow", title: "Structure",
  run: () => toggleToolWindow("left", "structure") });
```

If your feature already uses another id, alias it in `ACTION_ALIASES`
(`crates/forge-keymap/src/catalog.rs`):

```rust
("Generate", &["php.generate"]),
```

Rebuild the browser bundle after changing Rust keymap code: `pnpm --dir app/ui wasm`.

## Plugin actions

```ts
registerKeymapActions([
  { id: "Laravel.RunArtisan", title: "Run Artisan Command…", group: "Laravel",
    shortcuts: { $default: ["Ctrl+Shift+X"], macOS: ["Cmd+Shift+X"] } },
  { id: "Console.Jdbc.Execute", title: "Execute", group: "Database", context: "editor",
    shortcuts: { $default: ["Ctrl+Enter"], macOS: ["Cmd+Enter"] } },
]);
registerCommand({ id: "Laravel.RunArtisan", title: "Run Artisan Command…", run: openArtisanPopup });
```

- `group` places the action in the Keymap tree (`Plugins/<Name>` by convention, or a
  `Main Menu/...` group).
- `context: "editor" | "toolwindow"` limits where the shortcut applies, so the same keys can
  mean different things (`Alt+Insert` adds a row in a data grid, opens Generate in the editor).
- Shortcut syntax: `Ctrl+Shift+A`, `Alt+Insert`, chords `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`, double taps
  `Shift Shift`, macOS `Cmd`/`Opt`. Physical key codes are used, so layouts work.

Manifests can also declare `[[contributions.keybindings]]` (`command`, `key`, optional `keymap`
and `when`).

> **Note:** some editor-local keys are bound with CodeMirror keymaps inside a feature's editor
> extension (for example `Ctrl+O`/`Ctrl+I` in PHP files, `Mod-b`, `Mod-p`, `Mod-Alt-l`). Prefer
> the keymap engine for new actions.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p forge-keymap`: the tests detect unexpected conflicts in the default keymaps.
- Find Action lists the action with its shortcut; Settings | Keymap shows it and lets users
  rebind it.
- Update [the keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md).

Source: docs/guide/developer/screenshots.md

---
title: Screenshots and scenarios
description: Capture Playwright screenshots of the browser-mode UI with scenario files, review them in both themes and commit them with UI changes.
order: 120
tags: [screenshots, playwright, ui, testing]
---

# Screenshots and scenarios

Every UI change needs screenshots, and you must look at them. Recipe:
[`verify-ui-with-screenshots`](.claude/skills/verify-ui-with-screenshots/SKILL.md).

## How it works

Forge runs entirely in a browser with mocked IPC, so every feature can be captured headless.
`app/ui/scripts/screenshots.mjs` opens the dev server in Chromium (Playwright), runs a scenario
and writes `docs/screenshots/<scenario>.png` at 1440×900.

## Steps

1. Start the dev server on a free port:

   ```sh
   cd app/ui && pnpm dev --port 1430
   ```

2. Add or update a scenario in `app/ui/scripts/scenarios/<feature>.mjs`:

   ```js
   /** @type {Record<string, (page: import("playwright-core").Page) => Promise<void>>} */
   export default {
     "routes-tool-window": async (page) => {
       await page.click('[data-tool-window="routes"]');
       await page.waitForSelector(".routes-table tr");
     },
   };
   ```

   - The page starts with the demo project open and `User.php` in the editor (`.cm-content` is
     visible).
   - Start elsewhere with properties on the function: `fn.query = "?welcome"`,
     `fn.waitFor = ".welcome-project"`.
   - In the Project tree a double click opens folders and files:
     `page.dblclick('.tree-row[data-path="app/Models"]')`.
   - Run commands: `page.evaluate(() => window.__forgeRunCommand("settings.open"))`.
   - Press keys: `page.keyboard.press("Control+Alt+KeyS")`.
   - Light theme: `document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "light"`.

3. Capture:

   ```sh
   FORGE_URL=http://localhost:1430 node scripts/screenshots.mjs <scenario> [more…]
   ```

   Without arguments all scenarios run. Chromium is found under `/opt/pw-browsers/…` or set
   `CHROMIUM_PATH`.

4. **Open every image** and compare it with PHPStorm's New UI: layout, spacing, wording and
   states; colors must come from the Forge theme. Check the light theme too.
5. Commit the PNGs with the change.

## Existing scenario files

`ai-chat`, `ai-providers`, `browser-companion`, `context-menu`, `database`, `debugger`,
`dialog-windows`, `docker`, `editor-lsp`, `file-menu`, `forges`, `gemini`, `integration-polish`,
`language-servers`, `laravel`, `luaforge`, `navigation`, `php`, `project-tree`, `project-wizard`,
`remote`, `scratches`, `settings`, `symfony`, `syntax`, `terminal-run`, `vcs`, `webforge`,
`welcome`, `workbench`.

The guide links these screenshots relatively (`../../screenshots/<name>.png`); when you rename a
scenario, update the pages that use it.

## Troubleshooting

- `Timeout … .cm-content`: the dev server restarted (e.g. Vite re-optimized dependencies after
  `pnpm add`). Run the scenario again.
- `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`: the dev server is not running on that port.

Source: docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md

---
title: Quality gates
description: The checks to run before every commit - rustfmt, clippy, cargo tests, TypeScript typecheck, vitest, production build, browser extension checks and test rules.
order: 130
tags: [quality, testing, ci, clippy]
---

# Quality gates

Run all of these and fix every failure before committing. CI runs only on manual dispatch, so
local checks are the gate. Recipe:
[`quality-gates`](.claude/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md).

## Rust (repository root)

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

- `export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` saves disk space and time.
- With several worktrees, give each its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- After changing plugin manifests or project generators:
  `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`.

## UI (`app/ui`)

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test        # vitest
pnpm build
pnpm version:check   # Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json and package.json agree
```

## Browser extension (`browser-extension`, only when it changed)

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build       # dist/chrome and dist/firefox
```

## Test rules

- Tests must not need network access, installed language servers or real code-host accounts.
  Use fakes and local mock servers: a fake language server (`crates/forge-lsp/tests/fake_server.rs`),
  recorded agent CLI streams and fake CLI scripts (`crates/forge-agent-cli/tests/`), in-memory
  pipes for the remote protocol, local HTTP mock servers for code hosts and AI providers,
  SQLite for database tests.
- Parsers and models are tested in Rust; UI logic with vitest (pure modules, e.g. tree
  navigation, settings application, keymap dispatch).

## Before you commit

- UI changes have screenshots that you looked at ([Screenshots](docs/guide/developer/screenshots.md)).
- No stray files: mocks never write into real projects; caches go to the user cache dir.
- User-visible changes update the matching page in `docs/guide/`.
- Small commits with imperative English subjects, no trailers ([Git workflow](docs/guide/developer/git-workflow.md)).

Source: docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md

---
title: Release builds
description: Build Forge bundles (AppImage, deb, rpm, dmg, msi/nsis), bundle the remote agents with pnpm release, and smoke-test a build.
order: 140
tags: [release, build, appimage, bundles, remote agent]
---

# Release builds

Recipe: [`build-release`](.claude/skills/build-release/SKILL.md).

## Bundles

From `app/ui`:

```sh
pnpm release --bundles appimage       # Linux AppImage with the remote agents
pnpm tauri build --bundles appimage   # Linux AppImage without them
pnpm tauri build --bundles deb,rpm    # Linux packages
pnpm tauri build                      # all bundles for this OS (dmg on macOS, msi/nsis on Windows)
```

`pnpm tauri` runs the Tauri CLI from `app/`; it builds the UI first (`pnpm build`). Output:
`target/release/bundle/<type>/` (e.g. `Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage`) and the plain binary
`target/release/forge`. A build from scratch takes about six minutes.

Cross-compiling is not supported: build Windows and macOS bundles on those systems.

## Official releases

Versions follow Pride Versioning and are bumped with `pnpm version:bump`; see
[Versioning](docs/guide/developer/versioning.md).

Publishing a GitHub release runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, and nothing else does. It:

1. builds the static remote agents on Linux,
2. builds the bundles on Ubuntu (AppImage, deb, rpm), Windows (NSIS, MSI) and macOS (Apple
   Silicon and Intel) with `pnpm tauri build --config src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json`,
3. signs the updater artifacts and uploads everything plus `latest.json` to the release.

Forge's updater reads `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json`,
so a published (not draft, not pre-release) release is what users get offered.

The workflow needs, once, in the repository settings:

| Name | Kind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | secret | private key from `pnpm tauri signer generate` |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | secret | its password |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` | secret or variable | the matching public key, built into the app |

Keep the private key offline as well: losing it means installed copies can no longer verify
updates.

## Updates and signing

Forge updates itself with `tauri-plugin-updater`: it reads `latest.json`, downloads the bundle
for its platform, verifies the bundle's minisign signature against the public key built into
the app, installs it and restarts. When and what to offer (once a day, skipped versions,
channel, version compare) is decided in [`forge-update`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-update.md); the shell side
is `app/src-tauri/src/commands/updates.rs` and the splash steps are in
`app/src-tauri/src/startup.rs`.

### Create the key pair (once)

```sh
cd app/ui
pnpm tauri signer generate -w ~/.tauri/forge.key   # asks for a password
```

This writes the private key `~/.tauri/forge.key` and the public key `~/.tauri/forge.key.pub`.

- Store the private key and its password as the secrets `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and
  `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` (repository settings), and in a password manager.
- Store the public key (the contents of `forge.key.pub`) as the secret (or variable) `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY`.
- Never commit either file. The public key is not secret, but it lives in the build
  environment, not in the repository, so forks and local builds do not pretend to be official.

### How the keys reach a build

`pnpm tauri` runs `app/ui/scripts/tauri.mjs`, which passes everything to the Tauri CLI and adds
one `--config` to `tauri build` (applied last):

| Build environment | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` set | `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts` on: every bundle gets a signed `.sig` next to it |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` not set | `createUpdaterArtifacts` off, so the build succeeds without the key (even though `tauri.agents.conf.json` turns it on for releases) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` set | written to `plugins.updater.pubkey`; the Rust code also compiles it in (`option_env!`) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` not set | the app never checks for updates: it logs "update checks are disabled: this build has no updater public key" and the Updates settings page says "Updates are not configured in this build" |

The release workflow's call `pnpm tauri build --config src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json` goes
through the same script, as does `pnpm release`. A local signed build:

```sh
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/forge.key)"
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD='…'
export FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/forge.key.pub)"
pnpm release --bundles appimage   # Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage + Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage.sig
```

### latest.json

The workflow's `tauri-action` (`includeUpdaterJson: true`) writes `latest.json` from the `.sig`
files and attaches it to the release. Its format, for a feed you publish yourself:

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "notes": "What changed.",
  "pub_date": "2026-11-02T10:00:00Z",
  "platforms": {
    "linux-x86_64": { "signature": "<contents of the .AppImage.sig>", "url": "https://…/Forge_0.2.0_amd64.AppImage" },
    "windows-x86_64": { "signature": "…", "url": "https://…/Forge_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe" },
    "darwin-aarch64": { "signature": "…", "url": "https://…/Forge.app.tar.gz" }
  }
}
```

Keys are `{os}-{arch}` or `{os}-{arch}-{installer}` (`linux-x86_64-deb`); the more specific one
wins. Forge also sends a `HEAD` request to the download to show its size.

| Setting | Feed |
| --- | --- |
| `updates.channel = stable` (default) | `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json` |
| `updates.channel = beta` | `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/download/beta/latest.json` (a release tagged `beta` whose `latest.json` is replaced for each pre-release) |
| `updates.endpoint` | any other URL; release builds require `https` |

On the stable channel versions with a pre-release part (`0.3.0-beta.1`) are never offered.

> **Note:** the release workflow publishes the stable feed only; nothing maintains the `beta`
> release yet, so the beta channel finds no feed (the check reports an error) until one exists.

### Trying the update flow without a release

Development builds never check for real updates. Simulate one instead; it shows the update
panel with a fake 94 MB download and installs nothing:

```sh
FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE=0.2.0 pnpm tauri dev
```

In browser mode: `http://localhost:1420/?splash&simulateUpdate=0.2.0` (the splash, then the
workbench) or `?simulateUpdate=0.2.0` with Help | Check for Updates…. To test a real update,
build a signed release of the old version, publish a feed with a newer signed build on a local
`https` server and point `updates.endpoint` at it.

## Remote agents

Remote projects need the headless agent (`forge-remote-agent`) for the host's architecture. Build
the static Linux agents first:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl          # aarch64-unknown-linux-musl as well
pnpm --dir app/ui agents                              # or: pnpm agents x86_64
```

This writes `target/agents/forge-remote-agent-{x86_64,aarch64}-linux.gz` (gzip-compressed,
because AppImage tools would patch an uncompressed ELF file in the bundle). Architectures whose
musl target is not installed are skipped. aarch64 needs a cross compiler and linker
(`CC_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl`, `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER`); the
tree-sitter C code of the native architecture is built with the host's `gcc` (fortify off).

`pnpm release` builds the agents and then the bundles with
`src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json`, which ships `target/agents/` as the bundle's `agents/`
resource folder. Arguments go to `tauri build`.

At runtime Forge looks for agents in `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR`, the bundle's `agents/`
resources, `agents/` next to its executable and `target/agents`; a development build of
`forge-remote-agent` next to the executable serves hosts of the same architecture. Plain or
`.gz` binaries are accepted. The agent is uploaded to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` on the
host.

## Smoke test on a headless Linux box

```sh
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1440x900x24" \
  sh -c './Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage /path/to/project & sleep 15; import -window root shot.png'
```

Check the screenshot: the splash appears first; then, without a project argument, the last
project or the Welcome screen; with one, the workbench, file tree and Git branch. Use a throwaway
`HOME` (or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) so the run does not reopen your own last project. Make sure the run created no files in the project
(`git status` stays clean).

## Versioning

The version (0.1.0) is set in `[workspace.package]` of the root `Cargo.toml`,
`app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and `app/ui/package.json`. The bundle identifier is
`dev.forge.ide`; the `forge://` scheme is declared under `plugins.deep-link` in
`tauri.conf.json`.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/search-benchmark.md

# Search benchmark

`crates/forge-search/examples/bench.rs` runs the same scenarios against any project folder and
prints a Markdown table. Run it before and after a change to the index, the matchers or Find in
Files, and keep a change only when the numbers support it.

```sh
cargo run --release -p forge-search --example bench -- <project folder>
```

Each scenario reports the best of three runs. The first build of the index depends on the disk
cache: run it twice and compare the second result.

## Baseline

Measured on a source tree (272,700 files, Windows 11, release build, files in the OS cache).

| Scenario | Best of 3 | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index | 5458 ms | 272700 files, 272700 added |
| Load saved index | 1287 ms | 272700 files, cache 283 MB |
| Refresh, nothing changed | 336 ms | 0 changed |
| Go to File `usr` | 7.5 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `ordctl` | 4.5 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `index.php` | 4.1 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `zzqxvk` (typo pass) | 37 ms | 1 hit |
| Go to File `index`, substring | 11.1 ms | 100 hits |
| Classes `order` | 1.5 ms | 50 hits |
| Classes `user` | 1.3 ms | 50 hits |
| Find `return` | 248 ms | 508159 matches in 36900 files |
| Find `->get(` | 16.5 ms | 3325 matches in 1029 files |
| Find `function \w+\(` regex | 137 ms | 138491 matches in 15722 files |
| Find `.*` regex | 1078 ms | 13462140 matches in 168727 files |
| Find rare word `zzqxv` | 6.5 ms | 23 matches in 6 files |
| Find `.*` regex, cancelled after 100 ms | 116 ms | Search cancelled |

The first cold index after a rebuild or a reboot took 77 s on the same folder, because the
files were not in the OS cache. That time is disk speed, not the index.

## Tried and rejected

Measured with the benchmark above on the same tree.

| Change | Result | Why not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rarest trigram first with early stop | `->get(` 16.5 to 19.8 ms, `return` 248 to 249 ms | Choosing candidates is not where the time goes; reading and scanning files is |
| Skip lockfiles, `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map` | About 20 MB of 272,700 files | Too little to gain, and Find in Files would stop matching them |
| Identifier-run trigrams instead of byte trigrams | Cache 283 to 169 MB, load 1287 to 861 ms, but `->get(` 16 to 274 ms | Queries with punctuation lose most of their narrowing; a hybrid needs both indexes |

## Against ripgrep

ripgrep 15.1.0 on the same folder, same excludes (`--hidden --no-require-git`, case-insensitive, `-c`, best of 3, nothing else running). It reads every file on each run; the index reads only the candidates.

| Query | ripgrep | Forge index |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `return` | 46,228 ms | 248 ms |
| `->get(` | 57,746 ms | 16.5 ms |
| `function \w+\(` regex | 11,914 ms | 137 ms |
| `.*` regex | 56,040 ms | 1,078 ms |
| `zzqxv` | 24,074 ms | 6.5 ms |

The ripgrep times are dominated by reading 272,700 files on this machine (virus scanning included) and vary a lot between runs, so read them as a gap in magnitude, not as exact ratios. No query was faster with ripgrep. The index costs a one-off build (5.5 s warm, 283 MB on disk) and a refresh (340 ms) that ripgrep does not need.

Source: docs/guide/developer/versioning.md

---
title: Versioning
description: Forge versions follow Pride Versioning (PROUD.DEFAULT.SHAME); bump them with pnpm version:bump and release by publishing a GitHub release.
order: 145
tags: [release, version, pridever, updates]
---

# Versioning

Forge versions follow [Pride Versioning](https://pridever.org) 0.3.0: **PROUD.DEFAULT.SHAME**.

| Part | Bump it for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROUD | a release we are really proud of; DEFAULT and SHAME go back to 0 | `1.2.3` → `2.0.0` |
| DEFAULT | a normal release; SHAME goes back to 0 | `1.2.3` → `1.3.0` |
| SHAME | a fix too embarrassing to admit | `1.2.3` → `1.2.4` |

The written form stays `X.Y.Z`, so Cargo, npm and Tauri's updater parse and order versions like
SemVer. Pre-releases use a SemVer label (`0.2.0-beta.1`); they go to the beta update channel
(`updates.channel`).

## Where the version lives

The same version is written in three files:

- `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version`; every crate inherits it),
- `app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (the bundles' version and what the updater compares),
- `app/ui/package.json`.

Never edit them by hand. From `app/ui`:

```sh
pnpm version:check                        # fails when the three files disagree
pnpm version:bump default                 # 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 in all three files + Cargo.lock
pnpm version:bump shame                   # 0.2.0 → 0.2.1
pnpm version:bump proud                   # 0.2.1 → 1.0.0
pnpm version:bump default --pre beta.1    # 1.0.0 → 1.1.0-beta.1
```

The script (`app/ui/scripts/version.mjs`, logic and tests in `versionBump.mjs`) updates
`Cargo.lock` for the workspace crates, prints the release tag and does nothing else: it never
commits, tags or publishes.

## Releasing a version

1. `pnpm version:bump <part>` and run the [quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md).
2. Commit (`Release 0.2.0`) and merge to the release branch.
3. On GitHub, publish a release tagged `v0.2.0` (a pre-release for `-beta` versions).
4. The [release workflow](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#official-releases) builds the bundles, signs them and
   uploads them with `latest.json`; installed copies offer the update on their next start.

> **Note:** Only the project owner bumps versions and publishes releases. Agents never bump a
> version unless they are asked to, and never publish releases.

Source: docs/guide/developer/git-workflow.md

---
title: Git workflow
description: Branch names, commit style, no trailers, manual-only CI, worktrees and keeping the documentation in step with changes.
order: 150
tags: [git, workflow, ci, commits]
---

# Git workflow

- Repository: <https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge>, default branch `main`.
- **Branch names** describe the work: `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `docs/…`, `chore/…`
  (`feat/laravel-plugin`, `fix/tree-double-click`, `docs/user-and-developer-guide`).
- **Small commits** with imperative English subjects: "Add routes tool window",
  "Fix double toggle of the Terminal".
- **No co-author or other trailers** in commit messages, and no mention of AI tools.
- **Commit early and often** during long tasks so work is not lost.
- Do not push or open pull requests unless you were asked to.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs **only on manual dispatch** (`workflow_dispatch`): UI
typecheck/test/build on Ubuntu, and fmt, clippy and tests on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS. Never
trigger workflows yourself, and every branch must keep the `workflow_dispatch`-only trigger.
Run the [quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md) locally instead.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs **only when a GitHub release is published**. It builds the
Linux, Windows and macOS bundles (with the remote agents), signs the updater artifacts and uploads
them plus `latest.json` to that release. Only the project owner publishes releases; never add
push, pull request or schedule triggers to any workflow. See [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md).

## Worktrees

Several git worktrees can build in parallel; give each its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (a shared target
dir can return stale builds of workspace crates) and consider `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`.

## Pull requests

- Run the quality gates.
- Attach screenshots for UI changes.
- Update the docs: the matching page in `docs/guide/` for every user-visible change (see
  [`docs/guide/README.md`](docs/guide/README.md)), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for new IPC contracts, the
  README and `docs/ROADMAP.md` for new plugins.

Every Rust crate of the workspace. The pages are generated from each crate's `lib.rs` documentation, module headers and `Cargo.toml`, plus the IPC commands in `app/src-tauri/src/commands/` that use it. The desktop shell itself is the crate `forge-app` in `app/src-tauri` (see [Architecture overview](docs/guide/developer/architecture.md)).

title: forge-agent-cli
description: "Runs AI coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) headless and normalizes their output."

---

# forge-agent-cli

`crates/forge-agent-cli` — Runs AI coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) headless and normalizes their output.

## Purpose

Drive AI coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, ...) headless and expose their
output as a normalized `AgentEvent` stream for Forge's chat UI.

Forge never ships credentials: each adapter runs the user's own installed CLI with its
own login or API key.

Every CLI is an `AgentCli` adapter: its command line, how messages reach it
(`Transport`), an `EventParser` from its stream format to `AgentEvent`s, permission
prompts and session resume. `profile` describes each one (models, permission modes,
install hint).

`conversation` folds the events into the chat as the UI renders it (with `diff`s of
edits and Markdown ASTs). It, the event/prompt/profile modules and the Gemini parser are
pure; the adapters and sessions need the `runtime` feature (default).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `claude.rs` | Claude Code adapter: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`. |
| `cli.rs` | The adapter trait every agent CLI implements, plus start options and detection. |
| `conversation.rs` | The chat conversation as the UI renders it: the `AgentEvent` stream folded into turns and blocks (text with its Markdown AST, thinking, tool cards with diffs, permission requests, errors), plus the derived texts the cards show. |
| `diff.rs` | Line diffs of edit tool calls (`Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `Write`) for the chat's edit cards and permission previews. |
| `event.rs` | The normalized event stream every agent adapter produces. The UI only knows these events, so adding a new CLI never touches the chat UI. |
| `gemini.rs` | Gemini CLI adapter: `gemini --output-format stream-json`, one process per turn. |
| `host.rs` | Where an agent CLI runs: this machine (`LocalHost`) or, for a project on a remote host, that host (the app implements `AgentHost` over the project backend's process API, so the CLI sees the project's files and its own login there). |
| `profile.rs` | Static descriptions of the built-in agent CLIs: models, permission modes as each CLI understands them, and how to install it. Pure, so the browser-mode mock shows the same picker entries as the desktop app. |
| `prompt.rs` | Turns a chat message plus editor context (attached files, selection) into the prompt text sent to the agent. |
| `session.rs` | Runs agent CLI processes for a conversation and streams their normalized events: one long-running process (`Transport::Persistent`) or one process per message (`Transport::PerTurn`). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use claude::ClaudeCode;
pub use cli::{…};
pub use conversation::{Chat, ChatUpdate, PermissionStatus};
pub use event::{AgentEvent, EventParser, Usage};
pub use gemini::GeminiCli;
pub use host::{AgentHost, LocalHost, SpawnedAgent};
pub use profile::{AgentProfile, PermissionMode, PermissionModeInfo};
pub use prompt::{compose_prompt, MessageContext, Selection};
pub use session::{AgentSession, EventSink};
pub fn builtin_agents() -> Vec<Arc<dyn AgentCli>> { … }
pub fn agent_by_id(id: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn AgentCli>> { … }
pub fn pure_parser(agent_id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn EventParser>> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `agent_list`, `agent_start`, `agent_send`, `agent_respond_permission`, `agent_interrupt`, `agent_stop` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ai-chat`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-markdown`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-markdown.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `similar`, `tokio`, `tracing`
- Features: `default` = `runtime`; `runtime` = `dep:forge-core`, `dep:tokio`, `dep:tracing`

# forge-ai

`crates/forge-ai` — Forge IDE AI provider layer: Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible chat models.

## Purpose

Forge AI provider layer.

A `Provider` turns a provider-neutral `CompletionRequest` into a one-shot
`Completion` or a stream of `Delta`s. Two wire protocols are implemented:
the Anthropic Messages API and OpenAI-compatible chat completions (OpenAI, OpenRouter,
LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, custom servers). `AiService` stores provider configs in
`ai.toml` and API keys in the OS keychain.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `anthropic.rs` | Anthropic Messages API (`POST /v1/messages`). |
| `config.rs` | Provider configuration, persisted as TOML in `<config dir>/forge/ai.toml`. API keys are never written here; see `crate::secrets`. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `openai.rs` | OpenAI-compatible chat completions (`POST {base}/chat/completions`): OpenAI, OpenRouter, LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp server and any other compatible endpoint. |
| `provider.rs` | The `Provider` trait plus HTTP helpers shared by the implementations. |
| `secrets.rs` | API key storage: the OS keychain (service `forge-ai`, account = provider id) with an environment-variable fallback per provider kind. |
| `service.rs` | `AiService`: owns the provider config + key store and builds providers on demand. This is what the app's IPC layer talks to. |
| `sse.rs` | Minimal Server-Sent Events parser (WHATWG event-stream format). |
| `types.rs` | Provider-neutral request/response types. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use config::{…};
pub use error::{AiError, AiResult};
pub use provider::{cancellable, collect_text, DeltaStream, Endpoint, Provider};
pub use secrets::{KeySource, KeyringStore, MemoryStore, SecretStore};
pub use service::{AiService, ProviderInfo, ProvidersState, TestResult};
pub use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;
pub use types::{…};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `ai_complete`, `ai_stream`, `ai_cancel`, `ai_providers_list`, `ai_provider_save`, `ai_provider_delete`, `ai_provider_test`, `ai_models`, `ai_set_default` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/ai.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ai`, `app/ui/src/features/git (AI commit messages)`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- External: `async-stream`, `async-trait`, `bytes`, `dirs`, `futures-util`, `keyring`, `reqwest`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `toml`, `tracing`

order: 30

# forge-backend

`crates/forge-backend` — Forge IDE project backends: the Backend trait, the local backend and the remote agent protocol.

## Purpose

Project backends: where an open project's files, git, processes, language servers and
PHP index live.

- `Backend` is what the app's workspace, file system, git, terminal, run, LSP and PHP
  commands talk to. The UI never knows which implementation answers.
- `LocalBackend` serves a folder on this machine.
- `RemoteBackend` serves a folder on another machine through the Forge agent
  (`crates/forge-remote-agent`), which is itself a `LocalBackend` behind the
  `protocol`. `rpc::RpcClient` multiplexes calls, events and byte channels over any
  stream (SSH in `crates/forge-remote`, an in-memory pipe in tests).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `frameworks.rs` | Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine analysis of a project, run where its files are. |
| `langservers.rs` | Which catalog language servers (`forge-langservers`) start for a project, planned on the machine that has the project's files and the installed servers: the desktop app for a local project, the Forge agent for a remote one (its servers then start on the host through the LSP byte channel). |
| `local.rs` | A project folder on this machine. |
| `paths.rs` | Path helpers that do not touch the file system (the project may live on another machine). |
| `php.rs` | The PHP index of a project and the PHP language server lookup, wherever the project lives. Offsets are UTF-16 (JS strings), see `phpforge_lang_php::service`. |
| `process_io.rs` | Processes started through a `Backend` (on this machine or on a remote host) used like local child processes: line by line with cancelation (`run_lines`, artisan and Symfony console runs) or as async stdio streams (`spawn_stdio`, agent CLIs). |
| `protocol.rs` | The Forge agent protocol: MessagePack frames over a byte stream (the agent's stdio). |
| `remote.rs` | A project on another machine, served by the Forge agent over an `RpcClient`. |
| `rpc.rs` | The client end of the agent `protocol`(crate::protocol): calls with out-of-order answers, pushed events and byte channels over one stream pair. |
| `tunnels.rs` | Port forwarding between this machine and a remote project's host (SSH tunnels). Local projects have none; `forge-remote` implements them over the project's SSH connection. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use frameworks::{framework_call, FrameworkCall};
pub use langservers::{LangServersAnswer, LangServersRequest};
pub use local::LocalBackend;
pub use php::PhpBackend;
pub use remote::RemoteBackend;
pub use tunnels::{PortForward, Tunnels};
pub struct RemoteHost { … }
pub struct BackendInfo { … }
pub struct TerminalSpec { … }
pub trait Terminal: Send + Sync { … }
pub trait Process: Send + Sync { … }
pub trait Backend: Send + Sync { … }
pub struct BackendFiles(pub Arc<dyn Backend>);
pub fn folder_name(root: &Path) -> String { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: every project command (workspace, fs, git, terminal, run, php, lua) goes through `AppState::backend()`
- UI: `app/ui/src/state/workspace.ts`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-langservers`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-langservers.md), [`forge-lsp`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-lsp.md), [`forge-process`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-process.md), [`forge-project`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-project.md), [`forge-vcs`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vcs.md), [`phpforge-dql`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-dql.md), [`phpforge-fw-laravel`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-fw-laravel.md), [`phpforge-fw-symfony`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-fw-symfony.md), [`phpforge-lang-php`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-lang-php.md), [`phpforge-orm-doctrine`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-orm-doctrine.md)
- External: `dirs`, `futures-util`, `rmp-serde`, `serde`, `serde_bytes`, `serde_json`, `tokio`, `tracing`

## Tests

---
title: forge-containers
description: "Forge IDE containers: Docker Engine API, Docker Compose and Kubernetes for the Services tool window."
order: 40
tags: [crate, rust]
---

# forge-containers

`crates/forge-containers` — Forge IDE containers: Docker Engine API, Docker Compose and Kubernetes for the Services tool window.

## Purpose

Containers for the Services tool window: Docker, Docker Compose and Kubernetes.

Pure parts (no I/O, built for WebAssembly too):
- `docker`: Docker Engine API JSON (containers, images, volumes, networks) into models.
- `compose`: `compose.yaml` / `docker-compose.yml` parsing, project names, command lines
  and the mapping of containers to services by their labels.
- `kube`: kubeconfig parsing and Kubernetes API objects (pods, deployments, services).
- `logs`: the multiplexed Docker log stream and Kubernetes log lines.
- `pull`: image pull progress from the Engine's JSON messages.
- `endpoint`: where the Docker daemon is (`DOCKER_HOST`, settings, platform defaults).
- `tree`: the Services tree, details (Dashboard / Inspection) and toolbar state.
- `gutter`: ▶ markers for compose services and Dockerfiles.
- `portforward`: the Kubernetes port-forward channel protocol and active forwards.
- `ws`: WebSocket handshake and framing (Kubernetes streaming subresources).

With the `runtime` feature: an HTTP/1.1 client over Unix sockets, Windows named pipes,
TCP (+TLS) and SSH-forwarded sockets (`http`, `ssh`), the Docker Engine client
(`engine`), the Kubernetes API client (`kubeclient`), port-forward connections
(`forward`), compose / CLI processes (`cli`) and registry credentials in the OS
keychain (`secrets`), and the `hub` that holds the Services state for the app.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `cli.rs` | `docker compose …`, `docker build` / `docker run` (Dockerfile ▶) and other CLI runs with their output streamed line by line. Compose has no Engine API, so these are processes; everything else talks to the Engine directly (`crate::engine`). |
| `compose.rs` | Docker Compose files (`compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, overrides): services with their images, builds, ports, profiles and env files, the project name, `${VAR}` interpolation from the project's `.env`, and the `docker compose` command lines. |
| `docker.rs` | Docker Engine API objects (`GET /containers/json`, `/images/json`, `/volumes`, `/networks`, `/version`) as models for the tree. The raw JSON is parsed leniently: missing fields get defaults so older and newer Engine versions both work. |
| `endpoint.rs` | Where the Docker daemon listens: Settings \| Build, Execution, Deployment \| Docker (`docker.connection`, `docker.socketPath`, `docker.tcp.*`, `docker.ssh.*`, `docker.context`), else `DOCKER_HOST`, else the current Docker context (`~/.docker/contexts`), else the platform default (named pipe on Windows; `/var/run/docker.sock`, Docker Desktop's `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`, rootless `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock` or Podman elsewhere). |
| `engine.rs` | Docker Engine API client (no CLI): snapshot of containers, images, volumes and networks, container lifecycle, inspect, log streaming, image pulls with progress and the event stream that tells the tree to refresh. |
| `exec.rs` | Interactive command lines that run in a terminal PTY: a shell inside a container (`docker exec -it`), attaching to a container's console (`docker attach`) and a shell in a pod (`kubectl exec -it`) and attaching to a pod's container (`kubectl attach -it`). |
| `forward.rs` | Port-forward connections: the WebSocket upgrade to a pod's `portforward` subresource and the pump between a local TCP connection and the pod port (`crate::portforward` has the channel protocol, `crate::ws` the framing). |
| `gutter.rs` | ▶ gutter markers: on `services:` (up all) and every service of a compose file (up one), and on the first `FROM` of a Dockerfile (build the image and run a container), plus the command lines those markers run. |
| `http.rs` | A small HTTP/1.1 client for the Docker Engine API and the Kubernetes API server: one connection per request over a Unix socket, a Windows named pipe or TCP (optionally TLS), `Content-Length`, chunked and read-to-close bodies, and streaming bodies for logs, events and pulls. |
| `hub.rs` | The Services backend: one `Hub` per app holds the Docker connection (with a watcher that follows the Engine's events and reconnects), the project's compose files, the kubeconfig with lazily loaded namespaces and workloads, running log streams and the consoles (Log tabs). |
| `kube.rs` | Kubernetes: kubeconfig files (clusters, users, contexts) and the API objects the tree shows (namespaces, pods, deployments, services). |
| `kubeclient.rs` | Kubernetes API client for one kubeconfig context: TLS with the cluster's CA (rustls), bearer tokens, client certificates, basic auth and exec credential plugins (`gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`, `aws eks get-token`, …). |
| `logs.rs` | Container log streams. |
| `portforward.rs` | Kubernetes port forwarding (`kubectl port-forward`, PHPStorm's Forward Ports): the `portforward` subresource over a WebSocket with the `v4.channel.k8s.io` channel protocol, and the list of active forwards the Services tool window shows. |
| `pull.rs` | Image pulls: `POST /images/create?fromImage=…` answers with one JSON message per line (`{"status":"Downloading","id":"a1b2","progressDetail":{"current":1,"total":9}}`). |
| `secrets.rs` | Docker registry credentials in the OS keychain (service `forge-containers`, account `registry:<server>`). The list of servers and user names is not secret and is passed in by the caller (settings); only passwords and tokens go to the keychain. |
| `ssh.rs` | The Docker API of an `ssh://user@host` daemon: one SSH session (`forge-remote`: ssh-agent, `~/.ssh` keys and `~/.ssh/config`, `known_hosts`) and a forwarded Unix socket (`direct-streamlocal`) to the daemon's socket per HTTP request. |
| `time.rs` | Timestamps: RFC 3339 parsing (Kubernetes, volumes) and the "5 minutes ago" texts. |
| `tree.rs` | The Services tool window model: the tree (Docker → Containers / Images / Networks / Volumes, Docker Compose → projects → services → containers, Kubernetes → contexts → namespaces → Pods / Deployments / Services), the details pane (Dashboard rows, available tabs) and which toolbar actions apply to a node. |
| `ws.rs` | WebSocket (RFC 6455) pieces for the Kubernetes streaming subresources: the upgrade handshake headers and `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` check, frame encoding (client frames are masked) and an incremental frame decoder that also joins fragmented messages. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct Error(pub String);
```

## Used by

- IPC: `services_tree`, `services_refresh`, `services_compose_changed`, `services_expand`, `services_details`, `services_action`, `services_inspect`, `services_console`, `services_logs_start`, `services_logs_stop`, `services_terminal`, `services_port_forward_start`, `services_port_forward_stop`, `services_port_forwards`, `services_pull`, `services_compose_up`, `services_dockerfile_run`, `services_gutter`, `services_status`, `docker_test_connection`, `docker_contexts`, `docker_registry_login`, `docker_registry_logout`, `docker_registry_status` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/services.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/services`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-remote`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-remote.md)
- External: `base64`, `dirs`, `keyring`, `rustls`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha1`, `tokio`, `tokio-rustls`, `tracing`, `webpki-roots`, `yaml-rust2`
- Features: `default` = `runtime`; `runtime` = `dep:tokio`, `dep:rustls`, `dep:tokio-rustls`, `dep:webpki-roots`, `dep:keyring`, `dep:dirs`, `dep:tracing`, `forge-remote/client`

## Tests

21 source files, about 11468 lines; 65 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-containers
```

# forge-db

`crates/forge-db` — Forge IDE database tools: data sources, introspection, query execution and data editing.

## Purpose

Forge database tools (the DataGrip part of Forge).

- `config`: data sources in `.forge/dataSources.toml` and the global file;
  passwords in the OS keychain (`secrets`, service `forge-db`).
- `env`: suggestions from Laravel `DB_*` and Symfony `DATABASE_URL`.
- `conn`: MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite pools via `sqlx`.
- `introspect`, `ddl`: schemas, tables, columns, keys, indexes, routines, DDL.
- `service::DbService`: consoles with transactions and cancel, table paging, row
  editing (`edit`) and export (`export`).
- `value`, `split`, `export`: re-exported from the pure `forge-sql` crate.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `config.rs` | Data source configuration: `.forge/dataSources.toml` in the project and `<config dir>/forge/dataSources.toml` for global data sources. Passwords never go into these files; they live in the OS keychain (see `crate::secrets`). |
| `conn.rs` | Driver-neutral pools and connections. All SQL is sent as raw text (MySQL text protocol, PostgreSQL simple query protocol), so every statement type works and values arrive in a uniform text form that `crate::value` converts. |
| `ddl.rs` | Table DDL: read from the server where it keeps it (MySQL `SHOW CREATE`, SQLite `sqlite_master`), otherwise generated from introspection (PostgreSQL). |
| `edit.rs` | Row editing from the data grid; the statements are built by `forge_sql::edit`. |
| `env.rs` | Data sources suggested from a project's `.env` files: Laravel's `DB_*` variables and Symfony/Doctrine's `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `introspect.rs` | Database metadata: schemas, tables, views, columns, keys, indexes and routines. |
| `secrets.rs` | Data source passwords: the OS keychain (service `forge-db`, account = data source id). |
| `service.rs` | `DbService`: data sources of the open project plus global ones, their pools, console sessions with transaction state, table data paging and row editing. |
| `tunnel.rs` | Data sources of a project on a remote host connect through its SSH connection: the database host and port are as the remote host sees them (`localhost` is the remote machine), reached through a local port forwarded with a `direct-tcpip` channel. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use forge_sql::{export, split, value};
pub use config::{DataSource, DataSourceOptions, Dialect, Driver, Scope, SslMode};
pub use conn::{ColumnMeta, DbPool, RawResult};
pub use edit::{ChangeKind, RowChange};
pub use env::DetectedDataSource;
pub use error::{DbError, DbResult};
pub use forge_sql::ExportFormat;
pub use introspect::{…};
pub use secrets::{KeyringStore, MemoryStore, SecretStore};
pub use service::{…};
pub use split::{split_statements, Statement};
pub use tunnel::{DbTunnel, ProjectContext, TunnelEndpoint};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `db_data_sources_list`, `db_data_source_save`, `db_data_source_delete`, `db_test_connection`, `db_disconnect`, `db_schemas`, `db_introspect`, `db_table_info`, `db_table_ddl`, `db_table_data`, `db_apply_changes`, `db_session_open`, `db_session_close`, `db_execute`, `db_fetch`, `db_set_auto_commit`, `db_commit`, `db_rollback`, `db_cancel`, `db_detect_env`, `db_add_from_env`, `db_export`, `db_statement_at` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/db.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/database`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-sql`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-sql.md)
- External: `dirs`, `futures-util`, `hex`, `keyring`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sqlx`, `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `toml`, `tracing`

# forge-debug

`crates/forge-debug` — Forge IDE debugger: DBGp (Xdebug 3) server, path mappings and breakpoints.

## Purpose

Forge's PHP debugger: a DBGp server for Xdebug 3.

- `DebugServer` listens for Xdebug (default port 9003), accepts any number of
  connections and turns each into a `Session`.
- Sessions identify their server (`PHP_IDE_CONFIG`, `SERVER_NAME`), map server paths to
  project files (`PathMapper`), set the project's breakpoints and report state changes
  as `DebugEvent`s.
- Breakpoints live in `<project>/.forge/breakpoints.json`, servers with their path
  mappings in `<project>/.forge/php-servers.json`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `breakpoints.rs` | Project breakpoints, persisted in `<project>/.forge/breakpoints.json`. |
| `config.rs` |  |
| `connection.rs` | One DBGp connection: writes commands with transaction ids and routes the engine's answers back to the waiting caller. Packets that are not answers (`stream`, `notify`) go to a callback. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `events.rs` |  |
| `mapping.rs` | Server ↔ local path mappings (PHPStorm's "Servers > Use path mappings"). |
| `protocol.rs` | DBGp wire format and typed views of the engine's answers. |
| `server.rs` | The DBGp listener ("Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections") and the registry of sessions, breakpoints and servers it shares with them. |
| `servers.rs` | PHP servers (PHPStorm's "Settings > PHP > Servers"): which host a debug connection comes from and how its paths map into the project. Stored per project in `<project>/.forge/php-servers.json`. |
| `session.rs` | A debug session: one script run connected through DBGp. |
| `xml.rs` | A tiny DOM for DBGp messages. Responses are small, so building a tree is simpler than streaming and keeps the typed parsers in `protocol.rs` readable. |

## Main public items

```rust

```

# forge-filetypes

`crates/forge-filetypes` — File type recognition for Forge: names, extensions, shebangs and template data languages (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

File type recognition (PHPStorm's Settings | Editor | File Types): which language a file
is, what the status bar calls it, its indentation and, for template languages, the data
language between the template tags.

The bundled types (`builtin_file_types`) are extended or replaced by the file types of
plugin manifests (`[[plugin.contributions.fileTypes]]`). Detection prefers, in order:
file names and path patterns, the longest matching extension (so `x.blade.php` beats
`php`), and the interpreter of a `#!` line. Later registrations win ties.

The crate is pure so the desktop app (IPC) and the browser-mode UI (WebAssembly) share it.
The UI only maps a file type id to its CodeMirror syntax mode.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `builtin.rs` | File types every Forge installation knows (PHPStorm's bundled file types). Plugins add more, or replace one of these by contributing a file type with the same id, through `[[plugin.contributions.fileTypes]]` in their manifests. |
| `data.rs` | Template Data Languages (as in PHPStorm): the language of the content *between* template tags. |
| `glob.rs` | The two pattern flavours of file type settings. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use builtin::builtin_file_types;
pub use data::{data_language_for, DataLanguage, DATA_LANGUAGES};
pub use glob::{matches_glob_list, wildcard_match};
pub struct FileTypeSpec { … }
pub struct FileTypeRegistry { … }
pub struct DetectRequest { … }
pub struct FileRef { … }
pub struct FileTypeInfo { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `filetypes_detect`
- UI: `app/ui/src/editor/fileTypes.ts`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`

## Tests

5 source files, about 1004 lines; 12 unit tests.


Source: docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-find.md

# forge-find

`crates/forge-find` — Find in Files: query compilation, file masks and line matching (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Find in Files (PHPStorm's Ctrl+Shift+F): the search request, file masks and per-line
matching. The crate is pure so the desktop backend (walking the project with
`forge-core`), the remote agent and the browser-mode WebAssembly build share it.

- The query is a literal or a regular expression (`regex` syntax), optionally
  case-sensitive and limited to whole words.
- The file mask is a comma-separated list of globs (`*.php, *.twig`); `!` excludes
  (`!*Test.php`). A glob without `/` matches the file name, otherwise the whole path.
- Matches are reported per line, like PHPStorm's result list: the line text (trimmed and
  cut around the first match) with every match range in it. Columns and ranges are UTF-16
  offsets so the UI can use them directly.

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct FindRequest { … }
pub struct LineMatch { … }
pub struct FileMatches { … }
pub struct FindResult { … }
pub struct FileMask { … }
pub fn glob_match(glob: &str, text: &str) -> bool { … }
pub struct Finder { … }
pub fn is_binary(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool { … }
pub struct Collector<'a> { … }
pub fn find_in<'t>(
```

## Used by

- IPC: `find_in_files` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/workspace.rs`, a `Backend` method, agent call `FindInFiles`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/find`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `regex`, `serde`

# forge-forges

`crates/forge-forges` — Forge IDE code hosts: GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub merge requests, issues and pipelines.

## Purpose

Forge code hosts: GitLab (REST v4), Forgejo/Gitea (`/api/v1`) and GitHub (REST, plus
GraphQL for review threads) behind one `CodeHost` trait.

Repositories are detected from `git remote -v` (`remote`); accounts and their tokens
(OS keychain, service `forge-forges`) are managed by `ForgeService`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `accounts.rs` | Code host accounts. The list lives in `<config dir>/forge/forges.toml`; tokens are kept in the OS keychain (service `forge-forges`, account = account id), never in files. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `forgejo.rs` | Forgejo and Gitea (`/api/v1`, `Authorization: token ...`). Both share the API; Codeberg runs Forgejo. Pull request review comments are grouped into threads by file and line, since the API has no thread objects. |
| `github.rs` | GitHub REST API (github.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, `Authorization: Bearer`). Review threads are rebuilt from `in_reply_to_id`; their resolved state and resolving use the GraphQL API, which REST does not cover. |
| `gitlab.rs` | GitLab REST API v4 (gitlab.com and self-managed). Authentication with a personal access token (`PRIVATE-TOKEN`). Projects are addressed by their URL-encoded full path, so nested groups work without looking up numeric ids. |
| `host.rs` | The `CodeHost` trait implemented by GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub. |
| `http.rs` | A small JSON REST client shared by the host implementations: authentication headers, `Link`-header pagination and translating HTTP failures into friendly `HostError`s. |
| `json.rs` | Lenient accessors for API JSON. Hosts differ between versions (fields appear, vanish or become null), so missing values fall back to defaults instead of failing a whole list. |
| `model.rs` | Host-neutral types for merge requests, issues and pipelines. GitHub and Forgejo call merge requests "pull requests"; the UI picks the wording from `HostKind`. |
| `remote.rs` | Detect the code host and project of a repository from its git remotes (`https://`, `ssh://`, scp-like `git@host:path`, nested GitLab groups, self-hosted servers known through accounts). |
| `service.rs` | Accounts plus host construction: the entry point the IDE uses. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use accounts::{Account, KeyringStore, MemoryStore, SecretStore, KEYCHAIN_SERVICE};
pub use error::{HostError, HostResult};
pub use forgejo::Forgejo;
pub use github::GitHub;
pub use gitlab::GitLab;
pub use host::CodeHost;
pub use model::*;
pub use service::{open_host, review_ref, AccountInfo, ForgeService, TokenSource};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `forges_accounts`, `forges_login`, `forges_logout`, `forges_verify`, `forges_repo`, `forges_merge_requests`, `forges_merge_request`, `forges_mr_files`, `forges_discussions`, `forges_create_mr`, `forges_comment`, `forges_reply`, `forges_resolve`, `forges_approve`, `forges_merge`, `forges_close`, `forges_issues`, `forges_issue`, `forges_issue_comment`, `forges_pipelines`, `forges_ci_status`, `forges_members`, `forges_file`, `forges_checkout` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/forges.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/forges`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-vcs`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vcs.md)

# forge-fuzzy

`crates/forge-fuzzy` — PHPStorm-style fuzzy matching and Search Everywhere ranking (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

PHPStorm-style fuzzy matching, shared by the backend ("Go to File" over the file system)
and the UI (Search Everywhere, Recent Files, popups) through IPC and WebAssembly.

Query characters must appear in order (case-insensitive). Matches at the start, after
separators (`/ _ - . : $` and spaces) and on camel humps score higher, as do runs of
consecutive characters, so `OrCo` ranks `OrderController` first. The crate is pure (no
file system or threads) so it compiles to WebAssembly for browser mode.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `everywhere.rs` | Search Everywhere ranking: merges the candidates of all providers of a tab, scores them against the query, dedupes the "All" tab and cuts each group to its page size. |

```rust
pub fn rank_files<'a>(
pub enum FilterCandidate { … }
pub struct FilterRequest { … }
pub struct FilterHit { … }
pub fn filter(req: &FilterRequest) -> Vec<FilterHit> { … }
```

# forge-keymap

`crates/forge-keymap` — PHPStorm-compatible keymap: shortcut model, default keymaps, overrides, conflicts and the key resolver.

## Purpose

Forge's PHPStorm-compatible keymap engine.

- `shortcut`: parsing ("Ctrl+K Ctrl+C", "Shift Shift", "Cmd+,"), canonical ids, display
  strings ("Ctrl+Shift+A" / "⇧⌘A") and key names of DOM keyboard events.
- `catalog`: PHPStorm's default keymaps (Windows/Linux and macOS) and action aliases.
- `engine`: bindings, conflict detection and the `Resolver` state machine that turns
  key events into actions (chords, double taps, focus contexts).
- `keymap`: the `KeymapService` combining the catalog, plugin actions, registered
  commands and user overrides from the settings.
- `menu`: the main menu (PHPStorm's structure, plugin contributions, resolution).

The crate is pure (no file system or async runtime): the desktop app wraps it in IPC
commands, and browser mode runs the same code as WebAssembly (`crates/forge-wasm`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `catalog.rs` | PHPStorm's default keymaps as data: "Windows/Linux" (`$default`) and "macOS". |
| `engine.rs` | Bindings, conflict detection and the resolver state machine that turns key events into action ids. |
| `keymap.rs` | The keymap as the IDE sees it: the PHPStorm catalog, actions contributed by plugins and commands, the user's overrides from the settings, and the resolver built from all of it. |
| `menu.rs` | The main menu (PHPStorm's New UI hamburger menu and the classic menu bar) as data. |
| `shortcut.rs` | Keyboard shortcut model: parsing of PHPStorm-style strings, formatting for display (Windows/Linux text or macOS symbols) and conversion from DOM keyboard events. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use catalog::{catalog, ActionContext, ActionDef, KeymapId};
pub use engine::{FocusContext, KeyInput, Pending, Resolution, Resolver};
pub use keymap::{…};
pub use menu::{MainMenu, MainMenuRequest, MenuContribution, MenuEntry, MenuItem};
pub use shortcut::{KeyEvent, Platform, Shortcut};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `keymap_actions`, `keymap_register_actions`, `keymap_set_override`, `keymap_conflicts`, `keymap_find_by_shortcut`, `keymap_main_menu`, `keymap_resolve`, `keymap_import_legacy` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/keymap.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/keymap/`, `app/ui/src/features/keymapSettings`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

# forge-langservers

`crates/forge-langservers` — Forge IDE: catalog, detection, configuration and installation of language servers.

## Purpose

Forge's catalog of language servers for many languages, and everything around it:

- `catalog`: the data-driven catalog (`catalog.toml`) of languages and servers with
  commands, initialization options, settings, install hints and licences,
- `detect`: finding installed servers (PATH, npm/nvm/volta, pip/pipx, cargo, go,
  dotnet, gem, Mason, Windows `.cmd` shims),
- `scan`: which languages a project uses,
- `config`: building a `forge_lsp::LspServerConfig` for a project,
- `plan`: which servers start, and the rows of the settings page,
- `install`: running an install command with streamed output,
- `managed`: installs of npm servers without prerequisites (Node.js and packages
  downloaded and verified into Forge's data directory) and their update check,
- `licence`: the Intelephense licence key in the OS keychain.

PHP servers (Intelephense, phpactor) stay in the PHP pack; the app lists them next to
these rows.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/forge-langservers.rs` | Pre-install npm language servers the way Forge does (`pnpm langservers` in `app/ui`): Node.js (if missing) and the packages go into Forge's data directory, so `pnpm tauri dev` and installed builds find them at once. |
| `catalog.rs` | The built-in catalog (`catalog.toml`): languages Forge detects in projects and the language servers that serve them. |
| `config.rs` | Turning a catalog entry into a `LspServerConfig` for one project: file routing, user overrides and the project specific bits some servers need (TypeScript SDK, the Vue TypeScript plugin, ESLint's workspace folder, jdtls' data directory, Lua runtime). |
| `detect.rs` | Finding installed language servers: `PATH` plus the places package managers put executables that are often missing from `PATH` in a desktop session (npm global prefix, nvm/fnm/volta, `~/.local/bin` for pip/pipx, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/go/bin`, `~/.dotnet/tools`, gem user dirs and Neovim's Mason directory). |
| `install.rs` | Running an install command (`npm install …`, `pipx install …`) with streamed output. Commands come from the catalog only and run without a shell. |
| `licence.rs` | Intelephense licence key: kept in the OS keychain (service `forge-lsp`, account `intelephense`), never in settings files. |
| `managed/archive.rs` | Unpacking downloaded archives (`.tgz` npm tarballs, Node.js `.tar.gz` and `.zip` builds) into a directory. Entries are checked before anything is written: absolute paths, `..` components and symlinks pointing outside the destination are refused. |
| `managed/http.rs` | A small HTTP client for downloads with progress (Node.js builds, npm metadata and tarballs). The system proxy settings (`HTTPS_PROXY`, …) are honoured. |
| `managed/mod.rs` | Zero-prerequisite installs of npm language servers (Intelephense, typescript-language-server, vscode-langservers-extracted, yaml-language-server, …) on the user's machine: |
| `managed/node.rs` | A Node.js runtime for npm language servers: a suitable one on the machine (>= 18), or the official build from nodejs.org (or a mirror) downloaded into `<data dir>/forge/runtimes/node-<version>`, verified against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. |
| `managed/npm.rs` | npm packages without npm: registry metadata, tarball download with `dist.integrity` (sha512) verification, unpacking into `<managed dir>/node_modules/<name>` and the `node_modules/.bin` entries detection looks for. |
| `managed/testserver.rs` | A tiny HTTP/1.1 server on localhost for tests: fixed bodies per path, request counts. |
| `managed/updates.rs` | "A newer version is available": at most one registry check a day, remembered in `<managed dir>/.forge-update-check.json`. |
| `plan.rs` | Which servers to start for a project, and the rows of the Language Servers settings page. |
| `prefs.rs` | User preferences for language servers, read from Forge settings. |
| `scan.rs` | Quick scan of a project: which catalog languages occur (by file name, honouring `.gitignore`, capped), which root files exist and which npm packages it depends on. |

## Main public items

```rust

pub use config::{build_config, merge_json, ConfigContext};
pub use detect::{DetectEnv, Detector};
pub use plan::{plan, rows, Decision, LiveState, RowStatus, ServerRow, Skip};

```

- UI: `app/ui/src/features/langservers`

# forge-lsp

`crates/forge-lsp` — Forge IDE: generic Language Server Protocol client and server manager.

## Purpose

Forge's generic Language Server Protocol client.

- `framing`: `Content-Length` JSON-RPC framing over stdio.
- `LspClient`: one server process; request/response correlation, notifications,
  answers to server→client requests, document sync and typed feature requests.
- `LspManager`: routes files to servers by extension and starts them lazily; several
  servers may serve one file and their results are merged.
- `model`: editor-friendly result types consumed by the UI.
- `launch`: how server processes start (`LocalLauncher` here, or on a remote host).

Nothing here is language specific; language packs contribute `LspServerConfig`s.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `client.rs` | An LSP client talking to one language server process over stdio. |
| `config.rs` | Language server configuration as contributed by language packs. |
| `framing.rs` | JSON-RPC message framing used by LSP over stdio: a `Content-Length` header block, an empty line, then exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. |
| `launch.rs` | Starting language server processes. `LocalLauncher` spawns them on this machine; other launchers start them elsewhere (on a remote development host) and hand back their stdio as streams, so `LspClient`(crate::LspClient) works the same either way. |
| `manager.rs` | Routes files to language servers: one server per registered config, started lazily the first time a matching file is used. |
| `model.rs` | Editor-friendly views of LSP results. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use client::{path_to_uri, uri_to_path, LspClient, LspEvent, ServerState};
pub use config::{find_on_path, LspServerConfig};
pub use launch::{LocalLauncher, ServerIo, ServerLauncher, ServerProcess};
pub use lsp_types;
pub use manager::{LspManager, ServerStatus, COMPLETION_SERVER_KEY};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `lsp_did_open`, `lsp_did_change`, `lsp_did_save`, `lsp_did_close`, `lsp_hover`, `lsp_completion`, `lsp_completion_resolve`, `lsp_definition`, `lsp_references`, `lsp_document_symbols`, `lsp_signature_help`, `lsp_format`, `lsp_status`, `lsp_register_server` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/lsp.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/lsp`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md)
- External: `futures-util`, `lsp-types`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `tokio`, `tracing`

## Tests

7 source files, about 2596 lines; 17 unit tests and 4 integration tests in `tests/` (`fake_server.rs`).

# forge-markdown

`crates/forge-markdown` — Forge Markdown: a safe AST (no raw HTML) for chat messages and documentation popups, built with pulldown-cmark (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Markdown as a safe AST for the UI, which renders it with Solid components (never as
HTML). Raw HTML is never passed through: in chat messages it stays literal text, in
documentation `<br>`/`<p>` become line breaks and every other tag is dropped.

- `parse`: Markdown into `Block`s (`Flavor::Chat` or `Flavor::Docs`).
- `hover`: language server hover Markdown (Intelephense & co.) split into the parts of
  a PHPStorm-style documentation popup.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `ast.rs` | The Markdown AST sent to the UI (JSON tagged by `t`). |
| `hover.rs` | Language server hovers (Markdown as Intelephense, phpactor & co. send it) split into the parts of a PHPStorm-style documentation popup: owner FQCN, signature, description and `Params:` / `Returns:` / `Throws:` sections. |
| `parse.rs` | pulldown-cmark events into the `Block` tree. |

## Main public items

# forge-open

`crates/forge-open` — Forge IDE open requests: forge:// links, the CLI launcher and the Browser Companion local server.

## Purpose

Opening files in Forge from the outside world:

- `request`: open requests and `forge://open?file=…&line=…` links,
- `cli`: the `forge path/to/file:12` launcher,
- `resolve`: which project a file belongs to (open, recent, or none),
- `symbols`: find a component/class declaration by name,
- `server` + `pairing`: the Browser Companion's local HTTP API,
- `project`: project detection and dotenv edits for framework integrations.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `cli.rs` | Command-line launcher: `forge [project-dir]`, `forge path/to/file:12[:3]`, `forge --line 12 --column 3 file` (JetBrains style), `forge file 12 3` (launch-editor) and `forge forge://open?...`. |
| `http.rs` | A deliberately tiny HTTP/1.1 subset for the local Browser Companion API: one request per connection, `Content-Length` bodies only, small hard limits. |
| `pairing.rs` | Pairing browsers with Forge. |
| `project.rs` | What the Browser Companion settings page needs to know about the open project to show the relevant framework snippets first, and the one config change it may apply itself: setting a variable in a dotenv file. |
| `request.rs` | Open requests as they arrive from the browser extension, `forge://` links and the CLI, plus their validation. |
| `resolve.rs` | Map a requested file to a project: the open one, a recent one that has to be opened first, or none (the user has to confirm opening it). |
| `server.rs` | The Browser Companion's local HTTP API, modelled on JetBrains' built-in server. |
| `symbols.rs` | Find the declaration of a symbol the browser only knows by name (an Angular component's constructor name, a React component without debug source) in the open project. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use request::{LinkAction, OpenRequest, RequestError, SymbolKind, SymbolRequest};
pub use resolve::{resolve_file, KnownProject, ProjectContext, ResolveError, Target};
pub enum OpenSource { … }
pub struct OpenEvent { … }
pub fn open_event(
```

## Used by

- IPC: `companion_status`, `companion_start_pairing`, `companion_cancel_pairing`, `companion_revoke_client`, `companion_ui_ready`, `companion_open_link`, `companion_project_profile`, `companion_set_env_var` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/companion.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/browserCompanion`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

# forge-output

`crates/forge-output` — Forge process output: ANSI styling, console lines, file links and TeamCity test trees (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Process output for the Run tool window and the terminal, computed in Rust so the UI only
renders it.

- `ansi`: ANSI escape sequences (SGR colors and styles) into styled segments.
- `console`: segments into console lines with `\r` progress lines, as deltas the UI
  applies to its line list.
- `links`: clickable file references (`app/User.php:42`, stack traces) and URLs.
- `teamcity`: TeamCity service messages (`phpunit --teamcity`, Pest, Jest) into a test
  tree that is sent to the UI as node updates.
- `run`: everything above combined for one run.

The crate is pure (no I/O) so `forge-wasm` can run it in browser mode.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `ansi.rs` | ANSI escape handling: SGR colors and styles become styled segments, other control sequences (cursor movement, OSC titles) are dropped. Colors are CSS values, either a theme variable (`var(--ansi-red)`) or `rgb(…)`. |
| `console.rs` | Console lines built from styled segments, sent to the UI as deltas. |
| `links.rs` | File references in console and terminal output (`app/User.php:42`, `/abs/path/File.php on line 7`, `File.php(12)`, `#0 /path/x.php(31): …`) and web links, so the UI can make them clickable. |
| `run.rs` | The output of one run: console lines for every stream, and for test runners the test tree built from TeamCity service messages on stdout (those lines are not shown in the console). Output while a test runs is attributed to that test. |
| `teamcity.rs` | TeamCity service messages (`phpunit --teamcity`, Pest, Jest reporters) turned into the test tree of the Run tool window. The tree lives here; the UI receives changed nodes. |
| `utf16.rs` | Offsets for the UI: JavaScript strings and CodeMirror count UTF-16 code units, Rust counts bytes. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use ansi::{AnsiParser, Segment, Style};
pub use console::{ConsoleDelta, ConsoleLine, ConsoleModel, Span};
pub use links::{…};
pub use run::{OutputEvent, RunInput, RunOutput, RunOutputOptions};
pub use teamcity::{…};
pub use utf16::{byte_to_utf16, utf16_to_byte};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `output_file_links`, and the `console`/`tests` events of `run://<runId>`
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/run`, `app/ui/src/features/terminal`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `regex-lite`, `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

7 source files, about 2133 lines; 19 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-output
```

# forge-plugin-api

`crates/forge-plugin-api` — Stable plugin API for Forge language packs and feature plugins.

## Purpose

The contract between Forge and its plugins.

A plugin (a language pack like PHPForge, or a feature like Git) describes itself with a
`PluginManifest` and contributes capabilities through `Contributions`: commands,
keybindings, tool windows, typed settings, language servers, run configuration types and
AI providers/agents/generators. The `PluginRegistry` tracks installed plugins, their
enablement, and answers lookups over the contributions of enabled plugins. Packs depend
only on this crate, never on app internals.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `contributions.rs` | Contribution types: everything a plugin can add to the IDE. |
| `registry.rs` | The plugin registry: which plugins are installed, which are enabled, and lookups over the contributions of the enabled ones. |
| `settings_model.rs` | The model behind the Settings dialog (Ctrl+Alt+S): the page tree built from registered pages, search over pages, settings and plugins, and highlighting of search hits. The UI sends what it shows and renders the answer; this module decides what matches. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use registry::{PluginDescriptor, PluginInfo, PluginRegistry};
pub struct PluginManifest { … }
pub trait Plugin: Send + Sync { … }
```

# forge-process

`crates/forge-process` — Forge IDE processes: PTY terminal sessions, run configurations and the process runner.

## Purpose

Forge processes: everything the IDE starts on behalf of the user.

- `pty`: interactive terminal sessions on a pseudo terminal (Terminal tool window).
- `runner`: plain processes with piped output for run configurations (Run tool window),
  with exit codes and process-tree kill.
- `config`: Run/Debug configurations, their persistence in
  `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.toml` and the registry of configuration kinds that
  turns a configuration into a command line.
- `output`: the pure output models of the `forge-output` crate (ANSI, console lines,
  file links, TeamCity test trees), re-exported for the run backend.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `args.rs` | Splitting and quoting of argument strings as typed into run configuration fields ("Arguments", "Interpreter options", "Test runner options"). |
| `config.rs` | Run/Debug configurations. |
| `pty.rs` | Interactive shell sessions on a pseudo terminal, used by the Terminal tool window. |
| `runner.rs` | Non-interactive processes for run configurations: piped stdout/stderr streamed as text, stdin for input typed into the Run console, the exit code, and kill of the whole process tree (so `composer run` or `npm run` children stop too). |
| `shell.rs` | Picking the user's default shell. |
| `utf8.rs` |  |

## Main public items


title: forge-remote
