order: 210
tags: [crate, rust]
---

# forge-remote

`crates/forge-remote` — Forge IDE remote development: SSH connections, host keys, ~/.ssh/config and the Forge agent deployment.

## Purpose

Remote development over SSH, like JetBrains Gateway: Forge connects to a host, installs
its headless agent (`crates/forge-remote-agent`) there and opens the project through a
`forge_backend::RemoteBackend`, so indexing, Intelephense, git, terminals and runs all
happen next to the files.

Pure modules (also built for WebAssembly without the `client` feature):
- `ssh_config`: `~/.ssh/config` host blocks.
- `known_hosts`: host key verification and fingerprints.
- `deploy`: probing a host and planning the agent upload.
- `config`: saved SSH configurations.

With `client` (the default):
- `session`: SSH connections with russh (password, key file, ssh-agent; known_hosts
  check with a fingerprint confirmation).
- `agent`: installing and starting the agent.
- `connection`: a live connection to an agent with reconnects and latency.
- `store`: saved configurations on disk and their secrets in the keychain.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.rs` | Installing and starting the Forge agent over an SSH session. |
| `config.rs` | Saved SSH configurations (Settings \| Tools \| SSH Configurations), stored in `<config dir>/forge/ssh.toml`. Passwords and key passphrases never go there: they live in the OS keychain. |
| `connection.rs` | A live connection to the Forge agent on a host: connects (SSH + agent start), measures latency, notices a dead connection and reconnects with backoff. |
| `deploy.rs` | Installing the Forge agent on a remote host: probe the host with one shell command, decide whether the agent must be uploaded, upload it through `cat` (no SFTP needed) and start it. |
| `known_hosts.rs` | OpenSSH `known_hosts`: which host keys are trusted. |
| `session.rs` | SSH sessions with russh: host key verification against `known_hosts` (unknown and changed keys need the user's confirmation of the fingerprint), password, key file and ssh-agent authentication, command execution and streams, jump hosts (`ProxyJump`, one session tunnelled through the previous one) and `ProxyCommand`, port forwarding (`direct-tcpip` channels and remote `tcpip-forward` listeners) and forwarded Unix sockets (the Docker API over SSH). |
| `ssh_config.rs` | OpenSSH client configuration (`~/.ssh/config`): host blocks with patterns and the keywords Forge uses to connect. Like `ssh`, the first value obtained for a keyword wins and `IdentityFile` accumulates. |
| `store.rs` | Saved SSH configurations on disk (`<config dir>/forge/ssh.toml`), their passwords and passphrases in the OS keychain (service `forge-ssh`, account = configuration id), and the user's OpenSSH files (`~/.ssh/config`, `~/.ssh/known_hosts`). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use config::{AuthMethod, SshConfiguration, SshConfigurations};
pub use known_hosts::HostKeyStatus;
```

## Used by

- IPC: `remote_ssh_configs`, `remote_ssh_config_save`, `remote_validate_config`, `remote_ssh_config_delete`, `remote_ssh_hosts`, `remote_test_connection`, `remote_connect`, `remote_browse`, `remote_open_project`, `remote_disconnect`, `remote_status`, `remote_reconnect` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/remote.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/remote`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-backend`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-backend.md), [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md)
- External: `base64`, `dirs`, `flate2`, `hmac`, `keyring`, `russh`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha1`, `sha2`, `tokio`, `toml`, `tracing`
- Features: `default` = `client`; `client` = `dep:forge-backend`, `dep:forge-core`, `dep:russh`, `dep:tokio`, `dep:tracing`, `dep:dirs`, `dep:keyring`, `dep:toml`, `dep:flate2`

## Tests

9 source files, about 3257 lines; 32 unit tests and 5 integration tests in `tests/` (`ssh.rs`).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-remote
```

# forge-remote-agent

`crates/forge-remote-agent` — Headless Forge agent: serves a project's files, git, processes, language servers and PHP index over stdio for remote development.

## Purpose

The Forge agent: a headless `LocalBackend` behind the agent
`protocol`, run on a remote host over SSH (stdin/stdout).

The desktop app uploads this binary to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/`, starts
`forge-remote-agent serve` and talks to it with `forge_backend::rpc::RpcClient`. Every
service runs next to the project's files: file system, file search, git, terminals,
processes, language servers (Intelephense indexes the remote project itself) and the
PHP index.

# forge-scratches

`crates/forge-scratches` — Forge scratch files (PHPStorm's Scratches and Consoles): storage, naming, languages, run commands and the HTTP request client.

## Purpose

Scratch files, PHPStorm's "Scratches and Consoles".

Scratches are global: they live in the user config dir (`<config>/forge/scratches/`), not
in a project, and are listed at the bottom of the Project tool window.

- `languages`: the language list of the "New Scratch File" popup (file types from
  `forge-filetypes`, ranked with `forge-fuzzy`) and the language → extension mapping.
- `naming`: auto-numbered names (`scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, `buffer1.txt`) and name
  validation.
- `store`: create, list, read, write, rename and delete scratches on disk, plus the data
  source attached to SQL scratches.
- `run`: what runs a scratch (PHP with the project's autoloader, Node, ...) and the
  gutter run markers.
- `http`: the `.http` request parser and the console rendering of responses (PHPStorm's
  HTTP Client, lite); `handler` runs response handler scripts (`> {% … %}`) as a safe
  subset without a JavaScript engine; `client` sends the requests (feature `client`).

Everything except `store` and `client` is pure, so browser mode runs it as WebAssembly.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `client.rs` | Sends the requests of `.http` scratches (feature `client`). |
| `handler.rs` | Response handler scripts of `.http` requests (`> {% … %}`), PHPStorm's HTTP Client API as a small, safe subset: no JavaScript engine, no loops, no access to anything but the response and the global variables. |
| `http.rs` | `.http` request files (PHPStorm's HTTP Client, lite): parsing, `{{variable}}` substitution and the console text of a response. |
| `languages.rs` | Languages of the "New Scratch File" popup (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert): every file type of `forge-filetypes` with an extension, the extension a new scratch gets, and the popup's ordering and speed search. |
| `naming.rs` | Scratch names: PHPStorm numbers new scratches `scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, `scratch_2.php`, … and scratch buffers `buffer1.txt` … `buffer5.txt` (the oldest buffer is reused once all five exist). |
| `run.rs` | Running scratches: which program runs a scratch (PHP with the project's Composer autoloader, Node for JavaScript/TypeScript, …), and the gutter ▶ markers of runnable scratches and of the requests in `.http` files. |
| `store.rs` | Scratch files on disk. PHPStorm keeps scratches per user, not per project; Forge stores them in `<config dir>/forge/scratches/` and per-scratch settings (the data source of a SQL scratch) in `<config dir>/forge/scratches.json`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use languages::{LanguageItem, LanguageRequest, ScratchLanguage};
pub use run::{Marker, MarkerKind, RunCommand, RunContext, Runner};
pub use store::{ScratchFile, ScratchStore};
pub enum Error { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `scratches_list`, `scratches_languages`, `scratches_create`, `scratches_create_buffer`, `scratches_read`, `scratches_write`, `scratches_rename`, `scratches_delete`, `scratches_set_data_source`, `scratches_markers`, `scratches_http_environments`, `scratches_http_run` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/scratches.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/scratches`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-filetypes`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-filetypes.md), [`forge-fuzzy`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-fuzzy.md)
- External: `reqwest`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`
- Features: `default` = `client`; `client` = `dep:reqwest`

## Tests

8 source files, about 3746 lines; 34 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-scratches
```

# forge-sql

`crates/forge-sql` — Forge SQL text: dialects, statement splitting, literals, row changes and export (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Pure SQL text handling shared by `forge-db` and the browser-mode UI (WebAssembly):
dialect quoting, statement splitting and the statement at the caret, cell values as
JavaScript-safe JSON, row change statements and export.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `dialect.rs` | SQL dialects: quoting of identifiers and literals. |
| `edit.rs` | Row editing from the data grid: pending inserts, updates and deletes become `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` statements that identify rows by their primary key. |
| `export.rs` | Export a result set as CSV, JSON or SQL `INSERT` statements. |
| `split.rs` | Split a script into statements at `;`, respecting quotes, comments and PostgreSQL dollar quoting. |
| `value.rs` | Cell values as JSON that survives JavaScript: `null`, booleans, numbers only within ±2^53, everything else (big integers, decimals, dates) as strings, binary data as `{"$hex": "89504e47"}`. |

## Main public items

tags: [crate, rust, updates]
---

# forge-update

`crates/forge-update` — Forge update checks: when to check, which release is an update, the update feed, simulated updates and download speed.

## Purpose

The Tauri shell downloads, verifies (minisign signature) and installs updates with
`tauri-plugin-updater`. Everything that decides *whether* and *what* to offer lives here,
without a window or an app handle, so it is unit tested.

- `policy`: the update channel, the remembered state (last check, skipped and postponed
  versions), when a check is due (`plan`) and which release counts as an update (`evaluate`).
- `feed`: the `latest.json` feed that `pnpm tauri build` produces (`createUpdaterArtifacts`),
  fetching it, the download size and the `UpdateOffer` the splash screen shows.
- `simulate`: a fake offer and download for `FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE` (desktop dev builds) and
  `?simulateUpdate` (browser mode). Nothing is installed.
- `meter`: the download speed shown while an update downloads.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `policy.rs` | `Channel`, `UpdateState`, `plan` (once a day, dev builds, missing key, simulation) and `evaluate` (newer, channel, skipped, postponed). |
| `feed.rs` | `Feed` (`latest.json`), `check`, `fetch_feed`, `download_size`, `client`, `UpdateOffer` and its one-line summary. |
| `simulate.rs` | Simulated offer and chunk sizes of the fake download. |
| `meter.rs` | `SpeedMeter`: bytes per second over a two-second window. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use feed::{check, client, fetch_feed, CheckOutcome, CheckRequest, Feed, FeedPlatform, UpdateOffer};
pub use meter::SpeedMeter;
pub use policy::{evaluate, plan, Channel, CheckPlan, PlanInput, Postponed, SkipReason, UpdateState, Verdict};
pub const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT: &str; // https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json
pub const CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS: u64; // one day

```

# forge-vcs

`crates/forge-vcs` — Forge IDE version control: drives the git CLI and parses its output.

## Purpose

Forge version control. Drives the `git` command line (no libgit2, no shell) and parses
its machine-readable output into serializable types for the UI.

Paths in and out are relative to the *workspace* root, which may be a subdirectory of the
repository; `Repo` converts them to and from repository paths.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `blame.rs` | Parser for `git blame --porcelain`. |
| `branch.rs` | Branches and tags from `git for-each-ref`, plus recently checked out branches from the reflog. |
| `cmd.rs` | Running the `git` executable. No shell is involved: arguments are passed as-is, so paths with spaces or quotes need no escaping on any platform. |
| `diff.rs` | Parser for unified diffs as printed by `git diff`. |
| `log.rs` | Commit history: parser for a NUL/RS separated `git log` format, ref decorations and per-commit changed files. |
| `status.rs` | Parser for `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --branch`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use blame::{parse_blame, Blame, BlameCommit};
pub use branch::{parse_recent_checkouts, parse_refs, BranchInfo, Branches};
pub use diff::{parse_diff, DiffLine, FileDiff, Hunk, LineKind};
pub use log::{…};
pub use status::{parse_status, FileState, RepoStatus, StatusEntry};
pub use cmd::{GitExec, GitOutput, GitRequest, LocalGit};
pub struct RepoInfo { … }
pub struct RemoteResult { … }
pub struct Repo { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `git_info`, `git_status`, `git_show`, `git_diff`, `git_diff_head`, `git_blame`, `git_log`, `git_commit_details`, `git_branches`, `git_checkout`, `git_create_branch`, `git_delete_branch`, `git_merge`, `git_rebase`, `git_stage`, `git_unstage`, `git_rollback`, `git_commit`, `git_push`, `git_pull`, `git_fetch` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/git.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/git`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md)
- External: `serde`, `tracing`

## Tests

7 source files, about 1737 lines; 10 unit tests and 11 integration tests in `tests/` (`repo.rs`).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-vcs
```

order: 260

# forge-wasm

`crates/forge-wasm` — WebAssembly build of Forge's pure Rust logic for the browser-mode UI.

## Purpose

WebAssembly bridge for the browser-mode UI.

Forge's rule is "Rust computes, TypeScript renders". In the desktop app the UI calls Rust
through Tauri IPC; in browser mode (`pnpm dev`, screenshots, tests) the same Rust code runs
as WebAssembly so mocks never re-implement logic in TypeScript.

Only **pure** crates belong here (no file system, processes, network or tokio). Each area
adds a module that wraps its crate with `#[wasm_bindgen]` functions taking and returning
JSON strings, mirroring the matching IPC command:

```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn keymap_resolve(request_json: &str) -> String { … }
```

Rebuild the bundle with `pnpm --dir app/ui wasm` (output: `app/ui/src/wasm/pkg`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `agents.rs` | Agent CLIs (`forge_agent_cli`) for the browser-mode agent mock: the built-in agents' profiles (what `agent_list` reports besides detection) and the stream parsers, so the mock replays recorded CLI output through the same Rust code as the desktop app. |
| `containers.rs` | Services tool window (`forge-containers`) for the browser-mode mock: the mock keeps a fake Docker daemon as Engine API JSON, compose files and a kubeconfig as text, and asks Rust for the models, the tree, the details pane, the gutter markers, command lines and pull progress, like the desktop app's hub. |
| `filetypes.rs` | File type detection (`forge-filetypes`), mirroring the `filetypes_detect` IPC command. The desktop app builds the registry from its plugin manifests; browser mode loads the same manifests (the `builtinPlugins.json` snapshot) once with `filetypes_load`. |
| `keymap.rs` | Keymap bridge (`forge-keymap`). |
| `lua.rs` | LuaForge (`luaforge-lang-lua`), mirroring the `lua_*` IPC commands for the browser-mode mock: the mock hands over the demo project's Lua files once (`lua_index_files`), then asks for structure, hover, Go to Declaration, symbol search and run markers. |
| `parsers.rs` | Parsers and models of process output, SQL, DQL, Markdown and the AI chat, mirroring the IPC commands of the desktop app for the browser-mode mocks. |
| `parsers/chat.rs` | The AI chat conversation (`forge_agent_cli::conversation`) for the browser-mode agent: the mock feeds its scripted events into a `Chat` and emits the `chat` updates like the desktop backend. |
| `parsers/dql.rs` | DQL in PHP strings (`phpforge-dql`) for the browser-mode Doctrine backend. Sites are found by the lexical finder (the desktop app uses tree-sitter); the entity snapshot comes from the mock's demo mappings. |
| `parsers/markdown.rs` | Markdown (`forge-markdown`) for browser mode, mirroring `markdown_parse` / `markdown_hover`. |
| `parsers/output.rs` | Run output (`forge-output`) for the browser-mode run backend and terminal: the mock feeds process events into a `RunOutput` and emits the rendered events like the desktop app. |
| `parsers/sql.rs` | SQL text (`forge-sql`) for the browser-mode database backend and console. |
| `remote.rs` | Remote development (`forge-remote` without its SSH client): `~/.ssh/config` hosts, SSH configuration validation and `known_hosts` checks, mirroring `remote_ssh_hosts`, `remote_validate_config` and the host key step of `remote_connect`. |
| `scratches.rs` | Scratch files (`forge-scratches`), mirroring the pure parts of the `scratches_*` IPC commands for the browser-mode mock: the language list, naming, gutter markers, run command lines and the `.http` parser, request resolution (variables, dynamic variables, body files), response handlers and rendering. |
| `search.rs` | Fuzzy matching and Search Everywhere ranking (`forge-fuzzy`), mirroring the `fuzzy_filter`, `search_rank` and `fs_find_files` IPC commands. |
| `settings.rs` | The Settings dialog model (`forge_plugin_api::settings_model`), mirroring the `settings_search` and `settings_validate` IPC commands. |
| `web.rs` | WebForge (`packs/webforge/*`) for the browser-mode mock: npm packages and scripts, package manager detection, and React/Vue/Angular component navigation over the demo project's files, mirroring the `npm_*` and `web_*` IPC commands. |
| `window.rs` | Window chrome (`forge_window`), mirroring the `window_chrome` IPC command for browser mode. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn bridge_version() -> String { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: none: it mirrors IPC commands as WebAssembly functions for browser mode
- UI: `app/ui/src/wasm/`, `app/ui/src/mock/`
- Browser mode: is the WebAssembly bridge

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-agent-cli`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-agent-cli.md), [`forge-containers`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-containers.md), [`forge-filetypes`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-filetypes.md), [`forge-find`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-find.md), [`forge-fuzzy`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-fuzzy.md), [`forge-keymap`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-keymap.md), [`forge-markdown`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-markdown.md), [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-plugin-api`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-plugin-api.md), [`forge-remote`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-remote.md), [`forge-scratches`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-scratches.md), [`forge-sql`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-sql.md), [`forge-window`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-window.md), [`luaforge-lang-lua`](docs/guide/developer/crates/luaforge-lang-lua.md), [`phpforge-dql`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-dql.md), [`webforge-fw-angular`](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-fw-angular.md), [`webforge-fw-react`](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-fw-react.md), [`webforge-fw-vue`](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-fw-vue.md), [`webforge-lang-web`](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-lang-web.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `wasm-bindgen`

## Tests

18 source files, about 2393 lines; 23 unit tests.


# forge-window

`crates/forge-window` — Forge window chrome: desktop detection, title bar button layouts and dialog window geometry (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Window chrome for Forge's own (undecorated) windows.

- `desktop`: which OS and desktop environment Forge runs on, read from the target OS and
  environment variables (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, …).
- `chrome`: the title bar style and button layout for the setting
  `appearance.windowControls` (`auto | windows | macos | gnome | kde | linux | native`),
  including GNOME's `button-layout` and KDE's `kwinrc` button order.
- `geometry`: where a dialog window opens (centered on its parent, or where the user left
  it) and the remembered size and position of every dialog.

The crate is pure (no file system, processes or windowing): the Tauri shell reads the
environment and files and passes them in, and the browser-mode UI runs the same code as
WebAssembly.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `chrome.rs` | Title bar style and button layout for `appearance.windowControls`. |
| `desktop.rs` | Operating system and desktop environment detection. |
| `geometry.rs` | Where dialog windows open and the geometry Forge remembers for each dialog. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use chrome::{…};
pub use desktop::{detect_desktop, Desktop, Os};
pub use geometry::{place_dialog, DialogStates, Rect, Size};
pub fn dialog_label(id: &str) -> Option<String> { … }
pub fn dialog_id(label: &str) -> Option<&str> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `window_chrome`, `dialog_window_open`, `dialog_window_close`, `dialog_window_message` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/window.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/shell/window`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

4 source files, about 1046 lines; 24 unit tests.

title: luaforge-lang-lua
description: "LuaForge: Lua language support (lexer, structural parser, EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, project index, require resolution, hover, navigation; pure, also built to WebAssembly)."

---

# luaforge-lang-lua

`packs/luaforge/lang-lua` — LuaForge: Lua language support (lexer, structural parser, EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, project index, require resolution, hover, navigation; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

LuaForge language pack: Lua 5.1–5.4 and LuaJIT support. Pure Rust (no file system or
processes), so the same code backs the desktop app and the browser mode (WebAssembly).

- `lexer` and `parser` index a file into a `model::FileIndex`: locals with their
  scopes, globals, table fields, functions and methods (`M.f`, `M:f`), references,
  `require` calls and the module's `return`.
- `annotations` parses EmmyLua / LuaLS doc comments (`---@class`, `---@field`,
  `---@param`, `---@return`, `---@type`, `---@alias`, …).
- `require` resolves module names through `package.path`-like templates.
- `project::ProjectIndex` holds a workspace's files and resolves values across them
  (Go to Declaration, Search Everywhere).
- `hover` renders documentation as the `forge-markdown` AST, `structure` builds the
  Structure tool window and `run` finds main chunks for gutter run icons.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `annotations.rs` | EmmyLua / LuaLS annotations (`---@class`, `---@field`, `---@param`, `---@return`, `---@type`, `---@alias`, `---@deprecated`, `---@see`) and the Markdown description of a doc comment block. |
| `hover.rs` | Hover documentation from the index and EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, as the Markdown AST of `forge-markdown` (the same `HoverDoc` the UI renders for language server hovers). |
| `lexer.rs` | Lua 5.1–5.4 / LuaJIT lexer. Error tolerant: unterminated strings and comments end at the end of the line or file, unknown characters become one-character operators. |
| `model.rs` | What the parser extracts from one Lua file. |
| `offsets.rs` | Offset conversion. The parser works in UTF-8 byte offsets; the UI (CodeMirror / JS strings) uses UTF-16 code units. Convert at the IPC boundary. |
| `parser.rs` | Structural Lua parser: a tolerant recursive-descent pass over the tokens that records declarations (locals, parameters, globals, fields, functions and methods) with their scopes, name and field references, `require` calls, the module's `return` value and the doc comments attached to each statement. |
| `project.rs` | The project index: every Lua file of a workspace, with lightweight type resolution across files (locals, globals, table fields, `require`d modules, `---@class` / `---@type` / `---@param` / `---@return` annotations), Go to Declaration and symbol search for Search Everywhere. |
| `require.rs` | `require("a.b")` resolution through `package.path`-like templates relative to the project root (`?.lua`, `?/init.lua`, `lua/?.lua`, …), extended by the `lua.requirePaths` setting and the `runtime.path` of a `.luarc.json`. |
| `run.rs` | Gutter run icons (▶) for main chunks: scripts that do not return a module table, and the `main.lua` of a LÖVE game. |
| `structure.rs` | The Structure tool window (Alt+7) of a Lua file: classes with their fields and methods, module tables with their functions, top-level functions and variables. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use project::{IndexStats, Location, ProjectIndex, SearchKind, SymbolHit, SymbolKind};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `lua_index_workspace`, `lua_files_changed`, `lua_search_symbols`, `lua_file_structure`, `lua_hover`, `lua_goto`, `lua_run_markers`, `lua_format` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/lua.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/lua`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-fuzzy`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-fuzzy.md), [`forge-markdown`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-markdown.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

11 source files, about 4516 lines; 34 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p luaforge-lang-lua
```

# phpforge-dql

`packs/phpforge/dql` — PHPForge: Doctrine DQL tokenizer, parser, highlighting, completion and diagnostics, and DQL sites in PHP source (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Doctrine DQL for PHPForge, without I/O so it also runs as WebAssembly in browser mode.

- `model`: entity mapping metadata (filled by `phpforge-orm-doctrine`).
- `dql`: tokenizer, parser, semantic highlighting, completion and diagnostics.
- `site`: DQL inside PHP strings (`createQuery()`, QueryBuilder calls) and the
  source-level functions over a `site::SiteFinder`; `lexical` is a finder without a
  PHP parser, `editor` the same functions with UTF-16 offsets.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `dql/lexer.rs` | DQL tokenizer. Path expressions (`o.customer.email`) are single identifier tokens; `super::highlight` splits them into alias and field parts. |
| `dql/mod.rs` | DQL: parsing (identification variables and their entities), semantic highlighting, completion and diagnostics against the project's entity mappings. |
| `editor.rs` | The site functions with editor offsets (UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript strings and CodeMirror count), as the IPC commands and the browser mock expose them. |
| `lexical.rs` | A `SiteFinder` without a PHP parser, for browser mode (WebAssembly cannot run the tree-sitter grammar): string literals are found lexically, the call around them by walking back to its `(`, and QueryBuilder aliases are read from the whole file. |
| `model.rs` | Entity mapping metadata as the DQL functions need it. `phpforge-orm-doctrine` fills it from PHP attributes, annotations, XML and YAML; browser mode passes it in as JSON. |
| `site.rs` | DQL inside PHP code: a `Site` is one DQL text assembled from the string literals of a call argument (`createQuery('…')`, QueryBuilder fragments like `->andWhere('o.status = :s')`) with a mapping back to source offsets. |

## Used by

- IPC: `doctrine_complete`, `doctrine_goto`, `doctrine_diagnostics`, `doctrine_highlight` (through phpforge-orm-doctrine)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/doctrine/editor.ts`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `regex-lite`, `serde`, `serde_json`

# phpforge-fw-laravel

`packs/phpforge/fw-laravel` — PHPForge: Laravel support (routes, views, Blade components, config/env, Eloquent, translations, artisan).

## Purpose

PHPForge Laravel support, built on the PHP pack's tree-sitter parser.

`Laravel::load` analyses a project statically:
- `routes`: `routes/*.php` (groups, prefixes, names, middleware, resources) or the
  output of `php artisan route:list --json`;
- `views`: view names, Blade components (anonymous, class based, Livewire) and custom
  Blade directives;
- `config`: `config()` and `env()` keys;
- `eloquent`: models with columns from migrations, `$fillable`, casts, relations,
  scopes and accessors;
- `translations`: `__()` keys from PHP and JSON language files.

On top of that, `complete` offers completion, Go to Declaration and gutter markers
for an editor buffer, and `artisan` lists and builds artisan commands.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `artisan.rs` | Artisan commands: the list from `php artisan list --format=json` (with a built-in fallback when PHP is not available), command line splitting, and running commands with streamed output. |
| `complete.rs` | Editor services for PHP and Blade buffers: completion of route names, views, config and env keys, translations, columns, relations, model properties, scopes, components and custom directives; Go to Declaration for the same; gutter markers for routed controller methods, route definitions and `view()` calls. |
| `config.rs` | `config('app.name')` keys from `config/*.php` and `env('APP_NAME')` keys from `.env` files. |
| `context.rs` | What the caret is on, found lexically so it works while the code is being typed (`route('orders.\|` has no closing quote yet): a string argument of a call, a property access, a Blade component tag or a Blade directive. |
| `eloquent.rs` | Eloquent models: table columns from migrations, `$fillable`, casts, relations (with the related model), local scopes, accessors and `@property` docblocks. |
| `php.rs` | Small helpers over the tree-sitter PHP syntax tree: literal values, call arguments and returned arrays. Laravel's configuration lives in plain PHP arrays and fluent calls, so static evaluation of these few shapes covers routes, config, translations and models. |
| `project.rs` | Project layout: Laravel version, PSR-4 autoloading, file helpers and locations. |
| `routes.rs` | Routes: static parsing of `routes/*.php` (verbs, `match`, `resource`, `view`, `redirect`, groups with prefix/name/middleware/controller, included route files) and the JSON output of `php artisan route:list --json`. |
| `translations.rs` | Translation keys for `__()`, `trans()`, `trans_choice()` and `@lang`: grouped PHP files (`lang/en/messages.php` → `messages.welcome`) and JSON files (`lang/de.json`). |
| `views.rs` | Views and Blade components: `view('orders.show')` names, anonymous components in `resources/views/components`, class components in `app/View/Components`, Livewire components and custom directives registered with `Blade::directive` / `Blade::if`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use complete::{CompletionItem, Completions, GutterMark};
pub use config::KeyEntry;
pub use eloquent::{Model, ModelAttribute, Relation, Scope};
pub use project::{Location, Psr4};
pub use routes::Route;
pub use translations::Translation;
pub use views::{Component, CustomDirective, View};
pub struct Laravel { … }
pub struct LaravelInfo { … }
pub use project::is_laravel;
pub fn fingerprint(root: &Path) -> u64 { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `laravel_detect`, `laravel_routes`, `laravel_complete`, `laravel_goto`, `laravel_gutter`, `laravel_artisan_commands`, `laravel_artisan_run`, `laravel_artisan_cancel` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/laravel.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/laravel`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`phpforge-lang-php`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-lang-php.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `tree-sitter`, `walkdir`

11 source files, about 4735 lines; 18 unit tests and 11 integration tests in `tests/` (`fixture.rs`).

title: phpforge-fw-symfony
description: "PHPForge: Symfony support (service container, routes, Twig templates, console commands)."
order: 310
tags: [crate, rust, pack]
---

# phpforge-fw-symfony

`packs/phpforge/fw-symfony` — PHPForge: Symfony support (service container, routes, Twig templates, console commands).

## Purpose

PHPForge Symfony plugin: everything the IDE knows about a Symfony application.

- `container` reads `config/services.yaml` (explicit services, aliases, `_defaults` and
  autowired `resource:` directories) and, when present, the compiled container XML in
  `var/cache/<env>/`, which also lists the services and parameters of all bundles.
- `routes` collects routes from `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and
  YAML route files.
- `twig` lists templates, Twig tags/filters/functions/tests (core, Symfony bridge and
  project extensions) and which controller renders which template.
- `console` finds console commands and builds `bin/console` command lines.
- `complete` answers completion and Go to Declaration for route names, service ids,
  templates, parameters and Twig syntax; `gutter` computes the editor gutter marks.

`scan` builds a `Snapshot` of a project once; the IDE caches it and rescans when files
change.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `complete.rs` | Completion and Go to Declaration for Symfony references in PHP, Twig and YAML files: route names (`generateUrl`, `redirectToRoute`, Twig `path()`/`url()`), templates (`render()`, `{% extends %}`), service ids (`@id`, `#[Autowire(service:)]`, `$container->get()`), parameters (`%name%`, `getParameter()`) and Twig tags, filters, functions and tests. |
| `console.rs` | Console commands: the application's own (`#[AsCommand]`, `$defaultName`, `setName()`) plus the common framework and bundle commands, and the `bin/console` command line. |
| `container.rs` | The service container: services and parameters from `config/services*.yaml` (including `resource:` directories registered with autowiring) and from the compiled container XML Symfony dumps to `var/cache/<env>/` in debug mode. |
| `gutter.rs` | Editor gutter marks, like the Symfony plugin's line markers: routes on controller actions, "go to template" next to `render()` calls, "rendered by" on Twig templates and a run marker on console commands. |
| `routes.rs` | Routes from `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and YAML route files (`config/routes.yaml`, `config/routes/*.yaml`), including import prefixes. |
| `strings.rs` | String literal helpers shared by completion, navigation and the gutter: find the quoted string around a cursor and the call it is an argument of (`generateUrl('\|')`). |
| `twig.rs` | Twig: templates, the tags/filters/functions/tests available in templates (Twig core, the Symfony bridge and the project's own extensions) and which controllers render which template. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use complete::{CompletionItem, CompletionKind, CompletionList};
pub use console::ConsoleCommand;
pub use container::{Parameter, Service, ServiceSource};
pub use routes::{Route, RouteSource};
pub use twig::{Template, TwigSymbol, TwigSymbolKind};
pub struct Location { … }
pub struct Config { … }
pub struct SymfonyInfo { … }
pub struct PhpFile { … }
pub struct Snapshot { … }
pub fn is_symfony_project(root: &Path) -> bool { … }
pub fn framework_version(root: &Path) -> Option<String> { … }
pub fn line_col(text: &str, offset: usize) -> (u32, u32) { … }
pub fn index_php_files(root: &Path, dir: &str) -> Vec<PhpFile> { … }
pub fn scan(root: &Path, config: &Config) -> Snapshot { … }
```

# phpforge-lang-php

`packs/phpforge/lang-php` — PHPForge: PHP language support (tree-sitter index, docblocks, hover, code generation, language server config).

## Purpose

PHPForge language pack: PHP support built on tree-sitter.

- `parser` indexes a file into a `model::FileIndex` (namespaces, imports, classes,
  members, functions, docblocks and attributes).
- `docblock` parses PHPDoc including Doctrine/Symfony annotations.
- `index::ProjectIndex` indexes a workspace in parallel with an mtime-keyed cache,
  fuzzy symbol search, file structure and lazy vendor resolution.
- `hover` renders index-based hover markdown.
- `generate` implements the "Generate" actions (constructor, accessors, overrides, ...).
- `lsp` describes how to launch Intelephense / phpactor.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `docblock.rs` | PHPDoc parser: summary/description, the standard tags (`@param`, `@return`, `@throws`, `@var`, `@property[-read\|-write]`, `@method`, `@deprecated`, `@see`, `@template`, `@extends`/`@implements`), static-analysis prefixes (`@phpstan-`/`@psalm-`) and Doctrine/Symfony style annotations (`@ORM\Column(type="string")`, `@Route("/x")`). |
| `fuzzy.rs` | Fuzzy matcher for Go to Class / Go to Symbol: subsequence matching with bonuses for word starts, camel humps (`OrCo` -> `OrderController`) and consecutive runs. |
| `generate.rs` | "Generate" actions (Alt+Insert): constructor, getters/setters, `__toString()`, override/implement method stubs and PHPDoc blocks. |
| `hover.rs` | Index-based hover for project symbols: signature + attributes + parsed docblock as markdown. Complements a language server's hover (which covers built-ins). |
| `index.rs` | Workspace-wide PHP index: parallel indexing, mtime-keyed persistent cache, fuzzy symbol search, ancestor lookup and lazy resolution of vendor classes through Composer's PSR-4 metadata. |
| `lsp.rs` | How to launch a PHP language server: Intelephense (preferred, users bring their own licence key) with phpactor as fallback. Independent of the generic LSP client; the app turns `LspServerConfig` into a running server. |
| `model.rs` | Symbol model produced by the indexer. Everything is serializable so it can be cached on disk and sent over IPC unchanged (camelCase field names for the UI). |
| `offsets.rs` | Offset conversion. The index works in UTF-8 byte offsets; the UI (CodeMirror / JS strings) uses UTF-16 code units. Convert at the IPC boundary. |
| `parser.rs` | Tree-sitter based PHP file indexer: turns source into a `FileIndex`. |
| `resolve.rs` | Name resolution through namespaces and use-imports (PHP's rules, simplified to what an index needs: classes and type hints). |
| `service.rs` | Editor-facing PHP queries on a `ProjectIndex`: the same answers wherever the index lives (in the desktop app or in the remote development agent). Offsets crossing this boundary are UTF-16 (JS strings); the index works in bytes, so every query converts. |
| `structure.rs` | File structure for the Structure tool window (Alt+7). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use index::{IndexConfig, IndexStats, ProjectIndex};
pub use model::*;
pub enum PhpError { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `php_index_workspace`, `php_search_symbols`, `php_file_structure`, `php_hover`, `php_generate_targets`, `php_generate`, `php_detect_servers`, `php_lsp_config` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/php.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/php`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `dirs`, `rayon`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-php`, `walkdir`

## Tests

13 source files, about 6686 lines; 64 unit tests.

```sh

```

# phpforge-orm-doctrine

`packs/phpforge/orm-doctrine` — PHPForge: Doctrine ORM support (entity mapping, repositories, DQL parsing and completion).

## Purpose

PHPForge Doctrine plugin: ORM mapping metadata and DQL support.

- `mapping` reads entity mappings from PHP 8 attributes (`#[ORM\Column]`), legacy
  docblock annotations (`@ORM\Column`, parsed by the lang-php docblock parser), XML
  (`*.orm.xml`) and YAML (`*.orm.yml`) mapping files, and finds entity repositories.
- `dql` (from the pure `phpforge-dql` crate) tokenizes and parses DQL for highlighting, completion (entities, aliases,
  fields, associations, keywords and functions) and diagnostics.
- `php` finds DQL inside PHP: `createQuery('…')` (including concatenated strings and
  `Entity::class`) and QueryBuilder calls (`->where('o.status = :s')`), with the aliases
  the builder chain declares.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `mapping.rs` | Entity mapping metadata from attributes, annotations, XML and YAML. |
| `php.rs` | DQL inside PHP code: `createQuery()` arguments and QueryBuilder fragments. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use phpforge_dql::dql;
pub use phpforge_dql::model::{…};
pub struct Config { … }
pub fn is_doctrine_project(root: &Path) -> bool { … }
pub fn scan(root: &Path, config: &Config) -> Snapshot { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `doctrine_entities`, `doctrine_complete`, `doctrine_goto`, `doctrine_diagnostics`, `doctrine_highlight`, `doctrine_gutter` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/doctrine.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/doctrine`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`phpforge-dql`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-dql.md), [`phpforge-lang-php`](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-lang-php.md)

---

# webforge-lang-web

`packs/webforge/lang-web` — WebForge: package.json, npm scripts, package managers and the shared JavaScript/TypeScript/HTML scanning used by the framework plugins.

## Purpose

WebForge core (`forge.web`): `package.json` and npm scripts, package manager detection,
and the lexical scanning of JavaScript/TypeScript modules and HTML/JSX tags that the
React, Vue and Angular plugins (`webforge-fw-*`) build their component indexes on.

Everything except `fs` is pure, so the browser-mode UI runs the same code as
WebAssembly (`crates/forge-wasm/src/web.rs`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `component.rs` | The component model shared by the React, Vue and Angular plugins, and the gutter marks and navigation answers they return to the UI. |
| `fs.rs` | Loading `Sources` from disk (desktop app only; the browser mock passes its demo files). |
| `imports.rs` | ES module imports and re-exports, read lexically from JavaScript/TypeScript source. |
| `js.rs` | Lexical helpers for JavaScript/TypeScript: matching brackets, top-level members of object literals, type literals and destructuring patterns, string literals. |
| `json.rs` | A small JSON reader that keeps byte offsets, so `package.json` scripts can get gutter icons on their lines. Accepts what `tsconfig.json` allows too: comments and trailing commas. |
| `markup.rs` | Tags and attributes in HTML templates (Vue `<template>`, Angular templates) and JSX. A lexical scanner, not a full parser: it finds `<Name attr=… {expr}>` and keeps byte ranges, which is what navigation needs. |
| `npm.rs` | The npm tool window and `package.json` gutter: every `package.json` of the project with its scripts and package manager. |
| `package_json.rs` | `package.json`: name, scripts with their positions, dependencies, workspaces and the `packageManager` field. |
| `pm.rs` | Package manager detection, like WebStorm's "Package manager: auto": the `packageManager` field (Corepack), else the lock file next to the `package.json` or in a parent directory (workspaces), else npm. |
| `source.rs` | The project files the framework indexes read, and module resolution between them (relative specifiers, `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` path aliases, index files and workspace packages imported by their package name). |
| `text.rs` | Offsets and positions. Scanners work in UTF-8 byte offsets; the UI (CodeMirror, JS strings) uses UTF-16 code units and 0-based lines/columns. Convert at the boundary. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use component::{Component, ComponentKind, Framework, GutterKind, GutterMark, Member};
pub use npm::NpmPackage;
pub use package_json::{PackageJson, Script};
pub use pm::{Detection, PackageManager};
pub use source::{SourceFile, Sources};
pub use text::Location;
pub trait FrameworkIndex { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `npm_packages`, `npm_gutter` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/web.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/webforge`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `ignore`, `serde`, `serde_json`
- Features: `default` = `fs`; `fs` = `dep:ignore`

## Tests

12 source files, about 2546 lines; 29 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p webforge-lang-web
```

Source: docs/guide/faq.md

---
title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about Forge - licensing, PHPStorm compatibility, languages, AI, privacy, platforms and the project's status.
order: 900
tags: [faq]
---

# FAQ

## General

**What is Forge?**
A PHPStorm-style IDE for Windows, Linux and macOS, written in Rust (Tauri 2) with a SolidJS UI.
The layout, wording and keymap follow PHPStorm; the colors are Forge's own.

**Is it free?**
Forge is MIT-licensed. Third-party tools you connect keep their own terms: Intelephense premium
needs your own licence, AI providers need your own API key or subscription.

**Which version is this guide for?**
Forge 0.1.0 as on the branch that contains this guide. Recent additions and what is not available
yet are listed on the [start page](docs/guide/index.md#recently-added).

**Which platforms are supported?**
Windows 10/11, Linux (x86_64; WebKitGTK 4.1) and macOS. Remote development needs a Linux host
(x86_64 or aarch64).

## Compared with PHPStorm

**Can I use my PHPStorm shortcuts?**
Yes: the default keymaps are PHPStorm's (Windows/Linux and macOS). Custom PHPStorm keymaps cannot
be imported yet; re-create changes in Settings | Keymap.

**Does Forge read my `.idea` folder or `.run` configurations?**
No. Forge keeps its own data in `.forge/` and ignores `.idea/`.

**Is PHP support as deep as PHPStorm's?**
Not yet. Completion, diagnostics and navigation come from Intelephense (or Phpactor); Forge adds
its own index, Generate actions, Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine support. Refactorings, inspections
with quick-fixes, Find Usages and Replace in Files are not implemented yet. See
[Coming from PHPStorm](docs/guide/getting-started/from-phpstorm.md).

**Why does a shortcut say "not available yet"?**
The action exists in PHPStorm's keymap but not in Forge yet. Shortcuts stay reserved so they do
not do something unexpected; the [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) shows the status of every
action.

## Languages

**Which languages are supported?**
About 70 languages are highlighted. PHP, Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine, JavaScript/TypeScript, React,
Vue, Angular and Lua have dedicated packs. About 30 more languages (Python, Go, Rust, C/C++, Java,
Kotlin, C#, Ruby, Zig, YAML, TOML, XML, Markdown, Docker, Bash, SQL, LaTeX, Twig, …) get
completion and diagnostics through [language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md).

**Does Forge include language servers?**
No. They are separate programs you install, from the Language Servers settings page with one
click or with your package manager. Forge never bundles paid tools or keys.

**Do I need Node.js?**
Only for npm scripts and web project generators. npm-based language servers (Intelephense, TypeScript, Vue, …) do not need it: Forge
downloads an official Node.js build for them when none (18 or newer) is installed.

## AI

**Does Forge send my code anywhere?**
Only to the services you configure: the AI provider for commit messages (the diff of the files you
selected) and the agent CLI you chat with. See [AI: Privacy](docs/guide/user/ai.md#privacy).

**Can I use a local model?**
Yes: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server, for AI commit messages. The
AI Chat runs Claude Code or Gemini CLI.

**Do I need a Claude subscription for the AI Chat?**
You need a working `claude` (Claude Code) or `gemini` (Gemini CLI) installation with your own
login. Forge only runs the CLI.

## Projects

**Where are my settings stored?**
User settings in `<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`, project settings in `.forge/settings.toml`;
secrets in the OS keychain. See [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md).

**Should I commit `.forge/`?**
Commit `settings.toml`, `runConfigurations.toml`, `php-servers.json` and `dataSources.toml` if your
team should share them; ignore `runConfigurations.local.toml` and `cache/`.

**Can I open several projects at once?**
One project per window. Opening another project replaces the current one; multiple windows are not
available yet.

**Can I work on a server over SSH?**
Yes, see [Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md). Frameworks, language servers,
databases (through SSH tunnels), Xdebug and the AI agents work there; a few features are still local-only.

## Contributing

**How can I help?**
Read the [developer guide](docs/guide/developer/index.md), [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) and
[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Every user-visible change should update this guide.

**Can I write my own plugin?**
Plugins are built into Forge for now (there is no Marketplace or external plugin loading). Add one
to the repository: [Writing a plugin or pack](docs/guide/developer/plugins-and-packs.md).


---

Source: docs/guide/troubleshooting.md

---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Fixes for common problems - AppImage and FUSE, WebKitGTK, language servers not found, remote agent upload, the keychain on Linux, Wayland, Docker and Git.
order: 910
tags: [troubleshooting, appimage, fuse, webkit2gtk, wayland, keychain]
---

# Troubleshooting

## Starting Forge

### AppImage: `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`

The AppImage needs FUSE 2 to mount itself.

```sh
sudo pacman -S fuse2                 # Arch, EndeavourOS
sudo apt install libfuse2t64         # Ubuntu 24.04+
sudo apt install libfuse2            # Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12
```

Or run it without FUSE (slower start):

```sh
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
```

The same applies inside containers, where FUSE is usually unavailable.

### `error while loading shared libraries: libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0`

Forge uses the system's WebKitGTK 4.1 (also for the AppImage):

```sh
sudo pacman -S webkit2gtk-4.1                 # Arch
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0          # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1                # Fedora
```

Note the version: `webkit2gtk-4.0` / `libwebkit2gtk-4.0` is a different library.

### Blank or white window, or a crash right after start (Linux)

This is usually WebKitGTK's GPU path (often with NVIDIA drivers or under Wayland). Try, one at a
time:

```sh
WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 forge
WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 forge
```

These are WebKitGTK variables, not Forge settings; if one helps, put it in your desktop entry.

### Wayland

Forge runs as a native Wayland client through GTK. If something misbehaves (window placement of
dialog windows, title bar dragging, rendering), try the X11 backend:

```sh
GDK_BACKEND=x11 forge
```

Forge draws its own title bar; if window dragging or the buttons do not fit your compositor,
choose Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Window controls** → **Native title
bar**.

### macOS: "Forge is damaged" or "cannot be opened"

The app is not signed yet. Right-click → **Open**, or
`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Forge.app`.

### `forge` command not found

The deb/rpm packages install it. For the AppImage, link it into your `PATH`
(`ln -s …/Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/forge`).

## Language servers

### Language server not found

1. Check Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers: is the server **Installed**, and
   where was it found? Click **Detect Again** after installing.
2. Forge started from a desktop launcher may have a shorter `PATH` than your terminal (nvm,
   volta, fnm, `~/.local/bin` and Composer paths are often only set in shell profiles). Forge
   searches the usual places itself, but if it still fails, set the server's **Executable** to
   the full path, or start Forge from a terminal.
3. Servers you installed yourself and that run on Node need `node` on Forge's `PATH`; servers installed by Forge use its own Node.js.
4. Install with the **Install…** button: npm servers go to Forge's own folder
   (`~/.local/share/forge/langservers` on Linux) and are found there.
5. The server must be **Enabled**, its plugin active (e.g. `forge.vue` for Volar), and for
   ESLint, Tailwind and Angular the project must use them.

### Intelephense starts but premium features are missing

Enter your licence key (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers or PHP →
**Enter Licence Key…**). The status must read "Premium (key …1234)". If the keychain is not
available, the key cannot be stored (see below).

### No completion in PHP at all

Check Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | **Language server**: with "None (built-in index
only)" no server runs. With "Auto", install Intelephense (**Install Intelephense** on the PHP page) or
Phpactor.

## Keychain on Linux

API keys, tokens, passwords and licence keys are stored through the Secret Service API. You need
a running provider: GNOME Keyring (GNOME, most desktops) or KWallet with its Secret Service
integration (KDE Plasma 6 provides it; on older Plasma install `kwallet-pam`/configure KWallet,
or use GNOME Keyring). On minimal window managers start `gnome-keyring-daemon` in your session,
for example:

```sh
sudo pacman -S gnome-keyring libsecret
# then make sure the daemon runs in your session (PAM or your WM's autostart)
```

Symptoms of a missing keychain: saving an AI provider key, a code host token, an SSH password or
a database password fails with an error. Fallbacks exist for some secrets: the environment
variables `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`,
`GITLAB_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`/`GITEA_TOKEN`; for SSH use ssh-agent authentication.

## Remote development

### Remote agent upload

Forge uploads its agent to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` on the host. If connecting stops
at this step:

- **No agent for the host's architecture**: the build must bundle the agents (`pnpm release`)
  or you must provide them in `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR` or an `agents/` folder next to the `forge`
  binary (`forge-remote-agent-x86_64-linux.gz`, `forge-remote-agent-aarch64-linux.gz`). See
  [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#remote-agents).
- **The host is not Linux** (macOS, Windows, BSD): not supported.
- **`~/.cache` is not writable**, the disk is full, or the home directory is read-only: fix the
  permissions or free space.
- **The login shell prints text or asks questions**: output before `FORGE-AGENT-READY` is
  skipped, but interactive prompts in `.bashrc`/`.profile` block the start. Guard them with
  `[[ $- == *i* ]]`.
- **`noexec` home or cache**: the agent cannot run from `~/.cache`; ask your administrator.
- For details set `FORGE_AGENT_LOG=debug` on the host and run Forge with `RUST_LOG=debug`.

### Host key changed

Forge refuses to connect when the host key differs from `~/.ssh/known_hosts` and shows both
fingerprints. Confirm only if you know why it changed (reinstalled server).

### Feature says "not available in remote projects yet"

Expected for WebForge's npm tool window and component navigation, StyLua, code hosts, HTTP
request environments and project compose files in Services. See
[Remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md).

### Language server missing in a remote project

Catalog servers and Intelephense must be installed **on the host** (the settings page refuses to
install for remote projects). Install them there, e.g. `npm install -g intelephense`, then
reopen the project.

## Git

- **Push or fetch hangs or fails with an SSH remote**: Forge runs git with
  `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` and cannot answer passphrase prompts. Add your key to ssh-agent
  (`ssh-add`) or use a key without passphrase, or an HTTPS remote with a credential helper.
- **Wrong git binary**: set `FORGE_GIT=/path/to/git`.

## Services (Docker)

- **"Docker: not connected"**: check that the daemon runs and that your user may use the socket
  (`docker ps` in a terminal; on Linux add yourself to the `docker` group). For Docker Desktop
  or rootless Docker, Forge looks at `~/.docker/run/docker.sock` and
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock`; otherwise set the socket path in Settings | Build, Execution,
  Deployment | Docker and use **Test Connection**.
- **Docker over SSH fails**: the host key must be in `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (connect once with `ssh` to accept it) and your key must be in ssh-agent or `~/.ssh`; the Docker socket on the host must be readable by that user.

## Xdebug

- No connection: check `xdebug.mode=debug`, `xdebug.client_port` (9003, same as
  `php.debug.port`), `xdebug.client_host` (for Docker: `host.docker.internal`) and that Forge is
  listening (toolbar icon). A firewall may block port 9003.
- Breakpoints not hit in Docker: add a server with path mappings (Settings | Languages &
  Frameworks | PHP | Servers) and set `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<name>`.

## Browser Companion

- The extension cannot find Forge: **Accept open requests from paired browsers** must be on;
  the port (63342 or the next nine) must be free; Firefox needs the extra permission for
  `127.0.0.1`.
- Pairing code rejected: codes expire after five minutes and work once; start pairing again.

## Resetting Forge

Quit Forge and delete its folders (see [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md#clean-slate)).
Project files in `.forge/` are not touched by this.


---

Source: docs/guide/README.md

---
title: About this guide
description: How the Forge guide is organized and the content contract a documentation site generator can rely on.
order: 999
tags: [meta, contributing]
---

# About this guide

> **For agents and LLM tools:** the guide is also published in the
> [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) format. [`docs/llms.txt`](docs/llms.txt) is a hand-curated
> index of the most important pages with one-line descriptions; edit it when you add or rename
> an important page. [`docs/llms-full.txt`](docs/llms-full.txt) is every guide page as plain
> Markdown in reading order, without frontmatter. It is generated: never edit it, run
> `pnpm docs:llms` in `app/ui` (or `node docs/scripts/build-llms.mjs`) after changing any page.
> The script also checks the links in `llms.txt`; `--check` only verifies that both files are
> up to date.

`docs/guide/` is the complete user and developer documentation of Forge, written as plain
Markdown so any static site generator (or GitHub's own Markdown view) can render it. This file
describes the structure and the rules every page follows. It is meant for the people and tools
that build the documentation site, and for contributors who add or change pages.

## Folder structure

```
docs/guide/
  index.md                 start page of the guide
  README.md                this file (structure and content contract)
  faq.md                   frequently asked questions
  troubleshooting.md       known problems and their fixes
  getting-started/         install, first start, projects, switching from PHPStorm
  user/                    one page per feature, written for IDE users
  reference/               generated-style tables: keymap, settings, file types, servers, …
  developer/               contributor documentation
    crates/                one page per Rust crate in crates/ and packs/
  user/shortcuts/          shortcuts by topic and the keymap reference card
  reference/main-menu/     one page per top-level main menu

docs/llms.txt              curated index for LLM tools (hand-written)
docs/llms-full.txt         all guide pages in one file (generated)
docs/scripts/build-llms.mjs  regenerates llms-full.txt and checks llms.txt
```

Every folder has an `index.md` that introduces the section and links to its pages. Pages
inside a folder are sorted by their `order` value (see below), not by file name.

## Page format

- **CommonMark** plus **GitHub Flavored Markdown tables**. Nothing else is required to render
  a page correctly.
- **One page per file.** File names are lowercase, words separated by `-`, extension `.md`.
- **Fenced code blocks always name their language** (`sh`, `toml`, `json`, `php`, `ts`,
  `rust`, `http`, `text`, …).
- **Headings:** every page starts with exactly one `#` heading that repeats the `title`.
  Sections use `##` and `###`.
- **Links between pages are relative** and point at the `.md` file, for example
  `[Editor](docs/user/editor.md)` or `[keymap](docs/guide/keymap.md#navigate)`. Anchors are GitHub-style
  heading slugs.
- **Images** are the existing screenshots in `docs/screenshots/`, linked relatively, e.g.
  `![Commit tool window](screenshots/vcs-commit.png)`. They are 1440×900 PNGs captured
  from browser mode. Do not hot-link external images.
- **Notes and warnings** are ordinary blockquotes that start with a bold label, so they work
  without any admonition plugin:

  ```markdown
  > **Note:** not available in remote projects yet.

  > **Warning:** this deletes the folder and everything in it.
  ```

  Generators may turn `> **Note:**`, `> **Tip:**` and `> **Warning:**` into styled callouts.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** are written in code spans with PHPStorm's notation:
  `Ctrl+Shift+A`, `Alt+Insert`, `Double Shift`, chords as `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`. When Windows/Linux
  and macOS differ, both are given: `Ctrl+B` (macOS `Cmd+B`).
- **Settings paths** use PHPStorm's notation with `|`: Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP.
  Setting keys are written in code spans: `php.interpreter`.
- **No generator-specific syntax:** no MDX/JSX, no shortcodes, no `{% %}` or `{{ }}` template
  tags in prose, no custom container syntax (`:::`), no HTML except `<br>` inside table cells.

## Frontmatter contract

Every `.md` file starts with a YAML frontmatter block:

```yaml
---
title: Git
description: Commit, diff, blame, branches and AI commit messages.
order: 70
tags: [vcs, git]
---
```

| Field | Required | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | yes | string | Page title for navigation, the browser tab and search results. Matches the page's `#` heading. |
| `description` | yes | string | One sentence. Use it for meta descriptions, link previews and section listings. |
| `order` | yes | integer | Sort key within the page's folder (ascending). `index.md` uses `0`. Gaps are intentional so pages can be inserted. |
| `tags` | no | list of strings | Lowercase keywords for search and tag pages. |

No other fields are used. Generators should ignore unknown fields rather than fail.

## Sections and audiences

| Folder | Audience | Voice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getting-started/` | new users | step by step |
| `user/` | people using Forge as their IDE | PHPStorm wording: tool windows, actions, Settings paths |
| `reference/` | everybody | complete tables, little prose |
| `developer/` | contributors | how the code is organized and how to extend it |

## Keeping the guide accurate

The guide describes what is on the branch it lives on. When a feature is not finished, the
page says so with a `> **Note:**` instead of describing planned behaviour. Features that are
being built on other branches can be listed under "Coming soon" on the [start page](docs/guide/index.md); new
features are announced there under "Recently added".

Every user-visible change updates the matching page in `docs/guide/` (this rule is also in
`AGENTS.md`). The reference tables are derived from the sources below; when you change a
source, update the table:

| Page | Source of truth |
| --- | --- |
| [reference/keymap.md](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md) | `crates/forge-keymap/data/phpstorm.json`, `ACTION_ALIASES` in `crates/forge-keymap/src/catalog.rs`, `registerKeymapActions` calls in `app/ui/src/features/` |
| [reference/settings.md](docs/guide/reference/settings.md) | `[[contributions.settings]]` in `app/src-tauri/plugins/*.toml`, page ids from `registerSettingsPage` |
| [reference/file-types.md](docs/guide/reference/file-types.md) | `crates/forge-filetypes/src/builtin.rs`, `crates/forge-filetypes/src/data.rs`, `fileTypes` in the manifests |
| [reference/language-servers.md](docs/guide/reference/language-servers.md) | `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml`, `crates/forge-langservers/pack_servers.toml` |
| [reference/cli-and-links.md](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md) | `crates/forge-open/src/cli.rs`, `crates/forge-open/src/request.rs` |
| [reference/file-locations.md](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md) | `dirs::config_dir()` / `cache_dir()` / `data_dir()` call sites in `crates/`, `packs/` and `app/src-tauri/` |
| [reference/environment-variables.md](docs/guide/reference/environment-variables.md) | `std::env::var` call sites |
| [reference/main-menu/](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md) | `crates/forge-keymap/src/menu.rs` (structure, labels) and the commands the UI registers (enabled state) |
| [user/shortcuts/](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md) | `crates/forge-keymap/data/phpstorm.json`, the registered commands and the menu paths from `menu.rs`; screenshots from `app/ui/scripts/scenarios/docs.mjs` |
| [developer/crates/](docs/guide/developer/crates/index.md) | each crate's `lib.rs` documentation and `Cargo.toml` |

The developer pages summarize [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), which remains the
detailed contract for IPC commands and contribution points.
